notes: Post-hoc AUC vs ANC nadir/AUEC/severe neutropenia/ORR/PFS/OS showed no clinically meaningful efficacy relationship at 240 mg/m2 (exposure plateau); logistic regression showed AUC-dependent increases in headache and phlebitis/injection-site-reaction risk, not judged to warrant dose change.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: NCA (Study 03, n=24-29) and popPK confirmed trilaciclib (an OCT/MATE transporter inhibitor) had no effect on topotecan (MATE1/MATE2-K substrate) Cmax/AUC, supporting proposed sequential dosing instructions; similar confirmation for etoposide/carboplatin.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Active-metabolite melphalan Cmax/AUCinf/t1/2 derived via NCA (sparse sampling) pooled across OP-103/OP-104/OP-107 (n=96/11/7); linear regression identified BSA (primary) and eGFR as PK covariates; reviewer flagged bias risk from short t1/2 (~1h); no population PK analysis was performed by applicant.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Descriptive analysis by melphalan AUCinf tertiles (n=116) showed positive trend of grade 3/4 neutropenia (19%->61%) and thrombocytopenia (28%->39%) with increasing AUCinf; no exposure-efficacy analysis was possible (no PK data from pivotal trial OP-106); FDA issued a PMR for further population PK/E-R analyses.

structural_features: Transit compartment absorption model (TCAM); linear elimination
notes: 4351 samples/666 patients across 7 studies; moderate hepatic impairment reduced CL/F by 38.9% (supports dose reduction to 0.89 mg in moderate HI); sex (25.2% lower CL/F in females) and body weight (V/F) also significant; renal impairment had no significant effect.

structural_features: Tumor growth inhibition model with tumor-shrinkage rate (KD) and growth rate (KL) as functions of exposure and covariates (stepwise covariate modeling: study population, ECOG)
notes: Longitudinal tumor-size model using 4-week Cavg as exposure driver, identified as best predictor of tumor shrinkage rate.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Highest Cavg quartile vs lowest associated with ~33% PFS risk reduction; based on data from a single dose level, interpreted with caution.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Cavg was the sole significant predictor of hand-foot-syndrome (HFS/PPE) odds, exposure-dependent; no E-R relationship found for blood pressure.

structural_features: Non-linear, time-dependent elimination (TMDD-like declining clearance); allometric weight effect on CL and V1
notes: PopPK-based simulation supported the switch from 500 mg Q3W to 1000 mg Q6W (comparable predicted Cmin/Cavg); covariates albumin, ALP, ADA, age (CL) and ALP/sex (V1) significant but none warranted dose adjustment; no significant effect of renal/hepatic impairment; ADA effect on PK inconclusive.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Exploratory linear E-R analysis (Cycle 5 exposures vs ORR/AEs, single dose level only); no significant Cavg-ORR relationship, but Cmin associated with 2.4-2.6-fold higher OR odds in some populations; FDA deemed analysis exploratory/not fully characterized.

structural_features: Parallel linear and time-dependent (exponentially declining, Kdes) clearance components; shared structural model for ADC and total antibody
estimation_technique: Simulation; Stepwise covariate modeling; Bootstrap validation
notes: Model validated via VPC/bootstrap (104 runs); body weight, ECOG, albumin, sex, disease status were significant covariates on CL/DELT/V1, supporting BW-based dosing; simulation showed low-albumin patients had 52% lower Cycle-1 Cavg; time-dependent CL approached steady state by ~10 weeks supporting no further dose reduction after Cycle 3.

structural_features: Linked one-compartment model for free payload SG3199 driven by first-order ADC degradation (parent-conjugate/payload model)
notes: FDA deemed the SG3199 popPK model unacceptable: estimated volume of distribution (0.049 L) was implausibly below extracellular fluid volume, driven by ~96% of samples below LLOQ; reviewer recommended using observed SG3199 concentrations rather than model-derived metrics for E-R analyses.

structural_features: Not applicable
estimation_technique: Logistic regression; Cox proportional hazards regression
notes: n=282 DLBCL patients: multivariate logistic regression found Cycle-1 Cavg (OR 6.09 per 1 ug/mL), tumor burden, and disease phenotype predicted ORR; Cox PH found higher Cavg associated with 39% lower risk of death (OS); no exposure-DOR relationship (univariate Cox).

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: n=328: multivariate logistic regression found Cycle-1 Cavg associated with 3.73-fold higher odds of Grade>=2 GGT elevation (also predicted by race, baseline ALT, bulky disease, prior chemo); similar exposure-dependent signals for skin/nail and LFT AEs across cycles 1-3.

structural_features: Linear clearance; no notable additional structural features
fitting_method_software: NONMEM v7.3; R v3.4.1 or later
notes: Model in NSCLC/solid tumor patients supported weight-based dosing (RP2D); sex was significant covariate on CL (~24% higher clearance in men vs women); simulations confirmed similar exposure for <80 kg vs >=80 kg patients.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Logistic regression of ORR vs Ctrough.max in EGFR Exon20ins NSCLC patients; ECOG was a significant covariate; partially explained higher ORR at 1400 mg RP2D (45.5%) vs 1050 mg (34.1%) despite similar exposure.

structural_features: 3 transit absorption compartments; dose-dependent relative bioavailability (F1); time-dependent auto-induction of clearance/bioavailability via first-order rate coefficient (KIND_F) explaining nonlinear dose-exposure relationship
notes: 500 healthy subjects/patients across 6 trials, doses 120-960 mg; enzyme auto-induction reached steady state in 2-3 weeks (+91% clearance, -35% relative bioavailability); no clinically meaningful effect of mild hepatic or mild/moderate renal impairment on exposure, supporting no dose adjustment.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: 248 NSCLC patients (KRAS G12C); inverse exposure-efficacy trend (ORR/OS/PFS) confounded by baseline disease burden, deemed inconclusive; no significant exposure-safety relationship for Gr3+ AEs/LFT abnormalities in 421 patients.

structural_features: Minimal PBPK model with single adjusting peripheral compartment; first-order oral absorption
notes: Sotorasib evaluated as CYP2D6 inhibitor and CYP2C8/2C9/2B6 inducer perpetrator; model adequate to predict clinically relevant (>2-fold) CYP2D6 inhibition DDI, but deemed inadequate for CYP2C8/2C9/2B6 induction predictions (non-mechanistic clearance model underpredicted steady-state patient exposure, PE -65% to +10%).

structural_features: Parent (infigratinib) and two active metabolites (BHS697, CQM157) modeled independently due to rapid first-pass metabolism; first-order absorption; time-dependent decrease in elimination (dose-count effect) for parent and BHS697
notes: 572 subjects pooled from 11 Phase 1 + 2 Phase 2 studies; used to support PK-matching-based dose reduction (75 mg QD, 3-weeks-on/1-week-off) for moderate hepatic impairment; labeling PK parameters ultimately based on NCA of model-simulated data rather than direct popPK estimates due to V2 shrinkage concerns.

structural_features: First-order absorption/elimination; body weight and food effect on KA as structural covariates; CYP2C19 and UGT2B17 polymorphism covariates on CL/F and F
notes: 239 subjects, 5291 PK observations; CYP2C19 and UGT2B17 poor-metabolizer status each associated with ~46-56% higher exposure; missed/delayed-dose simulations showed a single missed dose reduces 3-day average AUC by ~30%, informing missed-dose dosing guidance.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Pooled 133 (efficacy)/155 (safety) VHL-RCC/RCC patients using post-hoc AUCss from popPK model; univariate logistic regression for binary endpoints (ORR/DCR/BOR), KM for time-to-event; E-R relationships generally flat within observed exposure range; EPO/Hgb biomarker E-R also examined.

structural_features: Minimal PBPK model with first-order oral absorption; in vitro-to-in vivo extrapolation of CYP3A induction via Emax model; virtual populations stratified by CYP2C19/UGT2B17 phenotype and ethnicity (Caucasian vs Japanese)
notes: Belzutifan (moderate CYP3A4 inducer) PBPK model used to predict DDI with midazolam; adequate to predict belzutifan PK across CYP2C19/UGT2B17 phenotypes and effect on a sensitive CYP3A substrate; CYP3A5 induction not studied in vitro, added as sensitivity scenario for Japanese PM/PM population (higher CYP3A5 contribution to midazolam clearance).

structural_features: Parent (mobocertinib) + 2 active metabolites (AP32960, AP32914) modeled simultaneously; 3 transit absorption compartments; enzyme compartment with Emax-based autoinduction of CYP3A driven by molar sum of all 3 moieties (time-dependent clearance)
notes: 427 patients (110 healthy, 317 NSCLC), 16673 PK samples; only covariate retained was healthy-vs-cancer-patient status on CL/V; no clinically meaningful covariate effects, supporting no age/renal/hepatic dose adjustment.

structural_features: Not applicable
estimation_technique: Logistic regression; Dose-subgroup analysis (graphical quartile analysis)
notes: Efficacy analysis in 114 NSCLC EGFR exon20ins patients (single dose level, 160 mg QD) showed a positive but inconclusive trend; safety analysis in 295 patients (5-180 mg QD) showed positive trend of Grade3+ AEs/diarrhea with exposure, supporting the dose-reduction strategy.

structural_features: Full PBPK model for mobocertinib + 2 active metabolites (AP32960, AP32914) as CYP3A4 substrates and mechanism-based inhibitors/inducers; separate GastroPlus absorption-PBPK model for formulation bioequivalence bridging
notes: Predicted DDI with strong/moderate/weak CYP3A inhibitors (itraconazole) and inducers (rifampin), plus effect on CYP3A probes (alprazolam, midazolam); no clinically meaningful P-gp/BCRP-mediated DDI predicted; model also predicted net weak autoinduction of mobocertinib's own CYP3A metabolism.

structural_features: Combined ADC-MMAE (antibody-drug conjugate + released payload) model; 100% linear ADC clearance directed into a delay compartment feeding the MMAE sub-model; ADC distribution limited to central vascular compartment
notes: 399 patients (4 studies, 4847 ADC + 5145 MMAE concentrations); body weight, baseline albumin, and sex retained as ADC covariates; no dose adjustment recommended for hepatic/renal impairment or ADA status.

structural_features: Not applicable
estimation_technique: Logistic regression (full covariate model); Cox proportional hazards regression
notes: ORR modeled via logistic regression on Cycle-1 AUC/Cmax with covariates (age, weight, tumor burden, albumin, LDH, renal/ECOG/histology/prior therapy); Cycle-1 ADC Cmax remained significant after covariate adjustment; analysis limited by single dose level studied.

structural_features: Delayed first-order oral absorption (lag time); allometric scaling of CL and Vc; correlations among CL/Vc/Vp and between Tlag/Ka
notes: 353 CML-CP/AP patients pooled from 2 studies; FDA rejected the Applicant's renal-function (aGFR) covariate as confounded with body weight and built an independent model (OFV 94753.99 vs. Applicant's 96288.32) retaining dose/weight/sex/age on CL and weight/sex/formulation on Vc; supported 80 mg QD as alternative to 40 mg BID.

structural_features: Not applicable
estimation_technique: Logistic regression (univariate and multivariate); Linear mixed-effects model
notes: MMR at Week 24 (236 non-T315I + 67 T315I patients) most associated with average daily AUC; identified 200 mg BID for T315I-mutant patients; separate concentration-QTc analysis (239 patients, no clinically relevant prolongation).

structural_features: ADAM (advanced dissolution, absorption, metabolism) PBPK model with first-order absorption; permeability from MDCK-KO cells; Qgut/fugut parameters optimized against midazolam DDI data
fitting_method_software: Simcyp V19r1 (enzyme/transporter-mediated DDI); Simcyp V20r1 (gastric pH-mediated DDI)
notes: Model adequate for asciminib as a CYP3A4 perpetrator, but FDA found it inadequate to assess asciminib as a victim of BCRP- and P-gp-inhibitor-mediated DDI (PMRs required); gastric-pH DDI (rabeprazole) predicted no clinically meaningful effect.

structural_features: First-order elimination from central compartment; base structure selected after comparing 1-, 2-, and 3-compartment candidates
notes: 179 subjects (23 healthy + 156 ovarian cancer patients), 784 PK observations pooled across 3 studies, doses 0.0125-0.2 mg/kg; no covariate (age, weight, renal/hepatic impairment, race, sex) had a clinically meaningful effect on PK; no dose adjustment recommended.

structural_features: First-order elimination from central compartment; renal function and high ADA titer (>=8192) included as covariates on CL
fitting_method_software: NONMEM v7.3 (ICON); R v3.5.1; Xpose 4.4.0; PsN v3.4.2
notes: Pooled 587 patients across 3 studies (IMC-gp100-01, -102, -202); CL slightly decreased with worsening renal function and with high ADA titer but remained within the normal-function range, supporting no dose adjustment; FDA required ADA status be treated as a time-varying rather than static covariate.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: No clinically significant E-R trends identified for safety or efficacy across the dose range studied (5 ng/kg-68 mcg); OS examined by Cavg quartile via Kaplan-Meier; apparent lower OS in lowest-Cavg quartile attributed to confounding rather than a true exposure effect.

structural_features: First-order absorption from gut; dose-dependent bioavailability (F1) and absorption rate (Ka); time-dependent decline in clearance over treatment course; Data-Transform-Both-Sides (log-scale) estimation approach
notes: 630 subjects (11 Phase 1 + 5 Phase 2/3 studies), 8674 PK observations; nonlinear dose-AUC relationship from NCA prompted dose-effects on Ka/F1; explained 33%/25% higher Cmax/AUC for 400 mg QD vs. equal-total-daily-dose 200 mg BID, informing dosing-regimen choice.

structural_features: Indirect-response/turnover model of spleen volume (Kin/Kout) with linear pacritinib-concentration effect on Kin (selected over Emax/sigmoid-Emax); sequential PK-then-PD approach using empirical Bayes PK estimates; joint Weibull-hazard dropout model
notes: 283 myelofibrosis patients pooled from PAC203/PERSIST-1/PERSIST-3; used together with Monte Carlo simulation to evaluate whether AE-driven dose-reduction strategies would preserve spleen-volume response.

structural_features: First-order oral absorption PBPK model incorporating in vitro CYP3A time-dependent inhibition (TDI) parameters; assumed complete CYP3A-mediated metabolism
notes: Used to extrapolate clarithromycin (strong CYP3A inhibitor) DDI to more conservative dosing scenarios and to predict efavirenz (moderate inducer) DDI; FDA judged the model inadequate (BCS class II dose-dependent solubility/absorption not captured; failed to reproduce observed multi-dose PK), recommending avoidance of CYP3A perpetrators pending revised model or added clinical data.

structural_features: Not applicable
estimation_technique: Logistic regression (univariate); Dose-subgroup analysis (AUC decile); Simulation (Monte Carlo)
notes: FDA's independent logistic-regression reanalysis (using reviewer-derived PopPK exposures) found pacritinib AUC significantly associated with thrombocytopenia, bleeding, and hemorrhage (not diarrhea/CV events); Monte Carlo simulations estimated only 38% (100 mg BID) or 15% (100 mg QD) of 200 mg BID responders with toxicity would remain responders after dose reduction, supporting the proposed dose-reduction strategy.

structural_features: Linear clearance; time-varying (declining) clearance over time (max ~21% reduction in 1L melanoma); no PK interaction with relatlimab detected
notes: Nivolumab combination with relatlimab produced <=5% difference in baseline CL and similar time-varying CL decline (max 21.1%) vs monotherapy, confirming no PK-based interaction between the two mAbs.

structural_features: Parallel linear and nonlinear (Michaelis-Menten, Vmax/Km) clearance (~31% of total CL nonlinear at recommended dose); time-varying (Emax function of time) decline in nonlinear CL component; body weight covariate on CL (>20% effect)
notes: Relatlimab exhibits nonlinear, time-varying PK; steady state reached ~16 weeks with ~2-fold accumulation at 160 mg Q4W; simulations supported both FDC (480/160 mg Q4W) and separate-vial (240/80 mg Q2W) regimens as producing similar exposures.

structural_features: Sigmoid Emax model linking relatlimab plasma concentration to peripheral LAG-3 receptor occupancy (RO); built on relatlimab population PK model
notes: Predicted peripheral RO at proposed dose (first dose and steady-state) was similar across FDC, SAV coadministration, and SAV sequential drug products, supporting interchangeability of dosing formats.

structural_features: Not applicable
estimation_technique: Dose-subgroup analysis; Cox proportional hazards regression
notes: Flat PFS relationship and no clear ORR difference were observed across the exposure range spanning 240/80 mg Q2W, 480/160 mg Q4W, and 480/480 mg Q4W regimens in 1L and prior-IO melanoma (n=1529); relatlimab exposure positively associated with Gr2+ immune AEs and Gr3+ drug-related AEs.

structural_features: Model integrates dosimetry with PK; CrCl covariate on clearance
notes: Population PK/dosimetry analysis (~30-patient substudy) found exposure/biodistribution unaffected by body weight or BMI; simulations of mild/moderate renal impairment showed a trend toward higher kidney dosimetry, but no dose adjustment was recommended given no clear dosimetry-toxicity relationship.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Radioactivity-blood AUCinf was a statistically significant predictor of kidney dosimetry (p=0.005), but this may be confounded by CrCl as a covariate on clearance; overall E-R/toxicity analyses were deemed inconclusive due to limited data (n=30 substudy).

structural_features: Sequential zero-order then first-order absorption; ANC (absolute neutrophil count) as time-varying covariate on CL/F reflecting target-mediated elimination; body weight covariate on CL/F and Vz/F (power models)
notes: 329 subjects/2147 PK observations; confirmed no dose adjustment needed for age, sex, race, weight, BMI, or renal/hepatic impairment; target-mediated (ANC-driven) clearance was the dominant covariate.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Using post-hoc PK parameters, applicant's E-R modeling for efficacy produced implausible parameter estimates (e.g., negative EC50) because eflapegrastim clearance is itself driven by neutrophil count, confounding and invalidating the E-R relationship.

structural_features: Sequential zero- and first-order absorption; first-order elimination; IIV on CL/F, Vc/F, and duration of zero-order input (D1) on F
fitting_method_software: NONMEM v7.4.3; PsN v4.8.1; R v4.0.0+
notes: Model built from 8 studies/496 subjects/7690 PK samples; hepatic/renal impairment (mild-moderate) not clinically significant; informed a postmarketing requirement to compare 16 mg vs 20 mg QD dosing.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: ORR and safety were compared between 16 mg and 20 mg QD cohorts using model-predicted exposure metrics; approved 20 mg QD dose may not be optimal, and FDA required a postmarketing trial comparing 16 mg vs 20 mg QD.

structural_features: Full PBPK model incorporating distribution phase; futibatinib modeled as CYP3A time-dependent inhibitor and as substrate/perpetrator via P-gp and BCRP transporters
notes: Model adequately captured observed PK and predicted validated DDI with itraconazole/rifampin, but was judged inadequate to predict effects of clarithromycin, fluconazole, fluvoxamine, carbamazepine, and efavirenz due to lack of clinical DDI data for verification; supported avoiding moderate-to-strong CYP3A modulators.

structural_features: Linear clearance only (monotherapy); parallel linear and time-dependent (declining, Emax-type with Tmax/TC50 parameters) clearance when combined with durvalumab; body weight and albumin covariates on CL, body weight and sex covariates on V1
notes: Pooled population PK analysis (n=4050 across HIMALAYA and supportive studies) jointly modeled durvalumab and tremelimumab; no clinically significant PK differences by weight, age, sex, race, or mild-moderate renal/hepatic impairment were found for either drug.

structural_features: First-order (SC) absorption; parallel time-independent and time-dependent (declining, first-order rate KDES) elimination pathways, consistent with target-mediated drug disposition; body weight covariate on CL1/V1/V2; ISS stage and myeloma type (IgG vs non-IgG) covariates on CL1/CL2
notes: Time-dependent clearance component ~31% of total CL at treatment start, declining to <5% by week 8; confirmed no clinically meaningful exposure differences by body weight and that mild/moderate renal or mild hepatic impairment did not affect PK, supporting the 1.5 mg/kg SC weekly RP2D with no dose adjustments.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: ORR increased with exposure across SC doses of 0.08-3 mg/kg weekly, plateauing near the RP2D of 1.5 mg/kg; near-flat E-R trend at RP2D itself and no clear E-R relationship for Grade>=3 cytopenias, supporting the selected dose.

structural_features: Mechanistic PBPK model of IL-6-mediated suppression of CYP enzyme expression/activity following cytokine release
notes: Predicted CYP activity suppression from teclistamab-induced cytokine release (IL-6) returns to >=80% of baseline within 7-8 days after the first treatment dose; model used only IL-6 effects and lacked clinical DDI data for verification, so labeling recommends monitoring concomitant sensitive CYP substrates during step-up dosing and CRS.

structural_features: Parent ADC (mirvetuximab soravtansine) with two circulating metabolites (unconjugated DM4, S-methyl-DM4) modeled; clearance decreased with increasing dose over 0.15-2 mg/kg range, suggesting a saturable elimination mechanism consistent with target-mediated drug disposition (TMDD)
notes: Applicant's PopPK model pooled across 3 studies; age and adjusted ideal body weight (AIBW) were significant covariates but each with <20% impact on exposure, so dosing is based on AIBW; data were sparse for severe impairment (only 1 moderate-HI patient, none severe), prompting a hepatic-impairment PMR.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: E-R analysis pooled pivotal (n=97-106) and supportive studies (safety pool n=542); lower AUC correlated with lower ORR at the 6 mg/kg AIBW Q3W dose (mostly from one dose level, low confidence), while Cmax (not AUC) correlated with Grade>=2 ocular AEs and peripheral neuropathy - this Cmax/AUC dissociation motivated a post-marketing dose-optimization study (fractionated/weekly dosing to lower Cmax while preserving AUC).

structural_features: First-order absorption into central compartment with peripheral compartment (Vc, Vp, Q)
fitting_method_software: Monolix v2021R1; Simulx v2021R1; R v4.04
notes: PopPK model used to support labeling statements (no dose adjustment for renal/mod hepatic impairment) and to derive Cmin for E-R analyses; reviewer verified with no significant discordance.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Dedicated thorough-QT Phase 1 study (supratherapeutic 100 mg, ~3-fold clinical exposure); concentration-QTc analysis was primary analysis; no clinically significant QTc prolongation observed at 8x max dose.

structural_features: First-order absorption (SC) plus IV infusion rates; allometric power-function effects of body weight and baseline albumin on CL
notes: Integrated Phase 1/2/3 dataset, 350 subjects; underprediction bias at highest concentrations attenuated after IIV.

structural_features: Sequential "life-span" compartment model: RET and mature-RBC (mRBC) turnover compartments (3rd/4th compartments) predicting RBC counts; hemoglobin derived from RET/RBC + observed MCH
notes: Final integrated Phase 1/2/3 PK/PD model for hemoglobin; stochastic simulations (with IIV/parameter uncertainty) show modest (<2 g/dL) Hgb increase, informing safety monitoring for erythrocytosis risk.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Separate E-R models for 6MWD and PVR efficacy endpoints (449 patients, 2868 obs) using model-predicted Cavg; both show plateau near the 0.7 mg/kg dose, supporting dose selection.

structural_features: First-order absorption; race (Japanese vs non-Japanese), health status covariates
notes: Reviewer notes mild-moderate renal impairment causes no significant AUC change; severe renal impairment subject numbers too limited to assess.

structural_features: Not applicable
estimation_technique: Linear regression; Poisson regression; logistic regression; Cox proportional hazards regression
notes: 679 ATTR-CM subjects; separate final models for %CFB serum TTR, cardiovascular hospitalization (Poisson), %CFB NT-proBNP, all-cause mortality (logistic, using change in TTR as indirect predictor since direct exposure was not significant), and time-to-event survival (Cox PH, TTR-based).

structural_features: Minimal PBPK/full-body model; enzyme kinetics for UGT-mediated elimination
notes: Predicts ~2-fold increase in CYP2C8 substrate (repaglinide) exposure and >2-fold increase in CYP2C9 substrates (tolbutamide/warfarin) when acoramidis is perpetrator; predicts ~50% decrease in acoramidis exposure with UGT inducer (rifampin) as victim - qualitative due to UGT isoform uncertainty.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Series of Phase 1 bridging studies comparing landiolol vs. esmolol and landiolol concentrate vs. Japanese-approved Onoact formulation, plus bolus+maintenance vs. maintenance-only dosing schemes; all analyzed by NCA only (no compartmental model).

structural_features: First-order absorption; weight covariate on CL/F,Vc/F,Q/F,Vp/F,ka; Japanese ethnicity (29% higher Vc/F); ADA-titer effect on CL/F; between-occasion variability tied to ADA-positivity status
notes: High ADA titer (>=3200) associated with up to 400% increase in AUC,ss/Ctrough,ss; used to bridge Phase 3 vial-syringe vs. commercial autoinjector formulation.

structural_features: Two sequential indirect-response (turnover) models: exposure-ApoC-III (inhibitory Emax on Kin, IC50=0.44 ng/mL) and exposure-TG (stimulatory Emax on Kout)
notes: Used to simulate 50 mg/80 mg Q4W vs Q1M regimens; supports 80 mg Q4W or Q1M achieving ~72-74% ApoC-III and ~28-29% TG reduction from baseline.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Exploratory exposure-safety analyses of platelet count (vs cumulative AUC/Cmax) and hypersensitivity relationship; no substantial trend found.

structural_features: Dual parallel first-order absorption depot compartments (Ka1, Ka2) from two SC injection sites, lag time on 2nd absorption; body weight (major) and BMI covariates on CL/F, V/F
notes: Covariate analysis found no clinically significant effect of age/sex/race/mild-moderate renal or mild hepatic impairment; derived exposure metrics not further used in K-PD model due to temporal disconnect between plasma PK and prolonged PD effect.

structural_features: Population K-PD model with hypothetical unitless effect compartment (mono-exponential decay, rate Ke) coupled to serum APOC3 and TG turnover model, decoupled from measured plasma PK
notes: Supports plozasiran 25 mg SC Q3M dosing regimen for FCS/severe hypertriglyceridemia.

structural_features: Full-binding target-mediated drug disposition (TMDD) model: high-affinity LIB003:PCSK9 binding, PCSK9 turnover, first-order elimination of free LIB003, free PCSK9, and complex; linked to LDL-C indirect-response (elimination rate inhibited by free PCSK9)
notes: 3,547 PK observations/2,425 subjects across 6 trials; supports 300 mg Q4W SC dosing; no clinically significant differences by age/sex/race or mild/moderate hepatic impairment; severe hepatic impairment uncharacterized. TMDD clearance: free-LIB003 CL 0.36 L/day vs. PCSK9-bound complex elimination 0.47 L/day.

structural_features: Two first-order absorption rate constants (ka1, ka2) with lag time on ka1, linear elimination; height on Vc/F; inverse-power BMI effect on ka1; intranasal-volume-dependent relative bioavailability (FVOL) for doses >100 uL
notes: Built from single-dose Phase 1 data only; no exposure-response analysis conducted (PK not collected in Phase 2/3); noted limitation extrapolating to pediatric populations or repeat dosing (NODE-103 showed less-than-dose-proportional PK with repeat dosing, implying nonlinearity not captured).

structural_features: First-order absorption after lag time, linear elimination; body weight and sex covariates on volume
notes: 9,963 PK samples/447 subjects (264 healthy, 183 oHCM); confirmed dose proportionality to 20 mg QD; post-hoc PK estimates used for subsequent PK/PD and E-R analyses.

structural_features: Longitudinal exponential-decline models linking Cavg,24 to post-Valsalva LVOT-G and LVEF
notes: Used to evaluate less-frequent dose-titration schedules (Q2W/Q4W/Q6W/Q8W vs. weekly) over 3 years for proposed commercial titration regimen.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Exposure-efficacy (pVO2 CPET, KCCQ, NT-proBNP via linear regression) and exposure-safety (TEAE incidence via logistic regression) from SEQUOIA-HCM Phase 3 data.

structural_features: Minimal PBPK model (single adjusting distribution compartment), first-order absorption, enzyme-kinetics elimination
notes: Predicts strong/moderate CYP3A inhibitors (voriconazole, fluconazole, itraconazole, verapamil, fluvoxamine, sulfaphenazole) increase AUC up to ~3.5-fold, driving dose-reduction guidance; rifampin (strong CYP3A/CYP2C19/moderate CYP2C9 inducer) predicted to reduce AUC 79%, leading to contraindication.

structural_features: First-order absorption (ka fixed at 0.175/h from Phase 1 data); allometric-type power-function covariates: body weight and baseline albumin on CL/F,V/F; ADA-titer quartile and T1D-vs-T2D categorical covariates on CL/F
notes: Body weight most influential covariate (34% higher exposure at 56 kg vs 83 kg) but no dose adjustment recommended; high ADA titer (>5000) increases exposure substantially (transient peak weeks 10-20).

structural_features: Effect-compartment delay (rate constant P2) linking insulin icodec concentration to daily pre-breakfast SMPG (4 population-specific models: nonlinear Emax-type with intercept/slope/alpha); common indirect-response (turnover) model linking weekly-average SMPG to HbA1c (Kin/Kout)
notes: Mechanistic E-R modeling used to simulate missed-dose/altered dosing-day scenarios and alternative weekly dose-titration strategies; found titrating on alternative days reduces hypoglycemia risk but compromises glycemic control in T1D, while reducing bolus insulin dose 30% on days 2-4 preserves control while lowering hypoglycemia risk.

structural_features: First-order absorption/elimination with a transit compartment for absorption delay; nonlinear (power-model) dose-dependent bioavailability (F)
notes: 3,790 participants/18,716 concentrations; covariates (weight, age, sex, renal function, ethnicity, race, T2D status) found not clinically significant - no dose adjustment needed.

structural_features: Longitudinal indirect-response model for body weight (Emax, with placebo effect and disease-progression component) plus secondary FG-HbA1c indirect-response model linked via glucose dynamics
notes: Predicted -13.1%/-11.0% weight loss at 72 weeks (non-T2D/T2D) aligning with observed ATTAIN-1/2 results (-12.35%/-10.54%); high IIV noted on Kout (272% CV).

structural_features: ADAM (absorption/dissolution/metabolism) model with intestinal P-gp transport, full PBPK distribution, permeability-limited liver model, enzyme-kinetics elimination; combined PopPK-PBPK approach quantifying gastric-emptying-delay (GED)
fitting_method_software: Simcyp Simulator v23 (Certara), modified Healthy Volunteers_LSV population
notes: Predicts strong/moderate CYP3A inhibitors (itraconazole, verapamil) ~2-fold increase orforglipron exposure; predicts no clinically relevant GED-mediated DDI on victim drugs (lisinopril, metoprolol, digoxin, oral contraceptive, sitagliptin, metformin, S-warfarin) even at highest-GED starting dose; approach cross-verified against observed dulaglutide DDI data.

structural_features: Two-compartment disposition with transit absorption compartment and first-order elimination; power-model covariates for body weight and eGFR on CL/F; sex/race/hyperlipidemia/T2DM/ethnicity indicators on CL/F; sex/hyperlipidemia/weight on V2/F; food effect on Ka
notes: Population PK model found no clinically meaningful impact of age, sex, race, or body weight on bempedoic acid PK; also used to bridge exposure across three tablet formulations, supporting their similarity as supportive evidence.

structural_features: First-order absorption/elimination; exponential IIV on ka, CL/F, Vc/F; combined additive+proportional residual error; CL/F-Vc/F covariance; dose-dependent bioavailability (F1 100%/84%/73% at 2.5/5/10mg); body weight covariate on CL/F and Vc/F
estimation_technique: Empirical Bayes estimation; stepwise covariate modeling
notes: 1-compartment popPK model (8092 samples, 2321 subjects) found body weight was the dominant covariate (steady-state AUC0-24 27% higher in <60kg, 19.6% lower in >90kg vs. 60-90kg reference); age, sex, race, eGFR, bilirubin, albumin, NT-proBNP were not significant; individual Bayes exposures fed the E-R analysis.

structural_features: Not applicable
estimation_technique: Cox proportional hazards regression; simulation-based VPC
notes: Individual empirical Bayes exposure estimates were used as covariates in a Cox PH model for time to CV death/HF hospitalization (4,474 subjects) and a longitudinal SBP safety model; flexible titration dosing in VICTORIA confounded raw dose-exposure-event relationships, requiring careful choice of exposure metrics.

structural_features: Whole-body PBPK model (18 organs/tissues, standard PK-Sim 3-compartment per-organ sub-model); Weibull dissolution functions per tablet strength; Rodgers & Rowland partition coefficients; linear UGT1A1/UGT1A9-mediated glucuronidation, minor CYP1A1/CYP3A4 oxidative contribution
notes: PBPK model adequate to predict vericiguat PK and DDI with mefenamic acid (UGT1A9 inhibitor, predicted AUC ratio <1.35) and atazanavir (UGT1A1 inhibitor, predicted AUC ratio <1.27), but inadequate for the M-1 metabolite; FDA cautioned mefenamic acid is not a strong UGT1A9 inhibitor so results shouldn't extrapolate to other inhibitors.

structural_features: Parallel linear + saturable (Michaelis-Menten, ANGPTL3-driven) target-mediated clearance; allometric BW scaling (CL exponent fixed 0.75, Vc exponent estimated 0.875); Km 1.02 mg/L, Vmax 3.12 mg/day; disease status (HoFH 25% lower Vmax) and ANGPTL3 concentration as covariates on Vmax
estimation_technique: Allometric scaling; forward addition covariate selection
notes: 2-compartment TMDD popPK model (278 subjects) found linear pathway dominates clearance at clinical doses (~8.4 mg/day) while saturable pathway remains partially engaged; HoFH patients had 25% lower Vmax than healthy subjects; no dose adjustment recommended for age/gender/disease status.

structural_features: Indirect-response (turnover) model of LDL-C with zero-order production (Kin) inhibited by evinacumab (Imax, IC50=57.4 mg/L); covariates: body weight/race on Imax, baseline LDL-C on IC50; sequential two-step popPK-PD approach
estimation_technique: Sequential PK-PD modeling; bootstrap CIs; VPC
notes: Indirect-response PK/PD model found observed pre-dose concentrations (258 mg/L non-apheresis, 144 mg/L post-apheresis) were well above IC50, with no exposure-response trend at the proposed dosing regimen, supporting adequacy of fixed dosing without exposure-based titration.

structural_features: First-order delayed absorption (Tlag) with first-order linear elimination; covariates: eGFR on CL, age (piecewise linear) and injection site/batch on F, sex on Ka; allometric scaling applied in an intermediate model to support pediatric dosing
notes: 1-compartment popPK model (pooled across 7 trials) used allometric scaling in an earlier iteration to support the single pediatric dose of 0.6mg (ages >=6 years) matching adult exposure; eGFR was a significant covariate on clearance.

structural_features: Indirect-response (turnover) glucose model combining sigmoid Emax (Hill factor) with an added linear component (statistically significant improvement over Emax-only, p=0.0019/0.0018); individual Kout, Emax, plateau (PLAT) with correlated Emax-PLAT random effects; model starts from non-steady-state hypoglycemic baseline
estimation_technique: Bootstrap; combined sigmoid Emax + linear turnover modeling
notes: PK/PD turnover model linking model-predicted concentrations to glucose response supported adequacy of the single fixed 0.6mg rescue dose for severe hypoglycemia across T1DM patients including pediatric patients >=6 years.

structural_features: Vc/F and Vp/F not separately identifiable (kept equal); 3 transit absorption compartments with 0.215h lag; covariates: body weight/eGFR (allometric, CL exponent 0.35, Vc exponent 0.65) and strong CYP3A4 inhibitor use on CL/F; SGLT inhibitor use and smoking on F1
notes: 2-compartment popPK model (5458 observations, 2284 subjects, FIDELIO-DKD) built on an earlier Phase 2b base model; time-varying eGFR, body weight, and strong CYP3A4 inhibitor use were significant on CL/F; individual estimates fed the serum-potassium E-R model.

structural_features: Indirect-response (turnover) model of serum potassium: zero-order production (Kin), Kout=Kin/BSL, disease-progression slope (TSLOPE), drug effect DE=Emax*AUCs^gamma/(IC50^gamma+AUCs^gamma) reducing Kout; covariates: eGFR/Japanese ethnicity on baseline K+ (BSL); eGFR/sex/UACR on Emax; UACR/BSL/treatment arm on TSLOPE
analysis_timing: Prospective/pre-specified (re-developed after an earlier Phase 2 model failed external validation)
estimation_technique: Stepwise covariate modeling; VPC; sensitivity analysis with reviewer's own popPK-derived AUCss
notes: Turnover model showed finerenone raises serum K+ by inhibiting elimination, with max Emax-driven increase ~9.95% (~0.44 mmol/L at baseline 4.4 mmol/L); slower disease progression on finerenone (0.412%/yr) vs. placebo (0.161%/yr); an earlier ARTS-DN-based model failed to predict pivotal FIDELIO-DKD data, requiring re-estimation.

structural_features: Whole-body PBPK, standard PK-Sim 3-compartment per-organ model; Rodgers & Rowland partition coefficients; finerenone as CYP3A4 (fm 0.9)/CYP2C8 (fm 0.1) substrate and competitive+time-dependent CYP3A4 inhibitor (IC50=12uM, KI=10uM); perpetrator models for itraconazole, clarithromycin, fluvoxamine, efavirenz, rifampicin, erythromycin, verapamil
notes: PBPK predicted AUC ratios >5 (itraconazole), >3.5 (clarithromycin), ~1.55 (fluvoxamine), ~0.2 (efavirenz), ~0.07 (rifampicin), supporting contraindication with strong CYP3A4 modulators; FDA cautioned that extrapolating from moderate-inhibitor data to strong-modulator predictions introduces uncertainty.

structural_features: Kinetic-PD (k-PD) model with hypothetical liver effect compartment (input-driven; plasma concentrations undetectable beyond ~24-48h); chained turnover structure: liver compartment inhibits PCSK9 synthesis (Imax model) which inhibits LDL-C degradation (second Imax model); covariates on IC50/Imax parameters: age, sex, weight, disease population, baseline PCSK9/LDL-C, statin use, CLcr
pk_exposure_metric: Not applicable (kPD bypasses standard exposure metrics)
notes: Because inclisiran plasma concentrations were undetectable beyond ~24-48h while PCSK9/LDL-C suppression persisted for months, a k-PD model was developed (per FDA EOP2 agreement) instead of conventional exposure-response; simulations directly supported selecting the every-6-month maintenance dosing interval over 4-month alternatives.

structural_features: Rapid first-order absorption with short lag time, rapid distribution, long terminal elimination; allometric weight exponent fixed 0.75 on CL/Q; covariates: CYP2C19 phenotype (PM -72%, IM -33% CL/F), HS status, omeprazole/esomeprazole, sex on CL/F; solution formulation/fed status on KA/F; dose level on ALAG1/F
estimation_technique: Allometric scaling (fixed exponent); stepwise covariate modeling (SCM)
notes: CYP2C19 metabolizer phenotype was the dominant covariate on clearance, supporting genotype-guided dosing; no clinically meaningful effect of age, race, or mild-moderate renal impairment.

structural_features: Two direct-effect E-R models using Cavg168: (1) LVEF, E=E0x(1-exp(kk)xCavg168^qq), baseline LVEF/population/sex on E0; (2) VLVOT, E=exp(E0)xexp(-exp(kk)xCavg168), baseline VLVOT/NT-proBNP on E0, plus placebo-time effect
notes: Direct-effect E-R models linked concentration to LVEF and VLVOT; FDA flagged that PD-guided dose titration could bias E-R estimates and confirmed consistent results using pre-titration-only data; simulations of ECHO-guided titration (VLVOT<30mmHg threshold) supported the labeled monitoring/titration approach.

structural_features: Simcyp PBPK model evaluating mavacamten as CYP3A victim (in CYP2C19 poor metabolizers) and as CYP2B6/CYP3A4/CYP2C8/9/19 inducer
notes: Strong CYP3A inhibitors predicted to increase mavacamten AUC ~2-fold in PM; fluconazole predicted AUC increase >=3-fold in NM; rifampin predicted to reduce AUC 3-8-fold depending on CYP2C19 phenotype; CYP2B6 induction PBPK analysis judged inadequate due to uncertainty in bupropion's fraction metabolized.

structural_features: First-order SC absorption without lag; linear elimination; body weight (power, centered 70kg) on CL/Q; fat-free mass/fat mass (time-varying) on Vc/Vp; formulation on Ka; study effect on F1 (fixed 80% bioavailability from IV-bridging study)
notes: Body weight was the only clinically relevant PK covariate (Cmax/AUC ~23% higher in 70kg vs. 21% lower in 120kg relative to 90kg reference); ~30% difference not considered to warrant dose adjustment; no significant effect of age, sex, ethnicity, organ impairment, or ADA.

structural_features: Sequential PK-PD: disease-progression/offset-compartment model for fasting glucose (FG) with drug/placebo effects; indirect-response model links HbA1c to FG (Kin driven by FG^phi); Emax dependent on baseline HbA1c; EC50 (174 ng/mL) decreased with cumulative weight loss
notes: Emax on FG lowering estimated at 38% (baseline 9.24->5.73 mmol/L); steady-state concentrations at 5/10/15mg (491-1470 ng/mL) achieved 74-89% of maximal effect; weight loss itself increased drug potency (5% weight loss -> ~29% EC50 decrease).

structural_features: Indirect-response model for fat-free mass and fat mass separately; linear drug effect reducing zero-order formation rate (Kin); shared elimination rate (Kout=0.0797/wk, ~9-wk half-life, ~45wk to new steady state); tirzepatide reduced fat mass ~3.2x more than FFM
estimation_technique: Sequential PK-PD modeling; VPC (external validation set)
notes: Weight-loss turnover model found tirzepatide preferentially reduces fat mass over fat-free mass, with ~9-week half-life for the weight-loss effect and ~45 weeks to reach new body-weight steady state.

structural_features: Discrete-time 3-state Markov model (no AE/mild/moderate-severe) for nausea/vomiting (joint) and diarrhea (separate); drug effect via hypothetical first-order tolerance compartment (KTOL) combined with plasma concentration; "first-event" and "current nausea" logit covariates; separate linear effect on recovery transitions
estimation_technique: Discrete-time Markov chain modeling (adapted from dulaglutide precedent)
notes: Markov exposure-safety model captured GI tolerance development with sustained exposure and first-event/current-nausea risk escalation, supporting the gradual dose-titration regimen used to mitigate GI tolerability.

structural_features: Not applicable
estimation_technique: Linear regression (per-timepoint); mixed-effects modeling (FDA confirmatory, n=29026 observations, 5066 patients)
notes: Concentration-heart rate regressions found the largest HR increase during dose-escalation (Week 12, ~13bpm at predicted steady-state Cmax 1920 ng/mL) vs. smaller increases (7.0-9.2bpm) later; Japanese patients showed similar slope but higher intercept (~3-4bpm greater increase).

structural_features: Mechanistic gastric-emptying-delay DDI models for 8 victim drugs (acetaminophen, atorvastatin, digoxin, lisinopril, metformin, metoprolol, sitagliptin, S-warfarin); ADAM oral absorption model for several; verified against clinical acetaminophen data
notes: PBPK modeling of tirzepatide-mediated delayed gastric emptying was adequate to qualitatively conclude no clinically meaningful PK impact on 8 co-administered oral drugs; oral-contraceptive interactions were instead assessed via a dedicated clinical DDI study.

structural_features: First-order absorption with lag time (base model); transit-compartment absorption used for final covariate refinement; covariates: body weight, CrCL, Asian race, food
estimation_technique: Forward selection/backward elimination covariate modeling; VPC
notes: 2-compartment popPK model (pooled healthy/diabetic/hypertensive populations) found body weight, CrCL, Asian race, and food as significant covariates; FDA reproduced both models and found no clinically meaningful exposure differences by body-weight or renal-function strata at 20mg.

structural_features: Sigmoid absorption (zero-order input duration) with linear clearance; formulation effects on ka/Vc/F; food effects on D1/Vc/F/F1; covariates: body weight (power 0.815 CL/F, 1.25 Vc/F), eGFR (power 0.416 CL/F), age (power -0.6 CL/F, -1.31 Q/F), disease status (heart failure -51.8% CL/F; T2DM/HF -45%/-71.1% Vc/F vs. healthy)
estimation_technique: Power-model covariate scaling; forward/backward covariate selection
notes: 2-compartment popPK model (2258 subjects, 16186 concentrations) found body weight, eGFR, age, and disease status as significant covariates; because pivotal CV-outcome trials (SCORED, SOLOIST) terminated early with minimal PK data, model-simulated exposures were used for the downstream safety exposure-response model.

structural_features: Not applicable
estimation_technique: Linear regression (logistic-type on probability of diarrhea); Simulation (10,000 virtual patients)
notes: Linear E-R model related steady-state Cmax to probability of diarrhea (age the only significant covariate); simulation at the approved 200->400mg titration predicted 5-12% diarrhea incidence vs. ~5% placebo; PK exposure was not significantly associated with hypoglycemia or volume depletion; no efficacy E-R possible due to early trial termination.

structural_features: Two-compartment model, first-order oral and IM (long-acting) absorption, linear elimination; body weight as allometric covariate on CL/F, V2/F, Q/F, V3/F
notes: Cabotegravir popPK model; 1,650 subjects, 24,039 samples across oral+IM studies; body weight was significant covariate; model used to support dosing incl. missed-injection simulations.

structural_features: One-compartment disposition with two parallel first-order absorption pathways (fast + slow) after IM administration; covariates: study phase (2 vs 3) on absorption bioavailability, age on fast absorption pathway
notes: Rilpivirine popPK model; 986 subjects, 18,261 samples, 7 studies. Source document is internally inconsistent (structural description implies 1-compartment; reviewer narrative elsewhere calls it "two-compartment"). Reviewer disagreed with applicant's proposed RPV safety Cmax threshold, deriving 551 ng/mL instead.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Pooled Phase 3 (n=581) quartile analysis of CAB/RPV exposure vs virologic failure (9 failures, 1.5%) and vs 6 adverse events of interest; no clinically meaningful exposure-response relationship for efficacy or safety identified.

structural_features: Minimal PBPK model with single adjusting compartment for CAB oral absorption (ADAM model); used to predict CAB inhibition of renal OAT1/3 transporters and effect of UGT1A1/9 inhibitors on CAB exposure
notes: Conducted in lieu of clinical DDI studies; verified against 9 OAT1/3 substrates and 3 inhibitors with known clinical DDI data; predicted UGT1A1/9 inhibitors not expected to interact clinically with CAB.

structural_features: 2-compartment disposition plus one transit compartment with delayed first-order absorption and first-order elimination from central compartment
notes: Pooled Phase 1-3 data; VVC patients had 42% larger peripheral volume and 35% higher bioavailability than healthy subjects; food increased bioavailability/exposure ~44%; age effect on peripheral volume not clinically relevant. FDA required label to state exposure-response relationship is unknown (no formal ER analysis conducted).

structural_features: Parent fexinidazole plus two active metabolites (M1 sulfoxide, M2 sulfone), each one compartment in a composite 3-compartment structure; zero-order absorption (duration D1); weight-based allometric scaling (fixed exponent 0.75) on clearance
fitting_method_software: NONMEM v7.4 (R v3.6.1 for data processing)
notes: FDA pharmacometrics team revised applicant's model; based on sparse PK data (4-6 samples/patient) from two Phase 3 studies in adult and pediatric HAT patients; Phase 1 data excluded (disease may affect PK).

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Concentration-QTc analysis using pooled healthy-subject data used in place of a dedicated TQT study; QTc prolongation associated with M2 metabolite, not parent; predicted mean ddQTcF of 17.2 ms (90% CI upper 20.0) at max therapeutic exposure.

structural_features: Static mechanistic DDI risk model (not dynamic PBPK simulation); FDA-guidance-based equations for CYP2D6/CYP3A4 victim DDI risk
fitting_method_software: Drug-Drug Interaction Risk Calculator (Pharmapendium); FDA-internal Excel-based static mechanistic tool (cross-check)
notes: Predicted fexinidazole/M1 as CYP3A4 inhibitor increasing exposure of sensitive substrates (lovastatin ~8-fold, simvastatin ~4-fold, midazolam ~2 to 2.4-fold); supported label recommendation to avoid CYP3A4 substrates.

structural_features: Two-compartment disposition, first-order absorption with lag-time, first-order elimination; strong CYP3A inhibitor/inducer effect on CL/F, dose effect on Ka, transplant/CMV status effect on CL/F, fixed allometric weight scalars (0.75 clearances, 1 volumes)
notes: 667 subjects across 12 studies; strong CYP3A inhibitors/inducers significant covariates on CL/F; fed downstream exposure-response and adolescent-extrapolation analyses.

structural_features: Not applicable
estimation_technique: Logistic regression; Linear regression; Kaplan-Meier time-to-event analysis
notes: Phase 2/3 analyses; no significant exposure-response for viral load reduction or undetectable CMV DNA; supported 400 mg BID dose selection.

structural_features: Full PBPK model (ADAM absorption, Rodgers-Rowland Method 3 Vd, retrograde hepatic CL apportioned CYP3A4 35%/CYP1A2 4%/UGT 61%); separate BCRP transporter DDI expansion (rosuvastatin)
notes: Verified against ketoconazole/rifampin DDI data; predicted exposure changes with moderate/strong CYP3A inhibitors and inducers; BCRP DDI (rosuvastatin) could not be excluded.

structural_features: Same 2-compartment base model re-simulated with alternate allometric exponents (fixed 0.75/1 vs. estimated) to predict adolescent exposures
notes: No PK data in patients <18y at review; simulations extrapolated adult model (36-140 kg) down to ~29 kg to support dosing in adolescents >=12y and >=35 kg without a dedicated pediatric study.

structural_features: Two-compartment, first-order absorption with lag-time; weight allometric on CL/F, Q/F (fixed 0.75) and volumes (estimated 1.43); covariates: formulation, race (non-Caucasian 48% higher CL/F), total bilirubin
notes: 8,033 PK observations, 604 subjects, 8 studies; simulations predicted ~2-fold higher exposure in 29-<40 kg vs 60-70 kg patients; no dose adjustment given favorable safety profile and minimal low-weight enrollment.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Post-hoc analysis of Cmax/Cavg quartiles vs. Grade 3/4 CPK elevation; no consistent or statistically significant relationship found.

structural_features: Static mechanistic model (R1/R3 equations per 2020 FDA DDI guidance, then AUCR-based refined model) for CYP inhibition/induction risk
notes: Basic model flagged concern for nearly all CYP isoforms; refined model AUCR all within 0.8-1.25, leading to no recommendation for dedicated clinical DDI study.

structural_features: First-order absorption and elimination; CL/F and V/F scaled by body weight via allometry; covariates tested (age, weight, sex, valproate/clobazam co-medication) - only weight retained
notes: Population PK analysis of stiripentol in children with Dravet syndrome co-treated with valproate and clobazam; stepwise covariate model retained only body weight (via allometric scaling); supported steady-state PK characterization/dosing guidance in the pediatric Dravet population.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: FDA reviewer analyses (multivariate logistic regression, exposure-response, minimal-CLB-change subgroup analyses; N=33 stiripentol vs N=31 placebo from STICLO studies) attempted to partition stiripentol's efficacy from concurrent increases in clobazam/norclobazam exposure; results were inconclusive (small sample size, all STP subjects also received clobazam).

structural_features: Not applicable (secondary two-compartment model with zero-order/first-order absorption and lag time also fit to same data)
notes: Single/multiple-dose PK and bioavailability studies in healthy volunteers (500-2000 mg doses), analyzed by NCA with a secondary two-compartment compartmental fit; supported dose-proportionality and formulation bioequivalence assessment.

structural_features: First-order absorption (ka), apparent volume (Vc/F), linear apparent clearance (CL/F), log-error residual model; body weight retained (allometric) on CL/F and Vc/F; race, patient status, age, sex, albumin, CrCl, ADA status/titer, concomitant meds tested but not retained
estimation_technique: Allometric scaling; Empirical Bayes estimation; Simulation
notes: Model built from 8346 PK samples in 2287 subjects (healthy volunteers plus episodic/chronic migraine patients) across phase 1-3; estimated terminal half-life ~31 days; used to simulate steady-state exposures across 225/675/900 mg monthly/quarterly regimens; no clinically significant covariate effects (age, sex, race, renal/hepatic markers).

structural_features: Longitudinal indirect Emax exposure-response model with exponential placebo time-course and Emax drug-effect (EC50) on monthly migraine/headache days; exposure metric (Cav) derived from final PopPK model
notes: Separate E-R models for episodic migraine (4444 records, N=1142) and chronic migraine (5312 records, N=1361); Emax=0.252 (25.2% additional reduction vs placebo), EC50=3.60 ug/mL; baseline acute-medication use was a significant covariate on baseline migraine days; consistent with shallow dose-response across doses.

structural_features: First-order absorption (ka), apparent volume (V/F), apparent clearance (CL/F); body weight retained (allometric power model) on CL/F; age, dose, race, ethnicity, sex, ADA status/titer, renal function, bilirubin, injection site tested but not retained
estimation_technique: Allometric scaling; Empirical Bayes estimation; Simulation
notes: Model built from 15770 PK samples in 2412 subjects (healthy volunteers, episodic/chronic migraine patients); estimated terminal half-life ~27 days; simulations at 5th/95th percentile body weight showed overlapping exposure and predicted efficacy, supporting no weight-based dose adjustment, consistent with lack of 120 vs 240 mg dose-response.

structural_features: Indirect response (turnover) model: dM/dt = kin(1-P) - kout(1+Emax*C/(EC50+C))*M linking plasma concentration to monthly migraine headache days via kin/kout; no covariates retained after prespecified criteria
notes: Fit to 17483 migraine headache-day records from 2881 patients (pooled EM+CM phase 3 studies); a related target-engagement Emax model (galcanezumab-CGRP, EC50 ~20138 ng/mL) was also explored but reviewer flagged inadequate goodness-of-fit reporting for that sub-analysis.

structural_features: Not stated
notes: Review references (in one sentence, no methodological detail) a population PK analysis of pooled healthy-subject/patient data (ages 18-80) showing age did not influence oral clearance; supported no dose adjustment for geriatric LEMS patients. No compartmental structure, software, or algorithm reported in source.

structural_features: 2-compartment (CL, V1, V2, Q) for continuous IV infusion; allometric scaling of CL/V1/Q/V2 by body weight (normalized to 82.9 kg); exponential IIV; proportional residual error; covariates (age, albumin, ALP, ALT, AST, bilirubin, BMI, creatinine clearance, race) tested but none retained
fitting_method_software: Not stated (likely NONMEM; not explicitly named)
notes: Model built from 156 subjects (1337 post-dose samples) pooled across phase 1/2/3 studies in postpartum depression patients; simulations of low/high-dose 60-hour infusion regimens informed Phase 3 dose selection; reviewer noted no label statements rest on this specific model (label based on milk-linked model below).

structural_features: 2-compartment (CL, V1, V2, Q) linking maternal plasma to breast-milk concentrations; allometric scaling by body weight (normalized to 80.25 kg); exponential IIV; proportional residual error; no covariates tested
notes: Fit to 144 plasma and 337 breast-milk samples from 12 lactating women (Study CLP-108, same infusion regimen as Phase 3); parameter estimates cross-checked against the larger multi-study plasma model; formed basis for Section 8.2 Lactation labeling on infant exposure via breastfeeding.

structural_features: Static mechanistic ("basic model") reversible-inhibition risk calculation (R1 = 1 + Imax,u/Ki) per FDA in vitro-in vivo DDI guidance using in vitro IC50/Ki for CYP2C9, CYP2C8, CYP2C19, UGT1A3/1A4/2B7/2B15/2B17 and steady-state Cmax; not a dynamic PBPK simulation
notes: Calculated R1 for CYP2C9 = 1.15, exceeding the 1.02 regulatory cutoff, triggering a required in vivo DDI study; dedicated study CLP-105 (oral phenytoin, CYP2C9 substrate) found no significant PK interaction. Other isoforms (CYP2C8, CYP2C19, UGTs) had R1 below cutoff (~1.0-1.04).

structural_features: SC/PO/IV dosing; dual first-order SC absorption (transit-compartment + direct pathways) plus PO first-order absorption; weight-normalized CL/Vc/Vp; healthy-volunteer vs. HIV-patient effect on CL and Vp; BMI effect on SC bioavailability (Fsc)
notes: 7053 PK observations from 384 subjects (7 studies) justified the 26-week SC dosing interval; underweight subjects have 66% higher SC bioavailability, obese subjects 23% lower, judged not clinically impactful on target Ctrough (above IQ4 of 15.5).

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Exploratory functional-monotherapy analysis related Day-10 concentration to reduction in HIV-1 RNA; near-maximum efficacy at lowest quartile of Ctrough informed target Ctrough threshold. No clear E-R relationship found in pivotal combination-therapy trial.

structural_features: Zero-order IV input into central compartment with 2 peripheral compartments; healthy-vs-infected categorical effect on CL and V1; log-normal IIV, proportional residual error
notes: Pooled 7 studies (2512 observations, 277 subjects) generated exposure metrics for renal/hepatic-impairment labeling (no dose adjustment) and downstream E-R/PTA analyses.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Pooled Phase 2+3 E-R analyses using Bayesian post-hoc exposures found flat relationships between exposure and global cure, time to negative blood culture, GI/serious AEs, suggesting exposures on plateau of response curve.

structural_features: Nonclinical PK-PD-target-based Monte Carlo PTA simulation linking clinical PK to in vitro/animal PK-PD targets (stasis, 1-log kill)
notes: PTA simulations supported selecting 400 mg loading/200 mg weekly regimen over a higher weekly dose; PTA >=90% achieved vs. C. albicans/C. glabrata MIC90 despite protein-binding uncertainty.

structural_features: Combined 2-compartment models for sulbactam and durlobactam (2 compartments each), linear kinetics; total clearance = renal (scaled to baseline CLcr) + nonrenal; off-diagonal omega for durlobactam
notes: 377 subjects; weight, infection status, CLcr (and East Asian region for durlobactam) significant covariates; used to derive renal-function-based dose-adjustment regimens (CLcr 0-200 mL/min).

structural_features: Monte Carlo simulation of 24,360 virtual ABC-infected subjects (15x replication of 203 phase 3 subjects across 8 renal strata) linking PopPK exposures to PK/PD targets (sulbactam %fT>MIC; durlobactam fAUC:MIC=10) and in vitro MIC surveillance (7026 isolates)
notes: Supported revised renal-function-stratified dosing regimens achieving >=90% PTA at MIC=4 mcg/mL across renal categories including ARC and hemodialysis.

structural_features: First-order absorption, 2-compartment disposition for nirmatrelvir with ritonavir coadministration; power-function weight effect on CL/Q/V2/V3; covariates: COVID-19 disease status, CYP3A inducers (carbamazepine)/inhibitors (itraconazole) on CL, age on V2, formulation/dose on F1; nonlinear CLcr-breakpoint on CL
notes: 1237 subjects; high ETA shrinkage (>50%) flagged by reviewer as limiting individual exposure estimate reliability; supported renal-impairment dose adjustment (150/100mg BID moderate impairment).

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: EPIC-HR efficacy E-R: linear regression of Day-5 viral RNA shedding change vs. Cmin/EC90 showed small, likely non-credible slope given narrow exposure range and high ETA shrinkage.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Univariate logistic regression of 10 AEs/10 lab abnormalities vs. Day-5 exposure quartiles; only dysgeusia showed robust signal (AUCROC 0.74); other associations had poor discrimination.

structural_features: Full PBPK model (Simcyp Method 2) for nirmatrelvir; first-order absorption; CYP3A competitive+time-dependent inhibition and induction plus renal clearance; combined with ritonavir first-order compound file
notes: FDA judged Applicant's ritonavir PBPK model inadequate for CYP3A inducers; using alternative model, predicted weak/moderate inducers (e.g. carbamazepine) would minimally affect nirmatrelvir exposure, informing DDI labeling.

structural_features: Linear 2-compartment, first-order absorption/elimination; fixed allometric weight exponents on CL/F, Vc/F, Vp/F, Q/F; asymptotic exponential maturation function on CL using postmenstrual age
notes: 9597 observations, 3133 subjects, 6 trials; maturation function supported extrapolating efficacy/dosing to preterm neonates not directly studied in pivotal trials.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Cox PH model related PopPK-derived AUC quartiles to hazard of medically-attended RSV LRTI; lowest quartile (<12.8 mg*day/mL) showed significantly reduced protection (HR 0.48, p=0.024), establishing target exposure threshold supporting weight-banded single-dose regimen (92.5% achieved target).

structural_features: Joint model for cefepime and enmetazobactam, each 2-compartment disposition with first-order elimination from central compartment; independent PK parameters per compound; combined additive+proportional residual error; added linear clearance term for hemodialysis
notes: 5070 cefepime and 6342 enmetazobactam observations from 588/649 subjects; supported dose adjustments for augmented renal clearance (eGFR>=130) and severe renal impairment/hemodialysis, with separate hemodialysis clearance term added.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Cefepime PK-PD target of 68% fT>MIC derived via logistic regression/CART analysis of 96 subjects with Gram-negative bloodstream infections; supported alongside nonclinical murine-thigh target (60% fT>MIC) for PTA-based dose justification.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: PBPK modeling reconciled contradictory in vitro CYP2E1 inhibition findings for enmetazobactam; predicted 46-208% increase in chlorzoxazone AUC, supporting weak-to-moderate CYP2E1 inhibitor conclusion.

structural_features: Linear elimination from central compartment with 2 peripheral compartments; baseline CLcr on CL a priori; base model refined across pooled ABSSSI, CABP, SAB indications (incl. 20 hemodialysis SAB subjects) with indication-specific covariates
notes: Final dataset pooled 953 subjects (6024 observations); supported ESRD/hemodialysis dosing (250 mg q24h, post-dialysis) and PTA-based dose selection across indications.

structural_features: Linear 3-compartment model with renal clearance-GFR relationship (Rhodin fat-free-mass formula); weight on volume (estimated exponent) and clearance (fixed allometric 0.75); fit to pooled pediatric (112 subjects, 3mo-18y) and phase 1 adult data
estimation_technique: Allometric scaling; Empirical Bayes estimation; Simulation
notes: Supported dosing down to 3 months age for CABP and pediatric renal-impairment dose adjustments via exposure-matching/PTA to adult exposures; PTA >=87% across pediatric renal-impairment subgroups.

structural_features: Absorption via transit compartments with fraction of dose in a slow transit chain; nonlinear (Michaelis-Menten) elimination above proposed dosage; central + 2 peripheral compartments; extended with urine compartment (~48% fixed fraction of plasma clearance to urine)
notes: 12 studies (rich phase 1 + sparse phase 3); ~2-fold AUC increase with decreasing CLcr, though correlated covariates (renal function, food, probenecid) limited interpretability; urine model misfit one phase 3 trial's urine data.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: PTA simulations used %fT>MIC targets from a murine thigh-infection model (deemed unreliable) and an in vitro model (prioritized) to support the 500 mg BID dose and 0.5 mcg/mL breakpoint; clinical E-R analysis infeasible given sparse PK sampling (n=118 of 787 ITT).

structural_features: 2-compartment disposition with transit-compartment absorption (3 fasted/4 fed) and linear elimination; separate renal/non-renal clearance; allometric weight scaling; eGFR on renal clearance; post-hoc hepatic-function (Child-Pugh B/C) covariate on non-renal clearance
notes: 14 studies (11,608 plasma + 2,700 urine concentrations, 1,177 subjects); weight/eGFR most influential covariates; hepatic-impairment covariate estimated 24%/56% higher AUC in moderate/severe impairment, comparable to NCA estimates.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Logistic regression of response vs. free AUCss/AUCss-MIC in uUTI subjects found no significant exposure-response relationship, supporting fixed 1500 mg BID dose across observed exposure range.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Logistic regression of cholinergic TEAEs vs. exposure in pooled uUTI studies; apparent association confounded by study (weight/exposure differences), lost significance after adjustment - no true causal exposure-AE relationship.

structural_features: Not applicable
fitting_method_software: Simcyp v21 (superseded v19; v23 for later MATE simulation)
notes: Full PBPK model (ADAM absorption) verified against itraconazole/rifampin DDI studies; predicted effects of weak/moderate CYP3A modulators and gepotidacin's MATE-inhibitor effect on metformin; reviewer flagged lack of P-gp component as limitation.

structural_features: Two-compartment disposition with first-order IM absorption and first-order elimination; body-weight power-function allometric scaling (reference 5 kg) on CL/F, Vc/F, Vp/F, Q/F; sigmoidal maturation function on CL/F based on time-varying adjusted (gestational+postnatal) age; informative adult-model priors on Ka, Vp/F and IIV of Ka/Vc/F due to sparse infant sampling
notes: Pooled 2942 preterm/full-term infants (5831 quantifiable concentrations) from 3 trials; body weight and race statistically significant but not clinically meaningful; supported a single fixed 105-mg IM dose across body-weight/age subgroups. FDA estimated median terminal half-life ~80 days vs. Applicant's NCA-based 44 days.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Logistic regression of RSV-associated MALRI and hospitalization (Days 1-150) vs. model-derived AUC0-150d/Ctrough in 2291 infants; relationship flat/not clinically meaningful, indicating the single 105-mg dose reaches an efficacy plateau; no significant effect modification by weight or age.

structural_features: Oral depot compartment with GI transit-chain absorption model (non-integer transit compartments, mean transit time) feeding first-order Ka into one systemic compartment with linear elimination; categorical IIV shifts for meal fat content; formulation-type effect on relative bioavailability
notes: 261 healthy/gonorrhea participants (6043 concentrations), 6 phase 1 studies + phase 3; food and body weight key covariates; simulations extrapolated PK to adolescents and 35-<50 kg patients (unstudied in phase 3), supporting body-weight-tailored fasted/fed single 3-g dosing with adequate PK-PD target attainment (fAUC/MIC >=70.6).

structural_features: Whole-body full PBPK model with ADAM absorption model (mechanistic Peff, particle-size population balance dissolution); hepatic elimination split CYP3A4 (~32%) vs. non-CYP (~68%); renal clearance component
notes: Verified against itraconazole DDI study; predicted strong CYP3A inhibitors increase AUC ~1.4-fold, strong/moderate inducers (rifampin/efavirenz) decrease AUC 56%/41%; supported labeling against strong CYP3A4 inducers for the single-dose 3-g regimen.

structural_features: One-compartment BLV disposition, first-order SC absorption, parallel linear plus nonlinear Michaelis-Menten elimination; inhibitory Emax effect of model-predicted bile-salt concentration on BLV Vmax; bile salts modeled as indirect-response (turnover) model with inhibitory Emax effect of BLV concentration on kout (bidirectional drug-biomarker interaction); fixed allometric exponents for weight
notes: 464 subjects (7024 BLV/8010 bile-salt observations), 4 studies; body weight and time-varying ADA-positivity the only significant covariates, no clinically relevant effect of age/sex/race/renal/hepatic function; supported 8.5-mg (nominal 10-mg) once-daily dose without adjustment. Applicant's separate E-R models for HDV viral load were rejected by FDA as confounded by >99% protein binding and time-varying ADA-bound fraction; FDA instead ran an independent descriptive (non-model) dose-response comparison.

structural_features: Separate two-compartment models for cefepime and zidebactam, first-order clearance from central compartment; renal clearance as sigmoidal Hill-type function of de-indexed eGFR; combined additive-proportional residual error
fitting_algorithm: Laplacian conditional estimation with eta-epsilon interaction
notes: Serum albumin, weight, age, ethnicity, BMI/sex covariates used, but renal function the only clinically meaningful one; 1000-subject-per-renal-group Monte Carlo simulations supported renal-function-stratified dosing achieving >=90% joint PK-PD target attainment up to MIC 64 ug/mL at FDA breakpoints.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Neutropenic murine lung-infection dose-fractionation studies across MDR K. pneumoniae, E. coli, P. aeruginosa identified %fT>MIC as best-correlated PK-PD index; established nonclinical PK-PD targets used in human PopPK-based Monte Carlo PTA analyses supporting dose selection and susceptibility breakpoints.

structural_features: First-order absorption, first-order elimination from central compartment; weight as fixed allometric exponent on CL/F and Vc/F; food and formulation (tablet vs suspension) effects on Ka
notes: 3,325 subjects/12,493 observations across 7 studies including pivotal SCORPIO-PEP; supported labeling of no clinically significant PK differences by age/sex/race; exposure decreases 2-3 fold with increasing BMI category.

structural_features: Not applicable
estimation_technique: Logistic regression; reviewer-fit Emax model with logistic link
notes: Applicant's logistic regression (placebo arm included, exposure forced in) found exposure statistically significant for COVID-19 infection risk; reviewer's analysis restricted to treatment arm only found flat exposure-response, concluding Applicant's finding was driven by placebo-vs-treatment differences. No dose adjustment for BMI >=40 despite numerically higher (imprecise, n=2/22) infection rate.

structural_features: Transit-compartment absorption; linear renal and non-renal elimination; weight as fixed allometric exponent on V1/V2/Q (1.0 volumes, 0.75 Q); eGFR (power function) on renal clearance; blood-to-plasma relationship modeled with hematocrit predictor
notes: 5 Phase 1 + 2 Phase 3 studies (9,064 observations, 1,401 subjects); supported renal dose adjustments (600mg q6h eGFR>=60; 300mg q6h eGFR 30-59; 300mg q12h eGFR 15-29); confirmed no meaningful age/sex/race/weight effect.

structural_features: Monte Carlo PTA simulation combining PopPK model with preclinical (murine acute pyelonephritis) PK-PD efficacy targets
notes: Used to inform susceptibility test interpretive criteria for Enterobacterales; reviewer disagreed with Applicant's in vitro-derived target, judging in vivo (murine)-derived target more appropriate; concluded Applicant's proposed STIC not well supported.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Univariable/multivariable analyses of Phase 3 cUTI/AP data found no significant exposure-response or dose-response with test-of-cure, likely due to limited exposure range; could not confirm dosage adequacy independently of PopPK/PTA approach.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Thorough QT study (therapeutic 600mg and supratherapeutic 1200mg vs placebo/moxifloxacin); concentration-QTc modeling demonstrated no clinically relevant QT/QTc prolongation at either dose.

structural_features: Mechanistic static and dynamic PBPK modeling per ICH M12 guideline for CYP1A2/CYP3A4 induction
notes: In vitro hepatocyte induction signals (1/3 donors each for CYP1A2/CYP3A4) triggered PBPK simulations at 600mg q6h; predicted up to ~30% reduction in sensitive substrate exposure, classified as weak induction risk, driven by hypersensitive donors, judged unlikely clinically meaningful.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Graphical dose-response analysis pooling Phase II/III trials (MADRS/HAM-D) supported that 20mg would provide similar efficacy to approved 40mg dose; dose-dependent AEs concentrated in titration phase (10->20->40mg over days 1-14).

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: PBPK simulations of strong CYP3A4 inhibition (ketoconazole) predicted worst-case ~85% inhibition of pre-systemic metabolism at 200mg BID ketoconazole (vs. ~50% AUC increase observed clinically at 200mg QD); separate simulations supported no clinically relevant interaction with CYP2C8 substrate rosiglitazone.

structural_features: Zero-order absorption with lag time (~0.5 hr); linear elimination; covariates of sex, body weight, creatinine clearance on CL/F and V/F
notes: Model integrated Phase I/II/III data; IIV of 20.5% (CL/F), 33.9% (V/F); used to derive renal-impairment dosing regimen (reviewer independently simulated concentration-time profiles, proposing a modified regimen vs. sponsor's); no additional age effect after accounting for renal function.

structural_features: Not applicable (dose/exposure-response relating to categorical/ordinal efficacy and safety scales)
notes: PK/PD model linked steady-state gabapentin AUC/Cmax (predicted) to RLS efficacy (IRLS score, CGI) and safety endpoints (dizziness, somnolence, cognition) using pooled 12-week Phase II/III data (600-2400mg, >10-fold AUC range); supported selecting 600mg maintenance dose over 1200mg (similar efficacy, better safety/sedation). Detailed pharmacometrics appendix was redacted (b)(4) in source PDF, so exact model form could not be confirmed.

structural_features: First-order absorption with lag time (Ka, Tlag); apparent clearance (CL/F) and volume (V/F)
notes: Model built from 791 Phase 1/3 subjects; renal function (CRCL, ESRD status) was the most influential covariate on CL/F, while age/sex/race were not significant; dose-normalized concentrations differed by assay method (HPLC vs LC-MS/MS), requiring a method-conversion factor.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: PK-model-derived individual exposures were linked to Delta-MWT/Delta-ESS efficacy (Emax model: placebo effect +0.8 min, drug Emax +13.3 min on MWT) and to insomnia/blood-pressure/heart-rate safety outcomes, with Cmax the best predictor of insomnia risk (6.2%/9.3% at 150/300 mg); supported the approved 75-300 mg titration scheme.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Dedicated single-dose (75 mg) PK study in normal/mild/moderate/severe renal impairment and ESRD-hemodialysis groups; AUCinf increased ~1.5-4.4-fold (6.2-fold in ESRD) and half-life increased ~1.2-3.9-fold with worsening renal function, directly supporting renal dose-adjustment recommendations and the ESRD contraindication.

structural_features: Two-compartment disposition with first-order elimination and combined zero-/first-order absorption (Ka, D1); full-block covariance matrix on IIV (CL/F, Vc/F, Vp/F, Q/F, Ka, D1); base structure carried over from a prior healthy-volunteer/RRMS model, re-estimated on sparse SPMS data with non-identifiable parameters fixed
notes: Model built on 3,362-3,454 plasma concentrations from SPMS patients (Study A2304); body weight and CYP2C9 genotype were significant covariates on CL/F (CL/F 38-74% lower in *1/*3, n=148; *2/*3, n=32; *3/*3, n=2 vs *1/*1, n=740), supporting genotype-based dose reduction/exclusion.

structural_features: Whole-body PBPK model with first-order absorption and enzyme-kinetics elimination (CYP2B6, CYP2C8, CYP2C19, CYP3A4, CYP2C9) using CYP2C9-genotype-specific intrinsic clearance values; verified against observed fluconazole (inhibitor) and rifampicin (inducer) DDI trial data
notes: PBPK model used to predict siponimod exposure changes with additional untested CYP3A4/CYP2C9 inhibitors (ketoconazole, erythromycin, fluvoxamine) and inducers (efavirenz) across CYP2C9 genotypes; supported DDI-based dosing/labeling recommendations beyond the two dedicated clinical DDI studies.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Dedicated Phase 1 studies (A2129 renal, A2122 hepatic) found Cmax/AUC changes under ~25% across severe renal and mild-severe hepatic impairment groups vs matched healthy subjects, with no correlation to Child-Pugh score or bilirubin; supported no dose adjustment in either population.

structural_features: Not stated in source; sponsor-developed model referenced only descriptively (no compartment/algorithm details reported in the ClinPharmR)
notes: Model characterized steady-state exposure at the 35.6 mg therapeutic dose (mean Cmax ~73 ng/mL, AUC ~812 ng*h/mL) and found ~2-fold higher exposure in CYP2D6 poor metabolizers, supporting labeling on CYP2D6 status.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Three dedicated 2-period crossover DDI studies (n=18 healthy adults each) evaluated paroxetine (CYP2D6 inhibitor: AUC +2.2-fold, dose halved), rifampicin (CYP3A4 inducer: AUC -48%, dose doubled), and itraconazole (CYP3A4 inhibitor: negligible effect, no adjustment); results directly set label dose-adjustment strategy.
