structural_features: Two-compartment model with first-order absorption (bi-exponential decline); apparent central/peripheral volumes (V1/F, V2/F), intercompartmental clearance (Q/F), apparent clearance (CL/F); terminal half-life derived from post-hoc (empirical Bayes) CL/F and V/F estimates
notes: PopPK database spanned ~1,034-1,449 subjects (2,645-10,909 concentrations) pooled across Phase 1-3 studies; body weight, bilirubin, sex, Asian race, smoking status, and concomitant CYP3A4 inhibitors were significant CL/F covariates; no dose adjustment recommended given lack of a clear dose-response relationship.

structural_features: Disease-progression/placebo-response (DP-PR) component combined with an Emax exposure-response term (individual predicted AUCss as driver) for Percent OFF time
notes: Model developed from 1,760 patients / 9,108 Percent OFF time measurements across six Phase 2/3 trials; smoking status (via lower AUCss) and concomitant COMT inhibitors were significant effect modifiers (e.g., smokers ~12-18% lower predicted response than non-smokers at 20-40 mg/day).

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: In 1,198 istradefylline-treated and 591 placebo patients from six Phase 2/3 trials, dyskinesia, dizziness, and nausea were selected for exposure-response modeling based on graphical screening; individual predicted AUCss was the exposure predictor in naive-pooled logistic regression models of each dichotomous adverse event.

structural_features: First-order absorption with 5 transit compartments modeling absorption delay, 2-compartment disposition, combined additive+proportional residual error
fitting_method_software: NONMEM v7.3+ (PsN for stepwise covariate modeling)
notes: 583 subjects from 16 Phase 1 studies (healthy + migraine patients); no clinically meaningful effect of age, weight, BMI, BSA, sex, race, ethnicity, disease status, or formulation on exposure; VPC supported model adequacy; absolute bioavailability 55-66%.

structural_features: Direct-effect power model linking individually predicted PopPK concentrations to standard deviation of lateral position (SDLP), SDLP=BASE*(1+SLP(t)*CONC^gamma), with time-decreasing slope parameter
pk_exposure_metric: Not applicable (linked to time-matched plasma concentration)
notes: Pooled driving-impairment studies LAHG (n=90) and LAIF (n=68); model could not reliably predict impairment dissipation between 1.5-8h; supported 8-hour no-driving labeling but showed some subjects had persistent impairment beyond 8h, unexplained by exposure or sedation scores.

structural_features: Whole-body PBPK (Simcyp ADAM absorption model) verified with quinidine (CYP2D6 inhibitor) and dextromethorphan (CYP2D6 substrate); also used for P-gp substrate digoxin
notes: Supported conclusion that lasmiditan (CYP2D6 Ki=20.7 uM in vitro, DDI index R1=1.02) is unlikely to cause clinically significant CYP2D6 inhibition of dextromethorphan or P-gp-mediated digoxin interaction, avoiding need for additional dedicated clinical DDI trials.

structural_features: 2-compartment, first-order absorption with absorption lag time, exponential inter-individual variability, combined proportional+additive residual error
notes: 8700 observations from 960 subjects (8 Phase 1, 2 Phase 2, 1 Phase 3 study), doses 5-750 mg single/50-600 mg/day multiple; CL/F increased with dose, body surface area, and carbamazepine coadministration; decreased with clobazam coadministration and bilirubin; lower CL/F and V1/F in African American/Hispanic subjects; used to support labeling and simulate alternative (slower) titration regimens.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: 104,037 seizure-diary records from 655 subjects (Phase 2 trials c013/c017); generalized Poisson model (base seizure rate modified by site and a power-law exposure-treatment effect) on daily partial seizure count; predictive checks reasonably reproduced observed 50%-responder rates across 100/200/400 mg/day arms, supporting dose/exposure-efficacy relationship. A parallel exposure-safety (ALT/AST) model was generated by the sponsor but not reviewed by FDA (too few events); DRESS exposure-response not assessable (only 3 events) - no rows created for these.

structural_features: Integrated parent-metabolite model for lumateperone (IC200056) and two direct unconjugated metabolites (IC200131, IC200161), including first-pass effect description
notes: Combined single/repeat oral (5-140 mg) and single IV (40 ug) data from 4 studies in healthy volunteers and schizophrenia patients; creatinine clearance found to modestly influence parent-drug clearance; body weight, gender, subject type, race tested but not significant; reviewer's independent analysis supported applicant's findings.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Studies ITI-007-005 and -301: change from baseline in Total PANSS score (Day 28) vs. IC200056 exposure showed a U-shaped pattern, complicating a simple monotonic dose-response interpretation used to help justify the recommended 42 mg dose.

structural_features: Structural compartmental model with absorption/disposition informed by intensively-sampled Phase 1 data; covariates (age, BMI, sex, race, PPI use) evaluated only on apparent oral clearance due to sparse Phase 2/3 sampling
notes: 12,230 observations from 1,892 subjects (Phase 1 plus insomnia studies 201/303/304); lower clearance in elderly (26% lower, not clinically relevant) and with higher BMI; no sex/race effect; simulations (N=250/subset) used to show AUCss differences by age/BMI were not clinically meaningful; concomitant PPI use was also evaluated.

structural_features: Whole-body PBPK model of CYP3A4/5-mediated lemborexant metabolism; simulated weak/moderate/strong CYP3A inhibitors (ranitidine, fluoxetine, fluconazole, itraconazole) and inducers (rifampin)
notes: PBPK model verified against clinical DDI data (itraconazole, fluconazole) and judged adequate; predicted <2-fold exposure increase with weak CYP3A inhibitors (e.g., ranitidine) not directly tested clinically, supporting labeling without additional dedicated trials.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Concentration-QTc analysis (Phase 1 Studies 002/003) used in lieu of a dedicated thorough-QT study, per QT-IRT agreement; upper bound of 90% CI for predicted ddQTcF at supratherapeutic (50 mg) exposure was <10 ms; QT-IRT concluded no clinically relevant QT prolongation.

structural_features: 2-compartment model with linear elimination from the central compartment; transit-compartment absorption model (TCAM) for absorption; log-additive (proportional) residual error
notes: 17,187 PK observations from 2,287 subjects (Phase 1-3, including a Phase 3 sparse-PK substudy of 1,216 patients); CL/F decreased with worsening hepatic impairment (94 to 76.3 to 53.5 L/h, normal/mild to moderate to severe); food, formulation, and race also evaluated as covariates; model supported hepatic-impairment dosing recommendations.

structural_features: Central + peripheral compartments; linear intercompartmental clearance (CLp) and linear elimination from central compartment (CL); additive + proportional residual error
notes: N=2123 subjects (83 healthy, 1313+ patients) pooled from 8 studies. Bodyweight, disease status, baseline migraine days, and creatinine clearance were significant covariates on CL; bodyweight, disease status, sex on central volume. All covariate effects <1.5-fold on AUC0-Tau, deemed not clinically relevant; applicant recommended no dose adjustment (fixed IV dosing only).

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Exposure metrics from final popPK model regressed against change from baseline in monthly migraine days using a placebo-anchored saturable inhibitory Emax approach, separately for episodic and chronic migraine. Supported flat dose 100 mg/300 mg efficacy relationship; reviewer found analysis reasonable.

structural_features: 4-transit absorption compartments, linear elimination; covariates on CL (weight, fluconazole, hepatic impairment, itraconazole), on transit rate (food, formulation, itraconazole), on volume (weight), and on bioavailability (food)
fitting_method_software: Not stated (nonlinear mixed-effects modeling software, not named in review text)
notes: Pooled data from 8 clinical studies (75 mg dose), validated against a 9th study. No clinically relevant effect of age/weight/sex/race on exposure after covariate adjustment; used to support labeling. Reviewer noted VPCs showed unexplained variability and Cmax underprediction.

structural_features: Same base structural model as above, used for simulation of fed state, hepatic impairment (moderate/severe), and CYP3A4 DDI (fluconazole-moderate, itraconazole-severe) scenarios
notes: Simulation (n=1000) showed itraconazole meaningfully altered rimegepant PK (observed: Cmax ~1.5-fold, AUC ~4-fold increase, consistent with ~74% CL reduction); alternative dosing intervals (2/3/3.5/4 days) simulated and a 3-day interval identified as exposure-matched/optimal.

structural_features: First-order formation of active metabolite CC112273 with lag time, first-order elimination; covariates on CL/F (sex, smoking, hepatic impairment, body weight, baseline bilirubin, RMS-patient status), on V2/F and K12 (sex, hepatic impairment, body weight)
fitting_method_software: NONMEM v7.3 (sponsor); reviewer replicated with NONMEM VII
notes: 9402 PK samples from 1687 subjects. Smoking was an important covariate: smokers had ~55% lower metabolite steady-state AUC than nonsmokers (lower MAO-B activity), supporting the 7-day dose-escalation scheme regardless of smoking status. Reviewer independently replicated sponsor's model.

structural_features: Indirect response model with inhibitory Emax model linking metabolite CC112273 concentration to absolute lymphocyte count (ALC, PD marker)
notes: Model characterized concentration-ALC relationship in healthy subjects and RMS patients. No relationship was seen between parent ozanimod AUCss and ALC reduction, supporting that the active metabolite (not parent) drives the PD effect.

structural_features: 1 transit absorption compartment, first-order elimination, dose-dependent (nonlinear) relative bioavailability; covariates: female gender, Asian race, baseline total bilirubin on CL/F; Asian race on V2/F; evening dosing on Ka; simultaneous levodopa/DDCI coadministration on Ka and F1; micronized vs. nonmicronized formulation effect on Ka and F1
notes: 9686 quantifiable concentrations from 724 subjects (18 Phase 1 studies + 3 PD-patient studies). Simulation predicted Asian subjects have ~40% higher exposure vs. White subjects (outside BE bounds); dedicated Japanese-vs-Caucasian study confirmed ~20% higher exposure but no dose adjustment ultimately required. Model also confirmed micronized formulation has 67% higher relative bioavailability at 50 mg and evening dosing slows absorption.

structural_features: Two-compartment model, zero-order IV infusion input; parallel linear and non-linear (modified Michaelis-Menten) elimination with mono-exponential decay of Vmax over time (TMDD-like nonlinear clearance); allometric scaling of CL, Vc, Q, Vp on body weight
notes: n=213 subjects (1617 PK obs) pooled from Phase 1-3 in SSc, MS, NMOSD patients. Renal markers, bilirubin, age, gender, race, ADA status tested but not retained; supported no dose adjustment for age or organ impairment.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: n=230 NMOSD patients (Study 1155). PopPK-derived AUC used to define exposure terciles; Cox model showed treatment effect vs. placebo but no clear exposure-response among treated subjects (applicant proposed an "efficacy plateau").

structural_features: Two-compartment model, first-order SC absorption, parallel linear and non-linear (Michaelis-Menten) elimination representing TMDD; allometric scaling of CL/Q (exponent fixed 1) and Vc/Vp (exponent fixed 0.75) normalized to 60 kg
notes: PK data from healthy volunteers and NMO/NMOSD Phase 3 trials. Disease status, body weight, time-varying immunogenicity, SC formulation were covariates on clearance. Formal E-R analyses not reviewed by FDA because both trials used a single dosing regimen.

structural_features: Minimal PBPK "disease-drug interaction" model linking IL-6-mediated CYP suppression to CYP450-probe-substrate exposure in virtual NMO/NMOSD patients (simvastatin/CYP3A4, S-warfarin/CYP2C9, omeprazole/CYP2C19, caffeine/CYP1A2, dextromethorphan/CYP2D6, midazolam/CYP3A4)
notes: Evaluated whether satralizumab-mediated IL-6 suppression (restoring CYP expression) could change CYP-probe exposure. FDA's Division of Pharmacometrics concluded the approach could not prospectively quantify this indirect interaction; deemed exploratory, not used for label DDI claims.

structural_features: Two-compartment model, sequential zero-order/first-order absorption, first-order elimination; covariates: body weight on CL/Vc/Vp, race on CL and peripheral volume, food/formulation on absorption lag time, disease status (psoriasis, MS, hepatic impairment) on CL and central volume
notes: n=680 subjects from 13 studies, including dedicated hepatic/renal-impairment cohorts (n=8 each). Simulations at 20 mg QD showed moderate/severe hepatic impairment increased Cmax beyond typical between-subject variability; renal impairment, race, weight, food/formulation within normal variability.

structural_features: Two linked submodels on base PopPK: (1) heart-rate model with circadian rhythm, tolerance compartment, Imax drug-effect term declining with tolerance; (2) indirect-response (turnover) model for total lymphocyte count with circadian variation and concentration-dependent inhibition of production rate
notes: Simulations of proposed up-titration regimen predicted <1% daily bradycardia incidence (~2.9-3.0% cumulative Days 1-15), consistent with observed 0.7% (4/565) in Phase 3; supported the up-titration dosing regimen adopted in labeling.

structural_features: Whole-body PBPK model of ponesimod as CYP3A/CYP2C9/CYP2C19 perpetrator; DDI simulations with midazolam (CYP3A), tolbutamide/S-warfarin (CYP2C9), S-mephenytoin/omeprazole (CYP2C19)
notes: Predicted low potential for clinically relevant DDI with sensitive CYP3A/2C9/2C19 substrates (ratios ~1.0-1.3); model reasonably reproduced observed PK but somewhat overpredicted exposure.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Concentration-QTc analysis found no clinically relevant QTc prolongation at therapeutic 20 mg dose, upper bound of two-sided 90% CI at 5.9 ms; supported label QT statement.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Cross-study NCA (relative bioavailability study, n=29) established PK "linkage" between KP415 and reference product Focalin XR despite non-bioequivalent profiles. Separate NCA across children (6-8y n=10; 9-12y n=10), adolescents (n=5), adults (n=28) supported extrapolating pediatric efficacy to adolescents/adults without age-based dose adjustment.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Concentration-QTc analysis from intranasal SDX human-abuse-potential study (n=46) at ~40-fold therapeutic Cmax margin found no clinically significant QTc prolongation (ddQTcF +0.9 msec); supported waiving a dedicated thorough-QT study.

structural_features: One-compartment model with first-order absorption/elimination of parent viloxazine, plus first-order formation/elimination of 5-hydroxy-viloxazine glucuronide metabolite (simultaneous parent-metabolite model)
notes: n=495 subjects from 4 studies; body weight was key covariate on Vd/CL for parent and metabolite. Simulations at 100-600 mg showed Cmax/AUC ~37-50% higher in children (median 31.5 kg) than adolescents (median 57.25 kg) at same dose, consistent with similar ADHD-RS-5 efficacy across ages; sex/race showed no clinically relevant effect.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Open-label 3-period crossover cocktail DDI study in healthy adults evaluated viloxazine ER 900 mg QD effects on CYP1A2 (caffeine), CYP2D6 (dextromethorphan), CYP3A4 (midazolam) probes; midazolam AUC increased ~1.7-fold with no Cmax change, indicating viloxazine is a weak CYP3A4 inhibitor.

structural_features: Separate 2-compartment models for retigabine and its N-acetyl metabolite; covariates CRCL (nonlinear) and BSA (nonlinear) and dose (linear) and lamotrigine coadministration on CL; age (nonlinear) on V2; metabolite model: CRCL and SGPT on CL
notes: Pooled 23 studies (15 Phase I, 5 Phase II, 3 Phase III) in healthy subjects, renal/hepatic-impaired subjects, and epilepsy patients; CRCL, BSA, dose and lamotrigine were statistically significant but not clinically meaningful covariates on clearance; supported no dose adjustment despite renal-impairment covariate effect.

structural_features: Not applicable
fitting_method_software: SAS 9.2 (FDA reviewer reanalysis); sponsor software not stated
estimation_technique: Nonlinear regression (inhibitory Hill/Emax equation); Logistic regression with probit link
notes: Pooled 2 Phase 3 trials (studies 301, 302); Hill/Emax model linked AUC to percent reduction in seizure frequency, plateauing near 1200 mg/day; probit-link logistic regression showed AUC-dependent increase in responder probability and 6 safety endpoints; supported effectiveness of proposed dosing.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Pre/post retigabine coadministration trough concentrations of concomitant AEDs from 2 Phase 3 studies compared via 90% CI of geometric mean ratios against 80-125% bioequivalence limits; retigabine reduced lamotrigine trough concentrations by ~20%, minimal effect on other AEDs.

structural_features: Parent (clobazam)-metabolite (N-desmethylclobazam/N-CLB) formation-elimination model; CYP3A4 inducers (phenobarbital, phenytoin, carbamazepine) tested as covariate on N-CLB formation fraction (Fm); CYP2C19 inducers/inhibitors tested as covariates on N-CLB elimination (K40); apparent Vd of metabolite fixed to 1
estimation_technique: Objective function value (OFV)-based covariate model selection
notes: Population PK model tested AED covariate groups (CYP3A4 inducers n=18, CYP2C19 inducers n=77, CYP2C19 inhibitors n=17); CYP3A4 inducers increased N-CLB formation fraction by 9.4% and CYP2C19 inducers increased N-CLB elimination by 10.5%, netting to no dose adjustment needed.

structural_features: NONMEM $MIX mixture model classifying patients as responder/non-responder; sigmoidal time-course placebo-effect model (asymptote, T50, steepness parameters); responder model based on competitive agonism between clobazam and N-CLB at shared receptor (Emax-type interaction); empirical Bayes patient-specific parameter estimates
notes: Two-stage NONMEM mixture model of Phase 3 (OV-1012) data modeling fractional change from baseline in drop-seizure frequency; responders showed competitive agonism between clobazam and N-CLB (N-CLB EC50=0.9 ug/mL, ~1/3 potency of clobazam EC50=0.303 ug/mL); confirmed clear exposure-response relationship.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Dedicated in vivo DDI study using dextromethorphan (CYP2D6 probe): clobazam coadministration increased dextromethorphan AUC by 90% and Cmax by 59%, indicating weak CYP2D6 inhibition; supported labeling caution for narrow-therapeutic-index CYP2D6 substrates.

structural_features: Covariates on CL/F: sex, bilirubin, albumin, enzyme-inducer co-administration; covariates on V2/F: albumin, age, race, body weight
notes: Pooled data from 834 patients (Phase II HMR1726D/2001, Phase III EFC6049) plus 10 healthy subjects (Phase I TDR10892); sex, enzyme-inducer use, bilirubin and albumin were significant covariates on CL/F; bilirubin increased AUC0-24ss 1.73-fold at 14 mg dose in patients with bilirubin >17 umol/L.

structural_features: Not applicable
estimation_technique: Nonlinear/binned regression of ARR vs. concentration
notes: FDA reviewer's independent exposure-response analysis of pivotal Phase III trial EFC6049 (TEMSO) linked annualized relapse rate to steady-state mean concentration, confirming a concentration-dependent reduction in ARR (contrary to sponsor's conclusion of no relationship); supported the 14 mg/day dose.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: In vivo DDI studies with rifampin (broad CYP/P-gp inducer, -40% teriflunomide AUC), repaglinide (CYP2C8/OATP1B1 substrate, +2.3-fold AUC), warfarin (no PK change, -25% peak INR), and oral contraceptives (+60% ethinyl estradiol exposure); supported labeling on OATP1B1/CYP2C8 substrate caution and inducer avoidance.

structural_features: Two-compartment model with first-order oral absorption based on 19 Phase 1 studies in healthy subjects (CPMS-E2007-2011-002)
notes: Phase 1 population PK model estimated Vd/F ~75L, CL/F ~11.9 mL/min; used by sponsor and FDA pharmacometrics reviewer to simulate titration regimens and confirm steady-state fluctuation index (~42%), supporting proposed titration/maintenance dosing schedule.

structural_features: Pooled analysis of 3 pivotal Phase 3 trials (CPMS-E2007-2011-003); enzyme-inducing AEDs (carbamazepine, oxcarbazepine, phenytoin, topiramate) as significant covariates increasing CL/F; gender effect (16-20% lower CL/F in females); creatinine clearance tested as covariate for renal function
notes: Pooled Phase 3 dataset (711 normal, 52 mild, 3 moderate renal-impairment patients); enzyme-inducing AEDs increased CL/F; no clinically significant correlation between CL/F and creatinine clearance; supported no dose adjustment for mild renal impairment and cautious use with slower titration in moderate impairment.

structural_features: Not applicable
estimation_technique: Binned/model-predicted regression of dose- and concentration-response
notes: FDA pharmacometric reviewer related average steady-state concentration (predicted from Phase 3 population PK model) to seizure-frequency reduction (efficacy) and hostility/aggression AEs (safety, MedDRA SMQ) across 3 Phase 3 trials; efficacy plateaued between 8-12 mg while AE risk continued to increase.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Dedicated single-dose (1 mg) study (E2007-044-015) in Child-Pugh A/B patients vs. matched healthy controls (N=6/group): total AUC0-inf increased 49% (mild) and 155% (moderate) with prolonged t1/2; free-drug AUC increased 1.81-fold and 3.28-fold respectively due to reduced protein binding.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: In vivo DDI studies: ketoconazole (strong CYP3A4/5 inhibitor) modestly increased perampanel exposure (~20%); carbamazepine (strong CYP3A4 inducer) markedly increased perampanel clearance; perampanel was a weak inducer of CYP3A/CYP2B6; supported avoiding strong CYP3A inducers and monitoring with strong inhibitors.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: NCA of active metabolite MMF across Phase 1 studies (single-dose escalation, food-effect studies) informed food/dosing labeling; PK samples not collected in Phase 3, so no exposure-response for efficacy/safety could be established; DDI assessed only in vitro (low potential), no clinical DDI studies conducted.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Pooled NCA of vortioxetine and metabolites (Lu AA34443, Lu AA39835) across 12 Phase 1 studies in healthy subjects; linear PK over 5-20mg QD with t1/2 ~65h at steady state; clinical DDI studies showed a strong CYP2D6 inhibitor (bupropion) raises exposure (dose halved) and strong CYP inducers (rifampicin) lower exposure (dose tripled).

structural_features: Not applicable
estimation_technique: Mixed-effects model repeated measures (MMRM) for efficacy; descriptive trend analysis for safety
notes: Pooled meta-analysis (10 studies, n=3060) found no consistent dose-response for MADRS efficacy across 5-20mg, but a dose-related increase in nausea (9.2% placebo up to ~32% at 15-20mg) and nausea-related discontinuation.

structural_features: First-order absorption and elimination; allometric function of body weight on CL/F as surrogate for renal-function effect
notes: Pooled Phase III data (BIA-2093-301/302/303) in adult epilepsy patients; carbamazepine and phenobarbital (enzyme inducers) increased CL/F, supporting higher maintenance dosing; gender, race, renal function not significant covariates.

structural_features: Sparse-sampling models estimating a single parameter (CL/F, fixed literature volume) fit separately for each of 6 co-administered AEDs (carbamazepine, gabapentin, levetiracetam, phenobarbital, phenytoin, valproate) to predict Cavss
notes: Evaluated effect of eslicarbazepine acetate (400/800/1200mg) on co-administered AED clearance; carbamazepine CL/F increased ~4-12% and phenytoin CL/F decreased ~4-11%; no clinically relevant effect on valproate, levetiracetam, gabapentin.

structural_features: Emax model relating predicted steady-state average concentration (Cavss) to log-transformed percent reduction in standardized seizure frequency from baseline; responder-rate (binary) endpoint also modeled
fitting_method_software: S-Plus 7.0 (sponsor's original fit); NONMEM (FDA reviewer's independent re-run)
estimation_technique: Nonlinear regression (GLS); logistic regression for responder endpoint
notes: Pooled Phase III data (studies 2093-301/302; 628 patients, 1256 observations); confirmed significant exposure-response relationship supporting approved 400-1200mg dose range.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Dedicated 2-period crossover DDI studies (e.g., digoxin, warfarin) used standard NCA (Cmax, AUCtau, Cmin, PTF) to assess PK/PD (INR) interactions between eslicarbazepine/metabolite BIA 2-005 and co-medications.

structural_features: Dose-dependent bioavailability (F1), sigmoidal absorption with lag time, linear distribution to first peripheral compartment, first-order elimination from central compartment
notes: PopPK model built from 16 Phase 1 studies; used to support 15mg starting dose selection for both elderly and non-elderly (no significant exposure difference between elderly 15mg and non-elderly 20mg); dose adjustment recommended for obese females.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: n=2809 phase 2/3 insomnia patients; no clear dose/exposure-response for objective sleep efficacy; Emax logistic model related C9hr to somnolence incidence (EC50 0.60 uM); supported conclusion that high dose provided no added efficacy benefit.

structural_features: Linear one-compartment model with first-order absorption; PD component links PK to neopterin biomarker; anti-PEG/anti-IFN antibody status evaluated as covariate
notes: Built from Phase 3 study 105MS301 (1512 patients) plus healthy-volunteer study; BMI significant covariate on CL; simulation of severe renal impairment vs normal used to assess dose-adjustment need; concentration-efficacy explicitly not formally explored.

structural_features: First-order absorption; covariates: age/weight/sex on Vc/F, sex on CL/F, CYP2D6 phenotype (PM/IM/UM) on CL/F, co-administered CYP2D6/3A4 inhibitors on CL/F; bioavailability scaling factor for MDD phase 2/3 vs phase 1
notes: n=2357 evaluable subjects from 12 phase 2/3 trials; simulations of CYP2D6/CYP3A4 inhibitor scenarios across EM/PM phenotypes supported dose-adjustment recommendations.

structural_features: Simple Emax model (efficacy, PANSS); logistic regression (safety, akathisia)
notes: MDD n=1848: flat exposure-response; schizophrenia n=1719: Emax exposure-response (Emax 4.37 points, EC50 10.1 ng/mL); FDA's independent logistic-regression safety analysis found significant exposure-dependent increase in akathisia.

structural_features: Multi-analyte kinetics for parent (CAR) plus active metabolites DCAR and DDCAR (DDCAR terminal half-life 2-3 weeks); resubmission revised DDCAR elimination model; sponsor's "effective half-life" simplification rejected by reviewer
notes: Resubmission review of updated popPK analysis (new study A002-A11); ~90% exposure decline within 1 week (CAR/DCAR) vs 3-4 weeks (total cariprazine/DDCAR) post last dose.

structural_features: Not applicable
pk_exposure_metric: Cave (time-weighted, individual predictions from popPK model)
notes: Schizophrenia + bipolar mania pooled studies; PANSS/YMRS improvement increased with Cave; model-predicted AE probability rose sharply above 4.5-6mg (e.g. akathisia 3% placebo to 23% at 12mg).

structural_features: PK bridge via simultaneous popPK fit of oral Abilify Tablet + IM aripiprazole lauroxil data (relative bioavailability of IM product = 58% vs oral); simulations of steady-state profiles for 2 unstudied dosing regimens, treatment-initiation supplementation, missed-dose re-initiation, dose-dumping risk
notes: Data from 4 Phase 1 + 1 Phase 3 study; simulations supported approval of 2 never-directly-studied dosing regimens (662mg monthly, 882mg q6wk).

structural_features: Minimal PBPK distribution model (Vd,ss 2.7 L/kg, Ka 1.5/h, hepatic CLint via retrograde method, fm,CYP3A4=0.45, fm,CYP2D6=0.41); extended with skin/dermal absorption sub-model to mimic IM depot release since Simcyp cannot natively simulate IM injection
notes: Verified against 3 sponsor clinical PK/DDI studies plus independent FDA carbamazepine-interaction simulation; confirmed CYP3A4/CYP2D6 dose-adjustment recommendations extrapolated from reference product Abilify Maintena.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: n=126 subjects; nonparametric superposition of single-dose Day-1 oral Abilify data independently predicted steady-state Cmin/Cmax, corroborating sponsor's PK-bridge exposure window.

structural_features: First-order absorption and elimination; allometric scaling of body weight on CL and V; automated covariate search flagged CBZ/PHT/PB/VPA/race/sex/age/dose, but only enzyme-inducing AEDs (CBZ, PHT, PB) met the 20% clinical-significance threshold on CL
notes: Sponsor's popPK model (report CL0028) pooled 5820 samples from 1248 epilepsy patients; co-administration with enzyme-inducing AEDs increased CL 24-35% but all changes <30%, supporting no dose adjustment.

structural_features: Mixture model separating responder vs. placebo-like subpopulations; negative binomial distribution for daily seizure counts; Box-Cox-transformed baseline seizure rate; Emax model linking simulated daily Cav to seizure rate
notes: Sponsor's model-based exposure-response analysis (CL0027): 251,278 seizure counts from 1912 subjects; EC50 ~0.572 mg/L; ~29% classified as responders; concomitant levetiracetam reduced responder fraction to near 0%; supported plateauing dose-response by 100-200 mg/day.

structural_features: Not applicable
fitting_method_software: R (Emax model fit to popPK-predicted exposures)
notes: FDA reviewer's independent exposure-response analysis in 1533 subjects from 3 pivotal Phase 3 trials, stratified by concomitant levetiracetam use; confirmed sponsor's flat/plateau efficacy exposure-response relationship.

structural_features: Sequential 3-stage popPK build: Stage 1 (healthy subjects, 3 formulations) established structural model with allometric scaling and formulation/food effects; Stage 2 (8 PD patients w/o psychosis) confirmed structural model; Stage 3 (PD patients with psychosis, trough-only sampling) fixed absorption parameters and tested covariates (height, lean body mass, age, sex, CrCL) on apparent clearance
notes: Final Stage-3 model retained height (+CL) and age (-CL) as covariates; competing CrCL model rejected as "physiologically unrealistic"; renal function, gender not required for dose adjustment.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Sponsor examined popPK-derived mean plasma concentration vs. SAPS-PD change (flat) and vs. 4 AEs (no relationship); FDA reviewer's supplemental analysis excluding non-North-American patients confirmed the exposure-response relationship supporting the approved 34 mg dose.

structural_features: Two-compartment model, first-order SC absorption (ka constrained > ke) and elimination; elimination via proteolysis plus target-mediated elimination (qualitatively described, not a formal TMDD sub-model); absorption lag time improved fit
notes: PopPK model built from 1670 healthy volunteers/MS patients, 17,139 samples; body weight (CL, V2) and neutralizing-antibody-positive status (+19% CL) were the only clinically significant covariates; bootstrap-validated.

structural_features: Negative binomial model for relapse/T2-lesion/Gd-lesion counts with an Emax function linking steady-state AUC to efficacy; logistic regression linking AUCss to safety endpoints
notes: Combined 2 Phase 2 + 2 Phase 3 RRMS trials; used EBE-derived AUCss (sparse trough-only sampling precluded reliable Cmax); found no meaningful ARR difference across weight-based AUCss quartiles.

structural_features: Linear one-compartment model, first-order absorption and elimination (NONMEM Model 136); CL/F and Vd/F increase allometrically with body weight; also used post hoc to assess PPI co-administration as absorption covariate
notes: Pooled concentrations from 446/452/273 PD patients across 3 pivotal Phase 3 trials (016, MOTION, SETTLE); age had small effect on CL/F; race gave small bioavailability difference; gender, renal function, levodopa exposure did not affect PK.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Sponsor's exposure-efficacy analysis (Studies 016, SETTLE) related Css,avg to "ON time" motor-fluctuation improvement; found no meaningful difference between 50 mg and 100 mg doses.

structural_features: Two-compartment model with constant clearance component (CLinf) plus time-dependent declining clearance component, CLt = CLT0*exp(-kdes*TIME); separate CLT0 for re-treatment arm after dosing interruption
notes: RMS popPK model built from 4901 samples/941 patients (Phase 2/3); covariates retained: body weight (CLinf, CLT0, V1, V2, Q), baseline B-cell count (CLinf), sex (V1); typical CL 0.173 L/day, Vss 5.6 L, t1/2 26.8 days.

structural_features: Same structural/covariate model as the RMS analysis, externally evaluated (parameters fixed, not re-estimated) against an independent PPMS dataset
notes: RMS-derived popPK model externally validated using 4340 samples from 482 PPMS patients; goodness-of-fit/VPC confirmed good predictive performance, supporting that MS disease stage does not affect ocrelizumab disposition.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: FDA reviewer's independent multivariate Cox regression relating early ocrelizumab exposure (Cavg1) to time to 12-week confirmed disability progression, pooling RMS studies and adjusting for additional risk factors.

structural_features: One central plus three peripheral compartments; nonlinear (saturable) clearance and distribution; autoinduction of clearance reaching steady-state by ~10 days; transit-compartment oral absorption
notes: 280 healthy subjects (91% female), 9008 samples across 12 Phase 1 studies (40-960 mg QD, 40-720 mg BID); absolute bioavailability 94%; Japanese subjects showed 1.5-2.5-fold higher exposures than non-Japanese, partly from lower body weight; characterized PK and OATP1B1/UGT1A1 genetic covariates across the dose range.

structural_features: Linear elimination and absorption with an absorption lag time; steady-state focused model (no autoinduction/nonlinearity terms)
notes: 2888 observations from 399 HSCT-transplant subjects across 5 studies; lower bioavailability/slower absorption in HSCT recipients vs. healthy volunteers; bioavailability rose from 35% to 85% with cyclosporine coadministration; ~50% higher exposures in Asian subjects (smaller peripheral Vd); derived individual exposures used in the Phase 3 exposure-response analyses.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Phase 3 HSCT CMV-prophylaxis population; AUC/Cmin not associated with CMV infection risk or most AEs; exploratory analysis in an intensive-PK subset (n=75, ≥1 IV dose) found Cmax associated with cardiac disorders, arrhythmias, and renal failure; flat E-R supported the studied regimen and cardiac/renal labeling.

structural_features: Full PBPK with permeability-limited liver compartment; first-order absorption; hepatic uptake via OATP1B1; elimination via biliary clearance plus UGT1A1/CYP3A4 metabolism; fitted ka, Kp scalar, biliary CLint, OATP1B1 Jmax/Km, fu,IW
notes: Qualified against IV/PO single/multiple-dose data in white/Japanese healthy volunteers and HSCT recipients (target simulated/observed AUC ratio 0.5-2); used in lieu of dedicated clinical studies to predict effects on CYP3A (midazolam, AUC ratio ~2.5) and CYP2C8 (repaglinide) substrates and to predict hepatic-impairment PK at low vs. high doses.

structural_features: One-compartment model with parallel Michaelis-Menten (saturable) and first-order elimination, consistent with target-mediated drug disposition at higher doses; M3 method used for BLQ data
notes: FDA reviewer's independent model pooling Phase 1a/1b/2a/2b data, built after determining the Applicant's model (which excluded concentrations <1 µg/mL) was unsuitable for E-R or dose extrapolation; body weight was a significant covariate on CL; used to simulate Ctrough at Week 24 for the approved 2000 mg Q4W / 800 mg Q2W regimens.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: 107 Phase 2b subjects; lowest Ctrough quartile (0.1-0.3 µg/mL) had markedly lower Week-24 virologic response (15%) vs. higher quartiles (38-43%); logistic regression of logit(response) on log(Ctrough) was significant (p=0.026), supporting a target trough concentration around 0.5 µg/mL.

structural_features: Three-compartment model with two-transit-compartment first-order absorption and first-order elimination; sex and BMI covariates on inter-compartmental clearance/peripheral volumes; high-fat meal increased relative bioavailability ~1.4-fold and mean transit time ~2.1-fold
fitting_method_software: NONMEM v7.3 (with PsN); post-processing in R
notes: 2827 concentrations from 210 subjects across 3 Phase 1 studies and 1 Phase 2 study in Onchocerca volvulus patients, updated with a QT study; ~11% of samples were BLQ and excluded (FDA reviewer separately assessed this exclusion's impact); model-derived AUC supported dose selection via linked PK/PD analysis.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Phase 2 data (n=98 with PK) showed increasing AUC associated with decreased skin microfilariae probability and increased sustained response at Months 6/12, plateauing near 8 mg; Applicant did not perform exposure-safety analysis; FDA reviewer's independent Phase 3 analysis found no clear dose-exposure difference for mean mf reduction but favored 8 mg for proportion with undetectable mf at Month 12.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Single-dose NCA of paired plasma/breast-milk concentrations in lactating women given 8 mg moxidectin; computed milk:plasma AUC ratio and estimated relative infant dose (normalized to 5 kg infant) to inform breastfeeding labeling.

structural_features: Zero-order IV infusion input with first-order elimination; BSA-normalized creatinine clearance as a time-varying covariate on CL via sigmoidal Hill function; CRRT clearance from patient-specific ultrafiltrate/dialysate flow rates and estimated sieving coefficient; covariates on Vc, CLd1, Vp1, CLd2, Vp2 (BSA, infection type, age, height, body weight, vasopressors)
notes: 564 subjects, 4990 plasma records pooled from 4 Phase 1, 1 Phase 2, 2 Phase 3 studies (incl. dedicated renal-impairment PK study); used to simulate exposures/Cmin across CLcr categories, including CRRT patients, supporting a renal-function-based dosing nomogram.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Applicant did not perform a formal efficacy E-R analysis; FDA reviewer's post-hoc analysis (184-189 cUTI patients, Study ACHN-490-009) found no relationship between AUC0-24h or AUC/MIC and composite/microbiological response at Day 5 or test-of-cure; bacteremia subgroup (n=25) too small for formal analysis.

structural_features: Not applicable
estimation_technique: Linear mixed-effects regression (repeated measures, random intercept)
notes: Applicant analysis pooling cUTI/AP data (Studies ACHN-490-002/-009, incl. zero-exposure comparator arms) modeled serum creatinine clearance vs. preceding plazomicin AUC/Cmin windows plus nephrotoxic co-meds/vasopressor use; found a significant exposure-nephrotoxicity relationship in patients with baseline CLcr 30-90 mL/min, informing renal dosing/monitoring recommendations.

structural_features: One-compartment model with first-order absorption (lag time) and first-order elimination for bictegravir (BIC)
notes: Pooled BIC PK data from 8 Phase 1/3 studies in healthy volunteers and HIV-1-infected (treatment-naive and switch) subjects; body weight (CL, Vc), health status (Vc), and PPI use (Ka) were statistically but not clinically significant covariates (<20% exposure change at extremes); supported the single 50 mg BIC dose in the FDC.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: 584-634 ART-naive HIV-infected subjects, Phase 3 Studies 1489/1490; no relationship between BIC exposure quartiles and virologic response (>89% response across all quartiles at Week 48); no exposure-safety relationship for diarrhea/headache (p=0.913 for headache); supported 50 mg BIC dose without exposure-based adjustment.

structural_features: Zero-order absorption, first-order elimination; rabbit PK model
notes: 82 NZW rabbits, 1430 PK samples across healthy and Rabbitpox-infected animals; supported the interspecies PK bridge used to justify the human dose under the Animal Rule (no human efficacy studies possible for smallpox).

structural_features: Zero-order absorption, first-order elimination; cynomolgus monkey PK model used to derive post-hoc exposure estimates for cross-species exposure matching
notes: 60 monkeys (healthy + MPXV/Rabbitpox-infected), 1558 plasma concentrations; model used to simulate uninfected vs infected exposure and anchor the "3 mg/kg fully effective monkey dose" used for human exposure matching.

structural_features: Zero-order absorption, first-order elimination; allometric scaling of CL/F and V2/F by body weight (exponent fixed at 0.75, sensitivity analysis estimated 0.898); food effect on Ka and F1; study effect on F1
fitting_method_software: Phoenix NLME (applicant); NONMEM v7.3 + R (FDA reviewer re-optimization)
analysis_goal: Dose/regimen selection; Animal-to-human bridging (Animal Rule); Extrapolation to new population
estimation_technique: Empirical Bayes estimation; Allometric scaling; Simulation
notes: 88 healthy human subjects, 1511 concentrations (applicant model); FDA reviewer added 2 more studies (100 mg and 600 mg BID fed/fasted data) and refit in NONMEM; used to simulate exposures in >150 kg patients and infected vs uninfected/fed vs fasted humans to support 600 mg BID pediatric and high-body-weight dosing.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Dose/survival relationship in MPXV-infected monkeys; ROC analysis identified 3 mg/kg QD as the minimal fully-effective dose (94.1% sensitivity/98.4% specificity vs 10 mg/kg), the key efficacy anchor for Animal Rule approval.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Study SIGA-246-015, 78 healthy subjects; tecovirimat increased omeprazole (CYP2C19) AUC 73-91% and decreased midazolam (CYP3A4) AUC 31-39%, with smaller effects on repaglinide (CYP2C8); no effect on flurbiprofen/bupropion.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Study SIGA-246-013; 4 matched cohorts (normal/mild/moderate/severe hepatic impairment); hepatic impairment had small impact on tecovirimat exposure but up to 2-fold increase in metabolite (M4/M5/TFMBA) AUC in severe impairment, judged not clinically significant.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Independent FDA E-R analysis of Study TAF112582 Part 1 (dose-ranging, N=54-57/arm); logistic regression of AUC vs 6-month recurrence-free rate and a time-to-event analysis (AUC bins) both showed response plateaus at AUC >=66 ug*h/mL, supporting the 300 mg single-dose regimen (median AUC 104 ug*h/mL).

structural_features: First-order oral / IV zero-order input; allometric scaling on CL and volume parameters; covariates for age (CL), sex (V2), renal impairment/ESRD (CL), hepatic impairment/Child-Pugh (CL), food and formulation (F1, Ka, Tlag), infection type (cIAI/cUTI)
analysis_goal: Extrapolation to new population; Regulatory-basis support
notes: Applicant model (TETR-PCS-100, pooled Phase 1-3 data) combined with FDA reviewer's expanded "Uni" model (736 vs 979 individuals, 6775 vs 7627 observations) adding hepatic-impairment covariate from Phase 2/3 patients outside the dedicated HI study; confirmed renal/hepatic impairment change AUC <10% (renal) but moderate/severe hepatic impairment reduces CL up to ~22%.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Phase 2/3 cIAI patients; clinical/microbiological response vs free-drug AUC:MIC analyzed continuously and by tertiles; FDA reviewer's full-covariate logistic model found no significant exposure-response relationship (flat) at approved doses (1 mg/kg q12h; 1.5 mg/kg q24h).

structural_features: Same structural popPK model above used to simulate CYP3A-inducer (rifampin) drug interaction scenarios
notes: Rifampin (strong CYP3A inducer) decreased observed eravacycline AUC0-inf 35% in a dedicated DDI study; population-PK-based simulations of 4 dosing scenarios showed only 1.5 mg/kg q12h kept AUC within 15% of reference exposure with a strong inducer, driving the label's inducer dose-adjustment recommendation.

structural_features: First-order absorption; two relative-bioavailability terms for <30 mg and >120 mg dose ranges (less-than-dose-proportional PK); automated stepwise covariate model building; covariates of body weight and HIV-1 infection status on V/F, age on CL/F
analysis_goal: Extrapolation to new population; Regulatory-basis support
estimation_technique: Empirical Bayes estimation; Covariate modeling; Bootstrap
notes: 20 Phase 1 + 1 Phase 2b + 2 Phase 3 trials; 341 healthy + 959 HIV-1-infected subjects; bootstrap and VPC-validated; found no clinically meaningful covariate effects (<25% change) including limited/inconclusive assessment of strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (n=8).

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Phase 2b trial P007; logistic regression of HIV-1 RNA response/virologic failure vs DOR AUC0-24 and C24 quartiles was flat (no significant slope) across the 25-200 mg dose range; separate linear D-R models for lipid changes (LDL, non-HDL) found dose was not a significant predictor after adjusting for age/baseline viral load/baseline lipids.

structural_features: PBPK absorption from single-dose oral data; distribution as 1-compartment (Vss from IV data); elimination via CYP3A4-mediated metabolism; separate M9 metabolite PBPK sub-model
notes: Verified against ketoconazole, rifampin, and efavirenz DDI studies (predictions within 10-30% of observed, rifampin under-predicted 2-fold before Indmax sensitivity analysis); used to justify contraindication with strong CYP3A inducers, dose-frequency increase with rifabutin, and 3-4 week rifampin/2-3 week rifabutin washout periods before starting doravirine.

structural_features: Zero-order IV input or first-order oral absorption with transit compartments (delayed absorption); epithelial lining fluid (ELF) modeled as sub-compartment of peripheral compartment 1; covariates of formulation/dose and food timing/type on bioavailability, sex on absorption
analysis_goal: Dose/regimen selection; Extrapolation to new population
estimation_technique: Covariate modeling (stepwise forward selection); Prediction-corrected VPC; External validation
notes: 613 subjects, 11331 plasma + 41 BAL(ELF) samples across Phase 1/1b/3 studies; externally validated against Phase 3 ABSSSI study; serum creatinine was not a significant covariate, supporting no dose adjustment in renal impairment; ELF:free-plasma penetration ratio of 2.06.

structural_features: Not applicable
estimation_technique: Logistic regression; Monte Carlo simulation (probability of target attainment)
pk_exposure_metric: AUC:MIC ratio (free-drug plasma and total-drug ELF)
notes: ABSSSI ME population (n=182/128 S. aureus subset); logistic PK-PD showed clinical success at ECR rose from ~80% (AUC:MIC~0) to 90% (AUC:MIC=14.7); population-PK-derived ELF/plasma AUC:MIC used in Monte Carlo PTA simulations to support susceptibility breakpoints (e.g., 0.12 ug/mL S. aureus, 0.5-1 ug/mL H. influenzae/S. pneumoniae); CABP exposure-response not feasible due to only 10-11 evaluable patients with PK data.

structural_features: First-order absorption with absorption lag time; covariates of body weight (CL/F, Vc/F, Q/F, Vp/F), race/non-Asian (CL/F, Vc/F), ALT (CL/F), gender (Ka), food (F)
notes: 8310 plasma concentrations from Phase 1/2/3 studies (single doses 6-80 mg) in healthy subjects and influenza patients; non-Asians had 72%/36% higher CL/F and Vc/F than Asians; food within 2h of dosing decreased exposure 13.1%; moderate hepatic impairment tested as covariate on Vp/F.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: FDA reviewer re-analyzed Phase 2/3 data after excluding placebo (which the applicant had improperly included); linear regression of C24 vs time-to-alleviation-of-symptoms and vs Day-2 virus titer change found no clear exposure-response relationship for either Type A or Type B influenza, even when stratified by ethnicity (though non-Asian Type B subgroup was small).

structural_features: Full PBPK model with first-order oral absorption for parent TCBZ; minimal PBPK models for active metabolites TCBZ-SO (sulfoxide, predominant in plasma) and TCBZ-SO2 (sulfone); sequential oxidative elimination via CYP1A2/2C9/2C19/2D6/3A
notes: Model built from in vitro CYP fm data and single-dose human PK (10 mg/kg fed); FDA judged the model inadequate to predict Egaten as a DDI victim (unverified fm inputs) but adequate as a perpetrator, predicting mild-to-moderate (<2.5-fold) increases in exposure of CYP1A2/2C8/2C9/2D6/3A substrates and a larger increase for CYP2C19 substrates (e.g., omeprazole); CYP2B6 (bupropion) prediction was inconclusive due to a known Simcyp bupropion-model discrepancy.

structural_features: Separate parallel 2-compartment models for imipenem and relebactam; linear clearance from central compartment, inter-compartmental clearance Q, covariance between CL and V1
fitting_method_software: NONMEM v7.3.0; PsN v4.7.0; R v3.5.1 (post-processing)
estimation_technique: Stepwise covariate modeling; Empirical Bayes estimation
notes: Built on 855 subjects pooled from 7 phase 1 studies plus cUTI/cIAI/HABP-VABP patient studies (4454/4814 imipenem/relebactam concentrations); CrCL and weight were key clearance covariates, used to derive the CrCL-banded dose adjustments. FDA reviewer re-fit the model fixing allometric exponents (0.75 on CL/Q, 1 on V) due to weight-CrCL collinearity and obtained comparable estimates, endorsing use of the model's renal-impairment dosing simulations.

structural_features: Stochastic inhibitory Imax model relating in vitro relebactam concentration to potentiated imipenem MIC; deterministic Hill/Imax models per bacterial strain relating exposure metrics (AUC0-24, Cmax, %fT>C) to 24-hr bacterial kill in a murine neutropenic thigh-infection model
notes: In vitro checkerboard and in vivo murine thigh (P. aeruginosa/K. pneumoniae) experiments identified AUC/MIC as the PK/PD driver for relebactam; a conservative pooled target (5.2 fAUC0-24/MIC for P. aeruginosa, 25.2 for K. pneumoniae) fed a joint PTA simulation (with the population PK model) supporting the REL 250 mg dose; FDA judged the resulting PTA insufficient to support the Applicant's proposed susceptibility breakpoints.

structural_features: 1-compartment disposition with mean-transit-time/transit-compartment absorption (MTT + Ka); dose- and fasted-state dependent bioavailability; time-dependent (autoinduction-like) clearance increase from week 6 in Nix-TB; DDI covariates for efavirenz and lopinavir/ritonavir on clearance
estimation_technique: Stepwise covariate modeling; Empirical Bayes estimation
notes: Built from 17,725 observations in 1,054 subjects (healthy, DS-TB, MDR-TB, XDR-TB) pooled across 6 phase 1, 6 phase 2, and 2 phase 3 studies (incl. pivotal Nix-TB); covariate simulations (fed/fasted, disease state, HIV, concomitant antituberculars) supported the fed-state 200 mg once-daily label dose.

structural_features: Exponential/Emax-type exposure-response functions relating model-predicted Cavg to early bactericidal activity endpoints (EBACFU0-14, EBATTP0-14) for pretomanid alone and BPaZ/BPaMZ/PaMZ combinations; Cox proportional hazards model for time to sputum culture conversion
estimation_technique: Nonlinear regression; Cox proportional hazards regression
notes: Pooled phase 2 EBA data (115 obs pretomanid-alone, 268 obs combination regimens) showed the dose-response plateaus by ~200 mg (>99% of maximal effect); supported fed-state dosing and combination-regimen selection. Multivariate Cox regression suggested BPaMZ/BPaZ achieved faster sputum conversion than BPaL, though confounded by differing TB-resistance profiles across arms.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Pooled phase 2/3 data found no significant exposure relationship for ALT/AST/bilirubin or reproductive hormones (one ALP association at week 12-26 had opposite-direction regimen effects). Nix-TB-only logistic regression (n=98, using population-PK-model-predicted Cavg) found significant associations between higher exposure and grade 3/4 adverse events, vomiting, and GI symptoms, informing safety labeling.

structural_features: Linear clearance from central to 2 peripheral compartments; nonlinear (Emax-based) plasma protein binding; zero-order IV infusion; biphasic (immediate + transit-compartment delayed) oral absorption; first-order distribution into/out of epithelial lining fluid (ELF)
fitting_method_software: Not stated (Applicant); NONMEM 7 used by FDA reviewer for verification
estimation_technique: Stepwise covariate modeling; Empirical Bayes estimation
notes: Built from 6,205 records in 849 subjects pooled across 4 phase 1 (incl. hepatic-impairment, renal-impairment, rifampin-DDI studies), 1 phase 2, and 2 phase 3 (CABP) studies; albumin and body size were significant covariates. Model-derived ELF exposure predictions had large uncertainty per FDA.

structural_features: Perfusion rate-limited whole-body PBPK model (permeability rate-limited liver/kidney) for lefamulin as victim/perpetrator of CYP3A/P-gp/BCRP/OATP1B1/1B3/MATE1/OCT1-mediated interactions
notes: Simulated DDIs with fluconazole, fluvoxamine, efavirenz, ketoconazole, rifampicin, midazolam, zolpidem, repaglinide, rosuvastatin, digoxin, ethinyl estradiol, and metformin; FDA concluded the perfusion-rate-limited model was not adequate to fully characterize enzyme/transporter-mediated DDI risk, limiting labeling claims.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: In 92 CABP subjects (Studies 3101/3102) with evaluable pathogen/MIC data, univariate/multivariate logistic regression found no significant relationship between free-drug plasma AUC:MIC and response because nearly all subjects exceeded the nonclinical PK/PD target plateau; supported adequacy of 150 mg IV / 600 mg oral q12h dosing.

structural_features: Linear 3-compartment disposition (central + 2 peripheral, Q2/Q3); time-varying creatinine clearance and infection site as covariates on clearance/volume
notes: Built from 2,934 samples in 406 subjects across 2 phase 1, 1 phase 2 (APEKS-cUTI), and 1 phase 3 (CREDIBLE-CR) study; time-varying CrCL outperformed baseline CrCL and directly supported the CrCL-banded dose regimen (incl. reduced ESRD/CRRT dose), confirmed adequate by post hoc AUC in hemodialysis/CVVH/CVVHDF patients.

structural_features: PK/PD index (%fT>MIC) identified via dose-fractionation in a neutropenic murine thigh-infection model (P. aeruginosa) fit with a sigmoid Emax model; Monte Carlo simulation combining the murine-derived 75% fT>MIC target with a virtual patient population (log-normal weight, modeled CrCL) from the human population PK model
notes: PTA >90% up to MIC 4 ug/mL across renal-function-adjusted regimens in both APEKS-cUTI and CREDIBLE-CR; FDA's independent bootstrap-resampled virtual population confirmed >90% PTA at 75% fT>MIC but not 100%. Exploratory AUC-quintile analysis of the composite clinical/microbiological endpoint in APEKS-cUTI (n=171) showed no exposure-response relationship at exposures achieved.

structural_features: 1-compartment disposition for dihydroartemisinin (active metabolite) with allometric weight scaling on clearance/volume and a sigmoidal age/maturation sub-model for enzymatic clearance (analogous to UGT-mediated morphine clearance maturation)
notes: Applicant relied on 2 published literature population PK models (Hendriksen 2013, n=70 children; Zaloumis 2014, pooled n=266 children/adults across 6 studies) rather than an applicant-generated model; FDA pharmacometrics reviewed and endorsed. Simulations supported a single fixed 2.4 mg/kg IV dose across all weights/ages including neonates <6 kg, predicting comparable-or-greater DHA exposure in the smallest patients, though no exposure-safety relationship could be evaluated for that higher-exposure subgroup.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: FDA QT-IRT performed a concentration-QTc exposure-response analysis plus categorical analysis of ECG data from Studies 1128/1142; concluded no significant QTc-prolongation effect of IV artesunate up to 8 mg/kg, supporting cardiac electrophysiology labeling language.

structural_features: Two-compartment model with dual zero-order and first-order absorption and first-order elimination; CYP3A inducers and CYP3A inhibitors as covariates on apparent oral clearance (CL/F); allometrically scaled body weight on CL/F, V2/F, Q/F, V3/F
notes: Pooled Phase 1-3 plasma temsavir data from healthy adults and HIV-1 patients; CYP3A inducers increased CL/F by 41% (Ctau -53%, AUC -29%); CYP3A inhibitors decreased CL/F by 28% (Ctau +79%, AUC +39%); sex, race, age, formulation, renal/hepatic labs had no effect on PK; supported DDI management labeling without dose adjustment.

structural_features: Emax inhibitory model linking Day 8 HIV-1 RNA decline to post-hoc TMR Ctau, with baseline HIV-1 RNA and CD4+ T-cell count (>20 vs <20 cells/mm3) as covariates
notes: n=258 (193 FTR 600 mg BID, 65 placebo) from Phase 3 BRIGHTE Randomized Cohort; relationship between Ctau and Day 8 virologic response was shallow and highly variable (EC50 64.3 ng/mL, large residual error); no exposure-safety relationship found for Cavg/Cmax vs. rash, liver enzymes, CPK, SCr, QTcF; no dose adjustment recommended, including for patients with high baseline EC50.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Maximal-use trials (Ha03-003/004) compared systemic absorption of topical abametapir lotion 0.74% in pediatric subjects (6 months-<17 years) vs. adults; pediatric Cmax and AUC0-8h were roughly 1.8-2.2-fold higher than adult values (Cmax 73 vs 41 ng/mL; AUC0-8h 264 vs 121 ng*h/mL); static in vitro DDI risk assessment (unbound Cmax/Ki and Cmax/IC50 ratios <0.1-0.24) supported low risk of clinically relevant CYP- or transporter-mediated interactions; no dose adjustment recommended.

structural_features: One-compartment model with first-order absorption (ka) and first-order elimination; fixed allometric weight exponents on CL and V; categorical age effect (<2 years vs >=2 years) as multiplier on clearance; built on pediatric-only data after an adult-derived model failed to describe pediatric troughs/Cmax
notes: Applicant's pediatric Model 620 (Study BP-16027, Chagas disease) had high eta-shrinkage (45%/33% on CL/V); FDA pharmacometrics reviewers refit in untransformed domain as Model 625d, reducing shrinkage to 23%/15%; weight and age(<2y) retained as significant covariates by backward elimination (OFV criteria); model-derived AUC used to support subsequent exposure-response analyses since Cmax was misspecified for some formulations.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: n=111 pediatric patients with paired PK/serology/safety data; model-predicted steady-state AUC and age were significant predictors (p<0.05) of serological response (recombinant ELISA assay) as a surrogate efficacy marker; AUC was also a significant predictor of abdominal pain, particularly in patients >=12 years (only 6 AE events, interpreted cautiously); AUC preferred over Cmax due to PK model misspecification of peak concentrations.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: NCA-derived mean PK parameters (Cmax, AUCinf, clearance, volume of distribution, half-life) for the three component mAbs compared between uninfected healthy adults and EBOV-infected/uninfected rhesus macaques from lethal-challenge studies; infected-NHP PK suggested target-mediated (nonlinear, dose-dependent) clearance most apparent at high viral loads and lower REGN-EB3 doses; human 150 mg/kg exposures exceeded the NHP 150 mg/kg exposures, supporting the single 150 mg/kg dose used in the PALM trial; PK was evaluated only in healthy adults 21-60y (not pediatric/geriatric/obese), yet the approved indication includes pediatric patients including neonates; PK not measured in infected humans, precluding exposure-response assessment.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: NCA-derived PK parameters in healthy uninfected adults after a single 50 mg/kg IV dose (AUC0-last ~29,288 ug*day/mL, Cmax ~1932 ug/mL, Vd 74.5 mL/kg, CL 1.66 mL/day/kg, t1/2 31.6 days); Cmax was dose-proportional (5-50 mg/kg) while AUC increased slightly more than dose-proportionally; exposure matching vs. uninfected NHPs (1.4-fold higher human exposure at matched 50 mg/kg dose) supported the single 50 mg/kg dose used under the Animal Rule pathway in the PALM trial/MEURI EAP; PK in infected humans not evaluated, precluding exposure-response assessment; a future combined compartmental/noncompartmental PK sub-study in an expanded-access protocol was planned but not yet conducted.

structural_features: Full PBPK distribution model for parent remdesivir; minimal PBPK (Kp-scalar) distribution models for metabolites GS-704277 and GS-441524; accounts for carboxylesterase (CES1)-mediated intracellular metabolism and age-dependent enzyme maturation
notes: PBPK simulations reasonably reproduced observed adult plasma PK of remdesivir and both metabolites; used to predict steady-state exposures in adolescents (12-<18 years, >=40 kg) under the adult dosing regimen (200 mg Day 1, 100 mg QD thereafter); predicted adolescent exposures were comparable to adults, supporting pediatric label extrapolation without a dedicated adolescent PK trial; reviewer flagged limitations regarding CES ontogeny data and noted the model should be optimized before use for DDI or other pediatric age-group predictions.

structural_features: Sequential parent-metabolite population PK model: RDV and GS-704277 each 2-compartment (central + 1 peripheral); active metabolite GS-441524 3-compartment (central + 2 peripheral); fixed allometric body-weight exponents retained on clearance/volume parameters across all three analytes (chosen over estimated exponents for extrapolation robustness)
notes: Built from 123 healthy adults (studies GS-US-399-1812/1954/5505; ~2967 samples/analyte, weight range 53-101 kg); stepwise covariate modeling retained fixed allometric weight scaling for all analytes; simulations projected adolescent (>=40 kg) exposures comparable to adults, consistent with the PBPK predictions; data were insufficient to evaluate renal impairment (cohort CrCL generally >87 mL/min).

structural_features: Not applicable
estimation_technique: Static mechanistic modeling (basic [I]/Ki and mechanistic AUCR equations)
notes: Using Day 1 (200 mg) and maintenance (100 mg) RDV Cmax, basic/mechanistic static equations predicted RDV as a potential inhibitor of CYP3A, UGT1A1, OATP1B1, OATP1B3, and MATE1 near Cmax, with predicted inhibition resolving within 2-4 hours post-dose; given short (<=10-day) treatment duration, the review team did not recommend additional human DDI trials but agreed to a postmarketing requirement for a rifampin interaction study.

structural_features: Two linked metabolite (alpha-HTBZ, beta-HTBZ) PK models built from Phase 1 data, updated with Phase 3 (First-HD) concentration data; used to compare exposure in HD patients vs healthy volunteers
notes: Population PK model (SD-809-CLN-078) for total (alpha+beta)-HTBZ compared simulated HD-patient exposure at 15 mg BID to observed healthy-volunteer exposure at the same dose; exposures were similar, supporting that dose selection was appropriate across populations.

structural_features: Nonparametric superposition principle applied to concentration-time data from dedicated DDI study (no compartmental/population model fit)
notes: FDA Pharmacometrics reviewer used nonparametric superposition on DDI study data (with strong CYP2D6 inhibitor paroxetine) to predict steady-state (alpha+beta)-HTBZ profiles at candidate doses, supporting the 18 mg BID (36 mg/day) dose cap for patients on strong CYP2D6 inhibitors or CYP2D6 poor metabolizers.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: TQT study found a statistically significant exposure-response relationship between total (alpha+beta)-HTBZ concentration and QTcF prolongation; flagged as a limitation since tested concentrations did not cover worst-case steady-state exposure.

structural_features: Not applicable
pk_exposure_metric: Not applicable (plasma concentration of active metabolite)
notes: Study 1304 (pivotal Phase 3, N=234 randomized, PK subset) related % change from baseline in Week 6 AIMS dyskinesia score to concentration of active metabolite; relationship did not plateau up to 80 mg/day, prompting a postmarketing commitment to study higher doses. NOTE: true ClinPharmR PDF 404s on FDA's site (confirmed via TOC.html metadata); this row is drawn from the Summary Review's clinical pharmacology synopsis, the best available primary source.

structural_features: Multi-phasic (3-compartment) disposition with combined Michaelis-Menten (nonlinear) plus linear elimination and a 24-hour fluctuation in maximum nonlinear elimination rate (Vmax); built to compare Japanese vs non-Japanese (US/EU) ALS-patient exposure
fitting_method_software: NONMEM v7 Level 3.0.16 (sponsor); NONMEM v7.3 (FDA reviewer verification)
notes: Pooled data from 5 Phase 1 studies, N=86 subjects, 1519 concentration records; race was significant covariate on peripheral volume, sex on CL/V2/V3; virtual population simulation (2,000 subjects) supported bridging Japanese-approved dose to US/EU trials.

structural_features: 2-compartment model with first-order absorption + absolute bioavailability (SC), linear clearance plus nonlinear target-mediated elimination pathway (turnover of unbound receptor, quasi-steady-state complex association/dissociation); allometric scaling (body weight) on CL and V2
notes: Final PopPK dataset: 9,759 quantifiable samples from 2,061 subjects; only body weight (via allometry) retained as covariate after testing age, eGFR, sex, race, population, injection site, anti-drug antibody status.

structural_features: Longitudinal logistic-regression PK/PD model: logit(probability of migraine day) as function of time-dependent baseline decline, time-dependent placebo effect, and sigmoidal Emax drug-effect term (Hill coefficient ~10.5, EC50 5.1 ug/mL) driven by PopPK-predicted daily serum concentrations
notes: Efficacy data from 3 episodic + 1 chronic migraine trial; EC50 approximated steady-state trough at the 70 mg dose; 97% of 140mg-dose subjects and 64% of 70mg-dose subjects exceeded EC50 within week 1, supporting rapid onset and the two approved monthly doses.

structural_features: Parent-metabolite model: 2-compartment CBD (zero-order absorption + lag time) linked to 1 compartment each for metabolites 7-OH-CBD and 7-COOH-CBD; allometric scaling on all clearance/volume terms; exponential IIV, additive+proportional residual error
notes: Healthy Volunteer model: n=45 subjects, 3,766 observations, Phase 1 study 1544 (SAD/MAD/food-effect).

structural_features: Same base structural model (2-compartment CBD + 2 metabolite compartments) applied separately to Dravet Syndrome (DS) and Lennox-Gastaut Syndrome (LGS) pediatric patients; apparent CL/V only (no bioavailability/Tlag); allometric scaling not implemented (estimated exponents converged toward zero)
notes: DS model: n=27 patients (ages 3.9-10.9y), 335 observations from Trial 1332; LGS model similarly structured; neither retained significant covariates after backward elimination.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: E-R analyses for efficacy/safety in LGS and DS patients (CBD AUC vs. time-to-first-seizure/seizure-responder status); utility judged limited by FDA reviewer because unrestricted meal timing/undocumented fasted-fed status made observed PK non-representative; no clear E-R relationship found in DS patients.

structural_features: PBPK model of CBD built from physicochemical/in vitro (HLM, hepatocyte, recombinant CYP) data to predict inhibition/induction of CYP2B6, CYP2C8, CYP2C9, CYP3A4, UGT1A9, UGT2B7 in adults and pediatric patients (2-17y)
analysis_goal: Drug-drug interaction (DDI) risk prediction; Extrapolation to new population
notes: FDA reviewer identified deficiencies: model did not include major circulating metabolites' contribution to DDI, was not verified against available dedicated clinical DDI studies (clobazam, stiripentol, valproate), and time-dependent CYP3A4 inhibition was incompletely incorporated - not accepted as fully adequate as submitted.

structural_features: Separate models for olanzapine and samidorphan; first-order absorption with lag time, linear elimination; covariates (weight, rifampin, smoking, hepatic/renal impairment, race, sex) on clearance, weight/age on volume, food effect on bioavailability
notes: PopPK models built from 10 studies (9 phase 1 + 1 phase 3) supported labeling for renal/hepatic impairment; ~10% higher clearance in Black vs non-Black subjects noted but not clinically actionable.

structural_features: PBPK model of samidorphan predicting effect of strong CYP3A4 inhibitor (itraconazole) and hepatic impairment on exposure
notes: PBPK predicted 1.3-/1.6-fold increase in samidorphan Cmax/AUC with itraconazole and ~2.1-/2.6-fold increase in severe hepatic impairment, concordant with clinical DDI/HI study data; supported no dose adjustment with CYP3A4 inhibitors.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: OCP identified positive exposure-efficacy relationships (CDR-SB, ADAS-Cog13, ADCS-ADL-MCI) and exposure-SUVR-clinical endpoint relationships across Studies 103, 301, 302; cited as key supportive evidence for the accelerated/standard approval recommendation despite Study 301 failing its primary endpoint; the statistical review disagreed that evidence was adequate. Note: best_url (StatR) had no PK signal; used SumR/MedR instead (ClinPharmR/IntegratedR/MultidisciplineR not posted for this BLA).

structural_features: Sequential zero-/first-order lag-time absorption, linear elimination from central compartment; covariates: formulation, dose, food, liver function, concomitant meds, body weight
notes: 11,763 observations from 1,356 patients; clearance 23.7% lower in migraine patients vs healthy volunteers; no clinically relevant covariate effects of age/renal function/sex/race/weight; supported renal-impairment dose recommendations.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Reviewer's zero-inflated Poisson model of migraine-day reduction found treatment effect comparable and independent of atogepant exposure across 10 mg QD-60 mg BID; supported lack of a clear dose-response, consistent with flexible dosing.

structural_features: PBPK model predicting CYP3A4 inhibitor/inducer and transporter (OATP1B1/1B3, P-gp, BCRP) DDI effects
notes: PBPK predicted fluconazole (moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor) +68%/+21% AUC/Cmax and cimetidine (weak) +8%/+5%; rifampin CYP3A4-induction-only effect AUC ratio 0.63; supported dose adjustment recommendations with strong/moderate CYP3A4 inducers, no adjustment for moderate/weak inhibitors or P-gp/BCRP inhibitors.

structural_features: Linear clearance PK model with covariates (body weight, eGFR with allometric scaling on clearance); linked PK/PD model for total IgG turnover to describe FcRn-mediated IgG reduction
notes: 4020 total IgG observations (Study 1704 N=167, Study 1705 N=125); body weight and eGFR were statistically significant covariates on clearance/volume but not clinically meaningful; model used to simulate missed/delayed dose scenarios and support dosing regimen; no CYP-mediated DDI studies needed (not CYP450 substrate).

structural_features: First-order absorption with lag time, nonlinear (Michaelis-Menten) elimination; allometric scaling of Vc/Km by lean body weight, Vp/Q by fat mass, Km by age
notes: 1898 subjects, 12,627 concentrations across 17 studies; age and body size covariates on Km with modest (-8% to +20%) exposure impact; sex/race not covariates.

structural_features: PBPK model predicting CYP3A inhibitor/inducer DDI effects
notes: PBPK predicted strong CYP3A inhibitors (itraconazole, ketoconazole) increase daridorexant AUC >5-fold and strong inducers (carbamazepine, rifampicin) decrease AUC <0.5-fold; supported contraindication/avoidance labeling with strong CYP3A modulators.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Graphical E-R analyses of WASO/LPS/IDSIQ/sTST vs morning-after PK sample showed inconsistent slopes across trials and dose levels (no clear E-R relationship), attributed to PK sample timing (~1 half-life post-dose) not capturing peak drug effect during sleep.

structural_features: PopPK model for phenylbutyrate (PB) and its active metabolite phenylacetate (PAA); TUDCA and its metabolites (UDCA, GUDCA) could NOT be modeled with PopPK approach and were characterized only by non-compartmental descriptive PK (food-effect study only)
notes: Some PK samples exceeded validated long-term stability duration (up to 967 vs 440 days); FDA required sensitivity re-analysis excluding flagged samples, which confirmed model robustness; PMRs issued for dedicated hepatic/renal impairment and CYP/transporter DDI studies (not yet conducted at approval).

structural_features: First-order elimination; covariates: weight and ADA on clearance, weight/sex/region on central volume of distribution
notes: 591 RMS subjects (75% of 7485-sample combined dataset incl. CLL/NHL); base model built on prior oncology-population model then extended to relapsing MS; no dose adjustment needed for weight/sex/mild renal or hepatic impairment (mAb, low renal/hepatic elimination).

structural_features: Zero-order input (IV infusion), first-order elimination; covariates: weight/albumin/sex/ADA on clearance, weight/sex on central volume, Japanese race on peripheral volume
notes: 9027 samples from 725 subjects (Studies 101, 104, 201 Core+OLE); none of the significant covariates were clinically meaningful (all within 80-125% reference interval); no dose adjustment needed.

structural_features: Linear disease-progression model (placebo arm) with added drug effect (linear function of Css,avg) on ADCOMS, CDR-SB, and ADAS-Cog14 decline slopes
notes: Drug-effect term (DESLOPE) was statistically significant (95% CI excluded zero) for all three efficacy endpoints; predicted dose-dependent reduction in cognitive/functional decline, supporting the accelerated/full approval efficacy case.

structural_features: Indirect response (turnover) models linking central-compartment lecanemab concentration to reduction in amyloid PET SUVR, increase in plasma Abeta42/40 ratio, and decrease in plasma p-tau181 formation rate
notes: Biomarker turnover models (indirect response) quantified target engagement across three fluid/imaging biomarkers; age affected Emax and APOE4 carrier status affected baseline SUVR; used as supportive mechanistic/surrogate-endpoint evidence for approval.

structural_features: Combined IV/intranasal/oral formulations; sequential zero- and first-order oral/IN absorption; allometric scaling
notes: 594 subjects, 10,819 evaluable concentrations across 10 phase 1 studies; no clinically significant effect of body weight, sex, race, ethnicity, or age; absolute bioavailability (~5%) determined via PPK.

structural_features: PBPK/DDI modeling of OATP1B3/NTCP transporter inhibition (rifampin, cyclosporine) on zavegepant disposition
notes: PBPK predicted rifampin (OATP1B3/NTCP inhibitor + CYP3A/P-gp inducer) 2.39-fold AUC increase; cyclosporine (dual OATP1B3/NTCP inhibitor) up to 1.58-fold; review team disagreed with applicant's proposed labeling and required avoidance with OATP1B3/NTCP inhibitors/inducers in severe renal impairment due to uncertainty in mechanism attribution and Ki verification.

structural_features: First-order absorption, linear elimination; separate residual error models for healthy vs RTT subjects; covariates: body weight/GFR/disease status (RTT, TBI) on clearance, age/FXS status on central volume, RTT/TBI on peripheral volume; food, diarrhea, and supratherapeutic-dose effects on bioavailability
notes: 455 subjects, 5709 records across 14 studies incl. RTT, FXS, and TBI populations; weight-banded dosing regimens simulated to target AUC0-12,ss 800-1200 ug*h/mL derived from the effective phase 2 dose; same model used to support extrapolation to ages 2-4 years via exposure-matching (Study 009).

structural_features: ACAT (intestinal absorption) + permeability-limited distribution PBPK model; used for renal impairment exposure prediction and CYP3A DDI prediction (midazolam as sensitive substrate)
fitting_method_software: GastroPlus v9.8 (PBPKPlus module); ADMET Predictor v9.5
notes: Model adequately described trofinetide plasma/urinary PK and predicted midazolam CYP3A DDI; however, the renal-impairment PBPK submission was judged inadequate (insufficient verification data) despite predicting clinically meaningful AUC increases with worsening renal function - a PMR was required instead.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Linear E-R models (264 subjects/1022 records, Studies RETT-002 and 003) showed higher trofinetide AUC predicted greater improvement in RSBQ, CGI-I, CSBS-DP-IT, and RTT-COMC scores; baseline body weight modified the RSBQ exposure-response slope; supported weight-banded dosing and provided supportive evidence of effectiveness.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Exposure-safety analysis found higher trofinetide AUC0-12 predictive of increased probability of diarrhea (0.71 at AUC 800 vs 0.89 at 1200 ug*h/mL) and Cmax predictive of vomiting probability; directly supported USPI dose-reduction/interruption guidance for diarrhea management.

structural_features: Two-compartment model for lumacaftor with zero-order input to absorption compartment, first-order absorption, absorption lag time; allometric scaling of CL/F and V on body weight; age effect on lumacaftor CL/F; Bayesian model with informative priors used to fit sparse Phase 3 data
notes: Combined Phase 1/2/3 data for lumacaftor and ivacaftor; bioavailability ~1.8x (lumacaftor)/~1.5x (ivacaftor) higher in healthy volunteers vs CF patients; CL/F 39%/131% of reference (70kg) for 20kg/100kg subjects; age effect modest, no dose adjustment needed.

structural_features: Individual predicted lumacaftor AUC0-24h (from popPK model) driving linear/Emax exposure-response model for change in ppFEV1; age effect on slope estimated for subjects >=24y
notes: Sponsor's model excluded ivacaftor's independent effect on ppFEV1 due to identifiability issues, judged uninterpretable by FDA since ivacaftor alone is known to increase ppFEV1.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: FDA's independent analysis of ivacaftor trough vs ppFEV1 (monotherapy n=104 vs combination n=341/342) found combination-therapy E-R curve shifted left despite lower ivacaftor exposure, suggesting lumacaftor reduces ivacaftor's EC50.
