structural_features: Population PK model (algebraic, translated to ODE system for cumulative AUC/Cavg); allometric scaling (exponent 1 on volume, 0.733 on clearance vs body weight); formulation strength (40 vs 100 mg/mL) as covariate on Ka/bioavailability; immunogenicity (ADA) evaluated as covariate
analysis_timing: Prospective/pre-specified (pre-specified covariate model); Post-hoc (exploratory covariate model)
pk_exposure_metric: Not applicable (activity, U/L, used as PK metric)
notes: 73 of 77 enrolled HPP patients (infantile/juvenile-onset) contributed PK data; renal/hepatic function and race not significant covariates; reviewer disagreed that youngest infants have lower exposure at same weight-based dose.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Small adult bridging study (n=6) comparing IV then SC dosing; absolute SC bioavailability 45.8-98.4%; apparent t1/2 longer after SC than IV, suggesting absorption-rate-limited elimination.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Individual Cavg and year-of-diagnosis used as predictors of overall survival in infantile-onset patients; HR 0.999 per unit Cavg increase (p=0.0041), confounded by natural-history comparator having Cavg=0 and only 4 events.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Exposure-response model (EC50=1620 U/L) fit per-individual for MPOMA-G gait score in 8 juvenile-onset patients; separate E-R analysis for linear growth found no apparent relationship with exposure.

structural_features: One-compartment model with central volume and clearance; linear elimination; body surface area (BSA) on CL as a step function distinguishing 3 mg/kg dose from lower doses
fitting_method_software: NONMEM v7 level 2.0 (Intel Fortran Compiler 14.0.0, Linux)
notes: Pooled analysis across Studies LAL-CL01/02/03; BSA the only significant covariate on CL; model unable to adequately characterize PK in infantile-onset LAL deficiency (<6 months); supported 1 mg/kg dosing across pediatric and adult age groups.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Graphical E-R analysis using cumulative AUC through Week 20 vs. %LDL-c change in late-onset disease; positive trend for primary and 5 secondary lipid endpoints; not feasible in infantile-onset disease due to small sample.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: PK from Studies 201/202/301/204 in DMD patients; sponsor did not conduct population PK or exposure-response modeling; in vitro-only DDI assessment concluded low potential via CYP1A2/2C9/2C19 inhibition, no in vivo DDI study conducted.

structural_features: Two CSF compartments linked to two plasma compartments; linear clearance rate constants; allometric scaling of body weight to V1/CLp, linear scaling to V2; unidirectional CSF-to-plasma transport tested against bidirectional
fitting_algorithm: FOCE with INTERACTION (Full Covariate Model approach)
notes: Pooled analysis (n=72); body weight the only significant covariate; median CSF terminal half-life 163 days; FDA reran the model and simulated (Berkeley Madonna) a simplified fixed 12mg dose for 0-3 month-olds.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Linear regression of partial CSF AUC vs. CHOP-INTEND/CMAP/SMN protein change; logistic regression vs. motor-milestone response in infants <7 months; higher exposure associated with greater efficacy, supporting 12mg over 6mg dose and loading doses.

structural_features: Minimal PBPK model (lumped tissue compartment plus liver/intestinal metabolism) for active metabolite 21-desDFZ; rapid esterase conversion of prodrug; first-order oral absorption; CYP3A4-mediated hepatic clearance; linear PK
fitting_algorithm: Not stated (sensitivity analysis, not NONMEM-style estimation)
notes: Built from adult clarithromycin/rifampin DDI data, verified against adult and pediatric (4-16y) virtual populations; predicted ~2-3 fold exposure increase with moderate/strong inhibitors, large decrease with inducers; supported 3-fold dose reduction with inhibitors and avoidance with inducers.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: CSF PK from Phase 1/2 dose-escalation (ICV administration); biphasic decline; less-than-dose-proportional increase 30-300mg partly driven by one outlier; no accumulation over repeated 300mg Q2W dosing. Proposed 300mg dose derived from allometric scaling of juvenile dachshund brain mass to human brain mass, not from this NCA.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Graphical E-R using mean NCA-derived CSF/plasma AUC vs. CLN2 motor score slope; no apparent exposure-efficacy relationship, limited by high intra-subject AUC variability and only 1 efficacy responder with PK data.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Pooled E-R analysis (doses 1-4 mg/kg QOW) relating Cmax/AUC0-t to % reduction in urinary/serum GAG biomarkers; positive E-R relationship for urinary CS/DS/total uGAG plateauing near Cmax ~15 ug/mL and AUC ~40 ug*hr/mL, supporting 4 mg/kg dose; no relationship for urinary HS or serum GAGs.

structural_features: Two-compartment model with parallel first-order/zero-order absorption for TEZ and M1-TEZ; body weight allometric exponent (0.75) fixed on clearance; full covariate model tested
fitting_method_software: NONMEM v7.3; Pirana v2.9.0; R v3.2.2
notes: Pooled data from 660-670 CF patients across 6 studies; female sex and F/RF genotype minor significant covariates on clearance; no dose adjustment by age, gender, race, weight, or mild/moderate renal impairment.

structural_features: Direct-effect Emax models linking total TEZ exposure (Cavg) to ppFEV1 (age-dependent change-point plus disease-progression component) and sweat chloride; IVA co-administration modeled as proportional Emax shift
notes: F/F-genotype CF patients across 5 studies; positive E-R relationship confirmed for total TEZ exposure vs ppFEV1; supported reduced TEZ dose during coadministration with strong CYP3A inhibitors.

structural_features: Minimal PBPK model for TEZ and M1-TEZ; CYP3A4-mediated intrinsic clearance; verified against itraconazole DDI data
notes: Predicted 2.1-fold increase in TEZ exposure with moderate CYP3A inhibitors, anchored to itraconazole strong-inhibitor data; supported TEZ dose-adjustment recommendations.

structural_features: Two-compartment model, linear time-dependent absorption; allometric exponents (0.75 CL/F, Q/F; 1 for V2/F, V3/F, subjects <70kg) added for pediatric extrapolation; eGFR and body weight retained as covariates on clearance
notes: Adult popPK model augmented with fixed allometric exponents for pediatric dose extrapolation; severe renal impairment (eGFR<30) not recommended for treatment; FDA sensitivity analysis confirmed relevance of covariates.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: EC50-normalized model-predicted Cmax/AUCtau evaluated against PD endpoints (urine GL-3/KIC, plasma lyso-Gb3, LVMi, GI symptom scores); no clear exposure-response relationship observed.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Dedicated PK interaction study in Fabry patients showed coadministration of agalsidase alfa or beta did not significantly affect migalastat exposure and vice versa; no dose-adjustment recommended.

structural_features: Not stated (immunogenicity/ADA titers act as covariate on apparent clearance)
notes: Population PK estimated terminal half-life ~34h in maintenance phase and steady-state trough:peak ratio of 0.61; anti-PAL/anti-PEG antibody titers increased apparent clearance and lowered exposure, consistent with immune-mediated clearance.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: FDA's Cox PH analysis comparing 20mg/day vs 40mg/day: 40mg/day associated with faster time to blood Phe <=360 umol/L (HR 2.22, 95% CI 1.18-4.16, p=0.013), supporting two-tier dose-titration regimen.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Sponsor's E-R analysis showed blood-Phe reduction increased with trough concentration, plateauing near 2500 ng/mL; higher ADA titers inversely associated with trough exposure and blood-Phe reduction.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: NCA of plasma ADA activity in only 4 evaluable ADA-SCID patients bridging elapegademase to historical Adagen (pegademase bovine) lead-in; dose-normalized max ADA activity/AUC0-168h ~66%/90% higher with elapegademase; trough ADA activity >15 umol/hr/mL used informally as surrogate effectiveness threshold.

structural_features: Two-compartment model with first-order absorption/elimination; dose-nonlinearity below 150mg via exponential model; lean body mass covariate (power model, exponent fixed=1); full covariate model tested (disease status, V30M mutation, TTR levels, eGFR, gender, race, albumin, ALT, bilirubin, age, concomitant meds, region)
target_population: Renal impairment; Hepatic impairment (both evaluated, neither clinically significant)
notes: Meta-analysis pooling 3 studies, 202 subjects, 3,602 plasma concentrations; no covariate clinically relevant (>20% change) on CL/F or Vc/F; model used to simulate exposure across 4 candidate dosing regimens.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Graphical assessment of Ctrough vs. % change in serum TTR (Week 65) and durability of TTR suppression after dose interruption; supported rationale that lower/less-frequent dosing might retain efficacy with improved platelet-count safety.

structural_features: Dual zero-order input (depot + direct-to-central) with first-order absorption from depot for elexacaftor (ELX); log-transformed parameters; IIV on CL, V, D1, FS
notes: ELX popPK from pooled Phase 1/2 + two Phase 3 CF trials (2794 concentrations, 167 subjects); metabolite M23-445 fit sequentially via empirical Bayes (2-compartment); sex, race, eGFR, AST, age, weight evaluated as covariates.

structural_features: Indirect-response Emax model linking ELX average concentration (Cavg) to ppFEV1 and sweat chloride, parameterized by baseline effect, Emax, EC50
notes: CF subjects anchored ELX exposure-response by genotype; bootstrap-based simulations explored dose-response at 50/100/200 mg qd.

structural_features: Minimal PBPK model for ELX with first-order absorption; active metabolite M23-445 not incorporated
notes: Predicted effects of strong/moderate CYP3A inhibitors and inducer (rifampin) on ELX/TEZ/IVA exposure, supporting dose-reduction (e.g., half dose with moderate CYP3A inhibitors); FDA judged PBPK adequate where no dedicated clinical DDI study existed.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: NCA of heptanoate PK from Phase 1 healthy-adult study used to inform labeled PK because the applicant's population PK model (sparse PK, atypical non-linear absorption/elimination) was deemed inadequate by FDA.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Applicant's exploratory analysis correlated heptanoate AUC/day with annualized major clinical events (rhabdomyolysis, hypoglycemia, cardiomyopathy) in LC-FAOD patients; FDA deemed inconclusive due to confounding by dietary changes, dose titration, and age.

structural_features: 3 transit absorption compartments with first-order absorption; first-order elimination; allometric power model (body weight) and sigmoidal maturation function (age) on CL/F and V; IIV on Ktr, CL/F, V/F
fitting_method_software: NONMEM (ICON Development Solutions); PsN for stepwise covariate modeling
estimation_technique: Empirical Bayes estimation; Allometric scaling; GAM screening + stepwise covariate modeling
notes: Pooled data from 4 studies (healthy volunteers + SMA Type 1/2/3 patients, ages 2 months-adults); only age and weight retained as time-varying structural covariates after GAM screening excluded SMA type, bilirubin, ALT, sex.

structural_features: Adult PBPK model extended to pediatrics via virtual population simulation; CYP3A-mediated inhibition of midazolam (in vitro-derived kinact optimized 6-18 fold to recover observed DDI)
analysis_goal: Extrapolation to new population; Drug-drug interaction (DDI) risk prediction
notes: Assessed whether adult-derived PBPK model adequately extends CYP3A-mediated DDI liability (midazolam) prediction to pediatrics as young as 2 months; cross-checked against population-PK empirical Bayes estimates across age strata.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Dedicated Phase 1 renal-impairment study (24 subjects: normal, CKD Stage 2, CKD Stage 3); AUC increased ~1.2-fold (Stage 2) and ~1.9-2x (Stage 3); FDA concluded no reliable creatinine-clearance-based dose adjustment feasible in DMD due to disease-related creatinine changes.

structural_features: Not applicable
pk_exposure_metric: AUC; Cmax; half-life; clearance; volume of distribution
notes: Standard IV PK characterization in pediatric DMD patients (age 4-12y): mean Vss 300 mL/kg, t1/2 2.5h, CL 217 mL/hr/kg; no renal/hepatic impairment study or population PK analysis conducted.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Attempted correlation of AUC with dystrophin expression across two dosing regimens (40 vs 80 mg/kg/week); with only n=16, effective assessment was not possible, so the applicant's proposal to select the maximum tolerated dose was accepted instead.

structural_features: First-order absorption and clearance; allometric scaling of body weight on CL/V (exponent 0.748); formulation effect on bioavailability (suspension ~20% lower F than capsule)
analysis_goal: Extrapolation to new population; Dose/regimen selection
notes: Final model used 1,166 PK observations from 76 subjects (28 HGPS patients + healthy subjects); FDA validated model as acceptable for simulating exposures under alternative dosing regimens, evaluating BW-based vs BSA-based dosing.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Concentration-QTc analysis from TQT study (lonafarnib + ritonavir, no monotherapy arm); FDA deemed results uninterpretable/inadequate and required a post-marketing DDI study.

structural_features: First-order SC absorption; dual elimination pathways (hepatic uptake clearance CLH + renal clearance CLR fixed to baseline eGFR*BSA/1.73); power function of dose on CLH; allometric exponents fixed (0.75 clearances, 1.0 volumes); IIV on CLH and Ka, IOV on Ka
notes: 763 plasma PK observations from 99 subjects (24 healthy adults + 75 PH1 patients); central volume fixed from nonclinical data; renal clearance fixed to baseline renal function; supported body-weight-based dosing.

structural_features: Plasma: 2-compartment model with depot (SC-like absorption) and linear elimination; CSF: separate 1-compartment linear model (trough-only data, no covariate analysis possible); ADA status and baseline body surface area on clearance, sex on central volume
notes: 166 SOD1-ALS subjects (Studies 101, 102); presence of ADA decreased plasma clearance by 32%.

structural_features: Indirect response models: post-hoc CSF tofersen exposure inhibiting production in effect compartments for (1) CSF total SOD1 protein and (2) plasma neurofilament light chain (NfL); no significant covariates identified
notes: PK-SOD1 model simulated CSF SOD1 reduction at 100/150/200 mg monthly doses (29.1% vs 23.4% median reduction at 200 vs 100 mg), concluding marginal benefit of higher doses given high interindividual Emax variability; supported retaining the 100 mg dose. Biomarker reduction (67% NfL) used as surrogate for likely clinical benefit given accelerated-approval pathway.

structural_features: Translational PBPK model using volume-based scaling of tofersen CNS tissue exposure from non-human primates to humans, combined with an exposure-SOD1 mRNA reduction curve derived from human transgenic mouse data
notes: FDA found substantial uncertainty in this translational PBPK approach (assumptions of identical potency and CNS drug-transfer rates across species could not be verified; predictive power unconfirmed against only 2 human autopsy CNS tissue samples); review team relied instead on observed clinical NfL reduction rather than the PBPK-based dose justification.

structural_features: 1-compartment TMDD model (quasi-equilibrium approximation) with linear FcRn-independent elimination plus nonlinear FcRn-mediated pathway; linked indirect-response model for total IgG turnover (target-occupancy-driven increase in IgG elimination) further linked to an MG-ADL efficacy model
notes: PK model: 266 subjects/898 concentrations; total IgG model: 412 subjects/5566 levels; MG-ADL model: 200 gMG patients/2180 scores. Body weight was a significant covariate on CL/F, V/F, and baseline IgG. Chained PK-IgG-MG-ADL models were used to simulate missed/delayed-dose scenarios and to justify a 2-fixed-dose regimen (vs. weight-tiered) with comparable predicted exposure/efficacy except in subjects >=100 kg.

structural_features: First-order absorption via two parallel transit-compartment chains (TCAMs), linear elimination; covariates: age, Black race, weight on clearance, sex and weight on central/peripheral volume
estimation_technique: Allometric scaling; Empirical Bayes estimation; Simulation
notes: 1376 subjects across 17 studies (healthy, MDD, PPD); model additionally used (with CYP3A4-maturation and body-weight scaling) to simulate infant PK exposure via breastfeeding, predicting infant exposure at 2.7-4.2% of adult levels and relative infant dose <1%, supporting standard lactation risk/benefit labeling.

structural_features: Longitudinal exposure-response model for HAMD-17 depression score: Weibull-shaped placebo-response kinetics plus a linear zuranolone drug-effect term on average plasma concentration (Cavg) within each dosing interval
notes: Estimated drug-effect slope 0.0191 (95% CI 0.0133-0.0276); predicted steady-state HAMD-17 reductions of 0.5/0.7/0.9/1.1 points at 20/30/40/50 mg; applicant noted the model likely underpredicted true treatment effect due to placebo-model assumptions; supported the proposed dosing regimen for severe PPD.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Exposure-safety analysis of 1792 subjects (1036 zuranolone, 756 placebo) found dose-related incidence of somnolence, sedation, dizziness, tremor, and confusion; used to support dose-reduction guidance for tolerability (50->40 mg).

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Dedicated NCA-based DDI studies: verapamil (CYP3A4 inhibitor) increased gepirone AUC ~3.5-fold; rifampicin (strong CYP3A4 inducer) decreased AUC ~20-fold (137.6->6.7 ng*h/mL); paroxetine (CYP2D6 inhibitor, affecting the 1-PP metabolite pathway) had no meaningful effect on parent gepirone exposure. No PopPK or formal exposure-response model was built; the clinical reviewers explicitly noted a true dose-response relationship "could not be determined" given the flexible-dosing trial designs and low proportion of patients receiving doses >=40 mg.

structural_features: First-order absorption; target-mediated exposure-enhancement model (quasi-steady-state approximation to TMDD equations) capturing complement C5 target engagement without explicit C5 concentration data; allometric scaling of CL/Q/Vc/Vp by body weight
estimation_technique: Allometric scaling; Empirical Bayes estimation; Simulation
notes: 200 subjects/2174 concentrations; race (Black/African American, Japanese) was the only significant covariate on Rmax but not clinically meaningful; model used with NHANES body-weight distribution data to confirm comparable steady-state exposures across the weight-banded dosing regimen (25-171 kg), supported by comparable MG-ADL and complement (sRBC lysis inhibition >95%) response across weight groups.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Concentration-QTc exposure-response analysis from a dedicated supratherapeutic-dose (0.6 mg/kg) TQT-type study found no evidence of clinically relevant QTc prolongation.

structural_features: IV infusion; ADA titer over time and body weight (allometric, exponents 0.8 CL/1.0 V) as covariates on clearance/volume
notes: 177 subjects/2578 concentrations (Phase 1b AACD + Phase 2 AACG); no dose adjustments recommended based on age, race, sex, APOE4, renal/hepatic impairment.

structural_features: Turnover (indirect response) models linking donanemab exposure to reduction in amyloid PET plaque level, inhibition of plasma p-tau217 formation, and plasma GFAP (via amyloid-mediated pathway)
notes: Amyloid plaque model: 12,128 observations/2023 subjects; p-tau217 model: 7195 observations/1675 subjects; none of the tested covariates (age, weight, ADA, APOE4, baseline tau) were retained in final models; supported mechanistic evidence of downstream AD pathophysiology effects alongside clinical efficacy data.

structural_features: Disease-progression exposure-response model linking donanemab exposure/amyloid reduction to clinical decline (iADRS, CDR-SB), used to simulate amyloid-based dose-cessation/titration strategy
notes: Modeling supported the amyloid-PET-guided dose-cessation regimen (stop dosing after plaque clearance <24.1 centiloids), though FDA noted uncertainty in amyloid re-accumulation rate estimates beyond 76 weeks and limited evaluation of patients who continued dosing past cessation criteria; overall regimen still judged acceptable.

structural_features: Two-compartment disposition model with zero-order absorption/biotransformation of prodrug sepiapterin into active moiety BH4, absorption lag time, linear clearance
notes: 242 participants (147 PKU patients, 95 healthy volunteers), 3320 observations; body weight allometric scaling on CL/V; health status, food, dose level significant covariates on relative bioavailability; FDA reran model excluding invalid assay data (PKU-001) with consistent results; used for Monte-Carlo dose simulation in pediatric PKU patients including <2y.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Logistic regression of BH4 AUC vs. binary Phe-reduction efficacy endpoints (>=15%, >=30% reduction; Phe<360/600 umol/L) in PKU patients from Trial PKU-003 Part 2; positive exposure-response relationship (p<0.001) for all four endpoints; not applicable to patients <2 years old (no data).

structural_features: Two-compartment model with first-order absorption and absorption lag; allometric scaling (power 0.75 CL/Q, 1.0 volumes)
notes: Applicant submitted 2 separate PopPK analyses (SPICP-105 healthy volunteers n=41; SPIBA-201 Barth syndrome patients n=7); FDA conducted sensitivity analysis integrating SPICP-105+SPIBA-201+SPIMM-301 (n=128) to strengthen covariate evaluation; body weight was significant covariate on CL/F (21% lower at 55kg, 29% higher at 105kg vs 75kg reference); no effect of sex, race, age, formulation, injection site; exposure-response for efficacy/biomarkers deemed infeasible due to small n=7 (Barth syndrome, ultra-rare disease).

structural_features: One-compartment models (separate for doxecitine and doxribtimine) with two parallel first-order absorption compartments (fed) or one (fasted), first-order elimination
notes: PopPK for TK2 deficiency built from 59 TK2d patients (age <1-81y) + 61 healthy adults across 5 studies; body weight, serum ALT, and moderate/severe renal impairment were significant covariates on CL/F; used for simulation-based dose selection under fed/fasted and renal-function strata; no formal dose-response for efficacy identified; graphical exposure-safety analysis (AUC0-24,ss vs diarrhea/ALT/CK/lactate) showed no apparent relationship.

structural_features: Two-compartment model with first-order SC absorption plus lag time, combined linear + nonlinear (Michaelis-Menten) elimination (target-mediated-like); allometric weight effects on CLlin/Q/Vmax/V2/V3
fitting_algorithm: Stepwise covariate selection (forward p<0.01, backward p<0.001)
notes: n=477 subjects, 5813 PK observations across phase 1-3 (IV+SC); significant covariates: body weight, ADA-positive status (~40% lower exposure), baseline uPCR-24h, PFS delivery method, baseline ALT/bilirubin on Vmax; simulations supported comparable exposure between 400mg SC Q4W and 4mg/kg IV monthly.

structural_features: Indirect response (turnover) model of serum total IgA production inhibition (Kout) driven by sibeprenlimab concentration (Imax/IC50), layered on 2-compartment PK model
notes: Baseline IgA level was the only significant covariate on Imax (higher baseline IgA -> lower Imax); used with popPK model to simulate comparable IgA suppression profiles between SC and IV regimens.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: n=446 subjects (253 sibeprenlimab, 193 placebo) from completed phase 2 (VIS649-201) + partial phase 3 (417-201-00007); Emax model linked steady-state AUCtau to ratio of uPCR-24h at 9 months vs. baseline; age effect on placebo response (E0); EC50 poorly estimated (RSE 78-123%); simulations supported 400mg SC Q4W dosing near plateau of E-R curve.

structural_features: Target-mediated drug disposition (TMDD) elimination pathway combined with linear clearance component (nonlinear at low concentrations, approaching dose-proportional/linear at higher doses as target pathway saturates)
notes: PopPK pooled across phase 1 healthy volunteer and phase 2/3 FOP patient studies; body weight, sex, and disease status (healthy vs FOP) were significant covariates on CL/Vd; renal/hepatic function, age not significant; supported no dose adjustment for intrinsic factors.

structural_features: Not applicable
estimation_technique: Simulation-based probability modeling (500 replicates); rate ratio comparison
notes: Dose/exposure-response analysis (pooled phase 2 Trial 1623 + phase 3 Trial 2175) supported similar efficacy for new HO lesions between 3 and 10 mg/kg Q4W, but greater flare-up reduction with 10mg/kg (rate ratio 0.69); dose-dependent increase in SSTI risk with 10mg/kg (rate ratio 1.38); no consistent E-R relationship for epistaxis; supported recommending 10mg/kg starting dose with option to reduce to 3mg/kg for tolerability.

structural_features: Two-compartment model (central plasma volume 7.95L; peripheral volume 315L) for intrathecally-administered antisense oligonucleotide; multiple structural model variants (S1-4, S8-4) evaluated in FDA reviewer sensitivity analysis
notes: FDA reviewer simulated CSF Ctrough and plasma AUCtau/Cmax across pediatric age range (<2 to <5y) using 2 selected model variants to support extrapolating 50mg every-3-months dosing to children <2y, based on comparable CSF exposure to 2-<5y reference population despite higher predicted plasma exposure in youngest patients.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Exploratory analysis (very small n: 1-4 subjects per arm) of observed CSF Ctrough (Weeks 13-49) vs. percent change in GMFM-88 Dimension D/E at Week 61 in subjects 2 to <5 years old; showed potential positive trend supporting higher 50mg Q12W dose for children <2 years; interpretation limited by extremely small sample size.

structural_features: One-compartment model, zero-order absorption duration (D1), parameterized with CL/F and V/F
notes: Pooled from 5 Phase 2 studies, 6039 observations from 1070 RA patients, doses 1-30mg BID and 20mg QD; body weight, age, gender, race not significant covariates on CL/F; time-dependence of CL/F assessed (no evidence of auto-induction/inhibition).

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Dose-response modeling of ACR20/50/70 efficacy and severe anemia safety (>2g/dL Hgb decrease or <8g/dL) from Study A3921025 used to select 5mg and 10mg BID doses for Phase 3 (both achieved >50% probability of target efficacy+safety effect); confirmed by Phase 3 results.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Observed concentration-time profiles in moderate/severe renal impairment and hepatic impairment subjects modeled via NCA/WinNonlin, then simulated for alternative dosing regimens to match AUC exposure to that of 5mg dose in normal function subjects; supported dose reduction recommendations (5mg BID max, or 5mg QD if only 5mg BID approved) for moderate/severe renal impairment; no adjustment needed for mild impairment or hepatic impairment.

structural_features: One-compartment model with first-order absorption (Ka) and lag time
notes: Identified disease status (PsA vs healthy), sex, and body weight as significant covariates on CL/F and Vc/F; PsA patients had ~1.4-fold higher steady-state AUC than healthy subjects; lower body weight/female sex associated with <26% higher exposure (not warranting dose adjustment); also supported comparing 20mg BID vs 40mg QD regimens (similar AUC, lower Cmax with BID, better GI tolerability).

structural_features: Two-compartment model with first-order SC absorption; allometric scaling on CL and V2 (exponents 0.8-1.0) by body weight; linear PK, no time- or dose-dependent clearance
notes: Pooled across phase 2/3 psoriasis studies; body weight the only clinically relevant covariate on CL/V; bioavailability estimated 72%; half-life ~27 days; supported evaluating body-weight-based vs flat dosing regimens.

structural_features: Indirect response (turnover) model linking secukinumab concentration to PASI score via EC50-driven inhibition of score turnover (Kout), plus disease progression component (linear or exponential decline)
notes: Turnover PK-PASI model with high shrinkage on some random effects (kout 20.7%, EC50 24.3%, SLOPE 18.8%) suggesting cautious interpretation; no clear covariate trends (body weight, age, baseline PASI, sex, region).

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Univariate/multivariate logistic regression of Week-12 trough concentration vs. IGA 0/1, PASI75/90/100 responses; concentration remained significant predictor after adjusting for baseline IGA score and body weight (p<2e-16); 90kg body-weight cutoff lost significance, but 100kg cutoff regained significance.

structural_features: Two-compartment model (IV administration, pooled across HES/asthma/eosinophilic esophagitis studies); body weight only significant covariate on CL/V1 (~30% lower in healthy vs patients, small healthy n)
notes: n=327 subjects across 6 studies (HES, asthma, healthy, eosinophilic esophagitis); model developed on pooled data applied without refinement to severe refractory asthma phase 3 population (Study MEA112997), described data adequately.

structural_features: Not applicable
estimation_technique: Negative binomial regression; Sigmoid Emax modeling; Logistic regression
notes: E-R analysis of clinically significant exacerbation rate (negative binomial GLM/Emax) and binary exacerbation outcome (logistic regression) vs average concentration in severe eosinophilic asthma; nonlinear Emax model modestly improved fit over binary treatment-effect model (dBIC=12) but EC50 poorly estimated (SE ~800%) due to lack of information in declining portion of E-R curve (10-fold dose range acted like step function); reviewer concluded a formal continuous E-R relationship could not be reliably characterized.

structural_features: Two-compartment model with allometric scaling of clearance/volume and an age-related renal-maturation factor on clearance; reviewer modified applicant's model (fixed renal elimination fraction at 40%, removed IIV on Q and Vp) to achieve convergence
notes: Rare disease (MoCD Type A), small pooled dataset from 2 trials; simulations across ages 0-5 years/weights 2.5-30 kg supported proposed initial dose (age/gestational-age tiered) and uniform 0.9 mg/kg max dose; also supported the 1.5 mL/min infusion rate.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Applicant's Exposure-Response Analysis Report examined fosdenopterin Cmax/AUC vs. biomarkers (plasma uric acid, xanthine, urothione; urine S-sulfocysteine, uric acid, urothione); strong positive E-R relationship found for plasma urothione (viewed as indirect evidence of restored molybdenum cofactor synthesis); no relationship for uric acid/xanthine.

structural_features: Linear 1-compartment model with first-order absorption and absorption lag time; final model did not adequately describe pediatric data (goodness-of-fit poor in pediatric trials due to sparse sampling, 60-80% BLQ)
notes: n=158 (105 healthy adults, 53 pediatric patients) across 4 trials; model deemed inadequate for pediatric PK estimation; reviewer instead relied on observed pediatric concentrations plus adult NCA-derived parameters to inform pediatric labeling.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Dedicated Phase 1 two-part DDI trial (n=22 healthy adults, Trial A4250-013); odevixibat coadministration decreased midazolam (CYP3A4 substrate) AUC by ~29% and Cmax by ~29% (not clinically significant, no CYP3A4 inhibition); Part B evaluated itraconazole (P-gp inhibitor) effect on odevixibat PK.

structural_features: 3-compartment model with parallel linear/nonlinear (Michaelis-Menten) clearance from central compartment; two concatenated peripheral compartments for secondary kinetic phase; body weight covariate (power model, median 70.5 kg) on CL/V/Vm; age, sex, renal function (eGFR), ADA status not significant
notes: n=91 (75 LOPD adults, 16 pediatric IOPD)/2583 PK samples across 4 trials up to 40 mg/kg qow; body weight was the significant covariate (lower exposure in lower-weight patients at same mg/kg dose); model used to support pediatric (1 to <18y) dose selection via virtual-population body-weight simulations matching adult exposure.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: COMET trial, n=51 (20 mg/kg); individual popPK-derived exposure regressed against %FVC and 6MWT change from baseline (weeks 13-49); no positive E-R relationship identified; negative trend attributed to baseline imbalance (heavier/older patients had higher AUC quartiles but lower baseline FVC/6MWT).

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Pooled data from 4 trials; multivariate logistic regression of TEAE probability vs. AUClast/log(AUClast) adjusted for age, disease type, treatment-naive status; no significant exposure-safety relationship, supporting extrapolation of pediatric IOPD safety data to LOPD population.

structural_features: PBPK model using an Advanced Dissolution Absorption and Metabolism (ADAM) model with mechanistic effective permeability (MechPeff) absorption submodel; applicant's model described SAD PK but failed to reproduce MAD PK (high interindividual variability, largely unquantifiable concentrations); FDA reviewer instead used a mechanistic static model (per 2020 FDA DDI guidance) with optimized gut/liver concentrations
fitting_method_software: Simcyp (fu,gut prediction); platform for full PBPK not stated
notes: Maralixibat is a time-dependent CYP3A inhibitor (kinact 0.015 min-1, Ki 5.1 uM) and OATP2B1 inhibitor in vitro; no population PK model was feasible (sparse, largely unquantifiable plasma concentrations); static-model analysis concluded minimal effect on CYP3A substrate midazolam at proposed therapeutic doses.

structural_features: One-compartment model with first-order absorption including a time-dependent change-point in absorption rate constant (Ka1=2.21 h-1 switching to Ka2=0.06 h-1 at 0.31h) and first-order elimination; body weight covariate on CL/V
notes: Used to support transition from mg/kg dosing to simplified 8-weight-band dosing table (10-90 kg); simulated AUC/Cmax at each weight band compared to observed exposures from pivotal (111-301) and phase 2 (111-202/205) trials, confirming comparable exposure across bands.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: n=60 (Study 111-301); no significant E-R relationship between exposure and efficacy biomarkers (BSAP, CXM) or annualized growth velocity; weak but statistically significant positive correlation between exposure and maximum heart-rate increase (safety), no correlation with blood-pressure change.

structural_features: Two-compartment model with first-order absorption with time lag; allometric scaling (fixed exponents 0.75 on CL/Q, 1 on V) normalized to 70 kg; weight covariate on maximum absorbed dose; VPC showed unreliable performance in pediatric patients (sparse absorption-phase sampling); enzyme-inducing AEDs not included as covariate (small subgroup, n=12)
fitting_method_software: Not stated (main report); supplemental adult-only report used Kinetica v5.0, discontinued/unverifiable, not reviewed
notes: n=146 subjects/694 samples pooled pediatric+adult; FDA found pediatric model performance unreliable; separate applicant exposure-response report (efficacy/safety) was submitted but explicitly not reviewed by FDA as it "did not provide additional insight."

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Phase 1 DDI study (1042-DDI-1001): itraconazole (strong CYP3A4 inhibitor) increased ganaxolone AUC by 17% (Cmax unchanged); rifampin (strong CYP3A4/2C19 inducer, moderate CYP2B6 inducer) decreased Cmax by 57% and AUC by 68%; findings supported dosage-increase guidance with concomitant enzyme inducers.

structural_features: Two-compartment model with first-order absorption from SC depot; clearance = sum of hepatic + renal clearance (renal CL fixed to eGFR*BSA/1.73); allometric scaling of CL/V by body weight; formulation (prefilled syringe vs. vial) affected absorption rate
notes: n=182 pooled from Phase 1 + pivotal HELIOS-A trial; body weight was most influential covariate (<64kg: +25% AUC/+51% Cmax; >=75kg: -22% AUC/-44% Cmax vs. 64-<75kg reference); mild/moderate renal impairment and mild hepatic impairment had no clinically meaningful effect; severe renal impairment (eGFR 15) predicted +27% AUC but not clinically studied; supported no-dose-adjustment labeling.

structural_features: Sequential zero-then-first-order absorption, linear elimination; separate models for twice-daily immediate-release tablet (used in pivotal trials) and once-daily extended-release capsule (to-be-marketed formulation); weight (allometric) covariate on CL/F and Vc/F
notes: Tablet model: 782 subjects/5277 concentrations (6 phase 1, 1 phase 2b, 2 phase 3 adult studies); ER capsule model: 328 subjects/10263 concentrations. Simulation-based bridging supported an intermediate 210-mg QD ER dose (in addition to applicant-proposed 140/280 mg) to match twice-daily tablet exposures demonstrated effective in adults; comparative bioavailability study additionally confirmed the 280-mg ER vs 200-mg BID tablet bridge.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: No apparent exposure-response relationship for ADHD efficacy was found in adults (consistent with comparable efficacy at both studied doses); logistic regression of Cmax against rash/skin eruption and insomnia showed dose/exposure-related trends supporting safety labeling. Limited pediatric PK sampling precluded a pediatric efficacy E-R analysis; pediatric approval instead relied on PK-matching (adult-equivalent dosing) plus disease similarity assumptions.

structural_features: First-order absorption, linear elimination; covariates: body weight on Vc/F, Q1/F, Vp1/F; T1-formulation effect and total daily dose (on Ka) on bioavailability/absorption; Asian race and female sex on volume terms; hepatic impairment (mild/moderate) and renal impairment (moderate/severe) on CL/F
fitting_method_software: NONMEM (FDA reviewer used 2 Metropolis-Hastings chains vs applicant's 1)
fitting_algorithm: SAEM (iterative two-stage for initial values, then SAEM; importance sampling for OFV)
notes: 494 subjects/8535 concentrations across phase 1-3 studies. Model-based simulation (not a dedicated comparative BA study) was used to bridge the phase 3 tablet (T3) to phase 2 tablet (T2) formulation, showing comparable Cavg,ss/Cmax,ss.

structural_features: Full PBPK model (first-order absorption + full distribution) incorporating CYP3A4-mediated clearance with both time-dependent inhibition (autoinhibition, Ki/kinact) and induction (autoinduction, Indmax/IndC50) of oveporexton's own metabolism, informed by in vitro data optimized/verified against clinical DDI studies (itraconazole, fluconazole, phenytoin)
fitting_method_software: Simcyp v23 (some library models modified by FDA reviewer, e.g. cimetidine Ki, phenytoin Indmax)
notes: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitor (itraconazole): 7.4-fold AUC increase, 67% Cmax increase, ~5-fold half-life increase (contraindicated); moderate inhibitor (fluconazole): 2.86-fold AUC increase (dose reduction to 0.5 mg BID recommended); strong inducer (phenytoin): 81% AUC decrease (avoid); PBPK-predicted moderate inducer: 72% AUC decrease (avoid); weak inhibitors/inducers predicted not clinically significant.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Using population-PK-model-predicted exposures, logistic regression found Cavg,ss a significant predictor of insomnia (p=0.048) and urinary events (p=0.034), with a near-significant trend for micturition urgency (p=0.052); no exposure relationship found for pollakiuria; supported characterization of oveporexton's dose-dependent on-target orexin-agonism adverse-event profile (TEAE incidence ~87% vs 49% placebo).

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Small dedicated PK study (n=3 healthy volunteers, n=3 AD/MCI participants per dose arm) using arterial blood sampling and log-linear terminal-phase NCA; found comparable clearance/PK between healthy and AD/MCI participants and dose-proportional increases in AUC across the two radioactivity dose levels (160/370 MBq) of this diagnostic tau-PET imaging tracer. Included because it is a genuine quantitative comparative PK analysis (not just boilerplate) despite being a diagnostic imaging agent.

structural_features: Two-compartment model with first-order SC absorption and linear elimination; allometric scaling of CL/V by body weight; study/site-specific bioavailability; M3 method for handling BLQ concentrations from ADA-mediated exposure loss
fitting_method_software: NONMEM (control stream referenced, version not stated)
notes: Pooled PK from 3 studies (RHAG, RHAJ, RHAZ) with different formulations; body weight and injection site significant covariates on CL/bioavailability but not clinically significant (exposure overlap across weight strata); individual Ctrough estimates used downstream in E-R analyses.

structural_features: Not applicable
estimation_technique: Logistic regression (ordered categorical, Emax-linked for sPGA; binary for PASI75/90/100)
notes: PopPK-model-derived individual Ctrough at Week 12/60 linked to sPGA (ordered categorical with Emax drug-effect term) and PASI 75/90/100 (binary logistic) responses in studies RHAJ/RHAZ; efficacy response approached plateau of E-R curve at 80mg Q2W induction dose, supporting body-weight-independent dosing.

structural_features: Two-compartment model (V1 central, V2 peripheral, intercompartmental clearance Q) for IV-administered reslizumab
notes: Reviewer confirmed model robust to inclusion/exclusion of below-LOQ cutoff (OLOQ) in analysis dataset (comparable parameter estimates).

structural_features: Sigmoid Emax time-course models linking reslizumab Cavg,ss to FEV1 improvement, ACQ7 score reduction, and blood eosinophil count reduction; each parameterized with baseline value, Emax, time to 50% max effect, sigmoidicity factor; BMI significant covariate on FEV1 Emax
notes: Linear relationship best described Emax vs Cav,ss for FEV1 (~70mL greater improvement) and ACQ7; response not significantly influenced by age, body weight, sex, race, or concomitant asthma medications (except BMI on FEV1 Emax).

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: E-R analysis of muscle disorder adverse events (broad MedDRA category) vs Cav,ss found no significant E-R relationship or dose-response trend; supported no dose adjustment needed for this safety signal.

structural_features: Two-compartment model with instantaneous IV or first-order SC input and combined linear + saturable (Michaelis-Menten, target-mediated-like) elimination; allometric weight scaling on CL/Q/V1/V2/Vmax; baseline PASI score covariate on Vmax
notes: Pooled dataset: 25,407 PK samples from 3,821 subjects across phase 1-3 (healthy volunteers, psoriasis/PsA patients); brodalumab exhibited nonlinear (greater than dose-proportional) PK reflecting saturable target-mediated elimination.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Emax dose-response model of Week-12 %PASI improvement and PASI75/90/sPGA(0,1) rates across 70-280mg regimens in phase 2 study 20090062 (dose used as driver given nonlinear PK); 140mg Q2W achieved near-maximal response, supporting phase 3 dose selection.

structural_features: Two-compartment model with 3 transit absorption compartments (SC) and parallel linear + Michaelis-Menten (target-mediated) elimination; Km fixed at 0.01 mg/L (steep target-mediated phase); body weight covariate on volume/clearance
notes: Pooled from 16 studies (2115 subjects: 202 healthy, 1913 AD patients); step-wise model building due to highly nonlinear PK and sparse phase 3 sampling; high/moderate ADA-titer subjects excluded (reviewer-flagged limitation, <1% of population).

structural_features: Not applicable
estimation_technique: Emax modeling (continuous %change EASI); Logistic regression (FDA reviewer, binary EASI-75)
notes: Applicant's Emax model (selected over sigEmax/logistic/linear by AIC) linked Ctrough/AUC0-112 to %change in EASI; BMI/body weight most influential covariate on baseline response (E0). FDA reviewer's independent logistic regression (full SOLO1/SOLO2 datasets incl. missing-data patients) confirmed significant AUCss-EASI-75 relationship; baseline EASI severity also significant.

structural_features: Michaelis-Menten approximation of TMDD; two-compartment model with first-order SC absorption from depot and parallel linear + nonlinear (M-M) elimination from central compartment
notes: Body weight, ADA status, drug product, albumin, sex, creatinine clearance, baseline CRP were significant PK covariates, none clinically meaningful; absolute SC bioavailability ~80%; ~3-fold accumulation, steady state by Week 20 (q2w).

structural_features: Indirect response models: (1) inhibition of DAS28-CRP "production" (Kin) via Emax function of concentration (efficacy); (2) stimulation of absolute neutrophil count (ANC) production via indirect response model (safety biomarker)
notes: DAS28-CRP model (n=2082 subjects, 17229 observations) included covariates on baseline (BLCRP, BLVAS, BLHAQ, weight), Emax (BLCRP), kout (prior corticosteroid use); ANC time-course model included smoking status and prior corticosteroid use as covariates.

structural_features: Not applicable
estimation_technique: Emax modeling; linear/log-linear comparison (AICc); logistic regression (time-to-event endpoints)
notes: Pooled safety data (Studies EFC11072 Parts A/B, EFC10832) modeled continuous (ALT change, neutrophil %change, LDL %change) and time-to-event (first neutropenia, first ALT>3xULN) vs Ctrough; Emax model best described ALT increase (EC50 0.97 mg/L at Week 24), plateauing near 200mg q2w exposure; higher baseline ALT/BMI and no prior biologic use associated with greater ALT increases.

structural_features: One-compartment linear model with first-order absorption and first-order elimination; body weight effect on CL/F and V/F; diabetes comorbidity and race (Caucasian vs non-Caucasian) effects on CL/F
notes: n=1454 subjects final dataset pooled across phase 1-3 studies; disease status (healthy vs psoriasis) not a significant covariate despite unadjusted Cmax/AUC differences (small-n confound in psoriasis studies).

structural_features: Indirect response (IDR) model of ordered categorical IGA/PASI outcomes over time, combining empirical placebo-effect function (asymptotic exponential onset) with Emax drug-effect term (EC50) on logit scale
notes: Longitudinal mechanism-based model used to characterize timing of onset of drug effect and support dosage recommendation (sequential modeling using popPK parameter estimates).

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Landmark analysis linking popPK-model-predicted individual Css/AUC to categorical IGA (0/1, 0) and PASI (75/90/100) responses at Weeks 16/28; FDA review team verified and agreed the E-R analysis provided supportive evidence for the dosing regimen.

structural_features: Two-compartment disposition model with first-order SC absorption; dose-proportional PK; allometric weight scaling on CL (0.807) and volumes; ADA positivity associated with 2.24-fold increase in CL
analysis_goal: Dose/regimen selection; Extrapolation to new population
estimation_technique: Empirical Bayes estimation; Allometric scaling; Simulation
notes: n=2267 asthma patients, 14,918 PK samples across 9 studies; body weight only clinically relevant covariate on CL (no dose adjustment needed); adolescent (12-17y) exposure simulated using 1200 virtual patients, showing substantial overlap with adult exposure at body weight >=35kg, supporting dosing extrapolation.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: E-R model on annual asthma exacerbation rate (AER) using steady-state trough concentrations from Phase 2b Study MI-CP220 estimated 30mg SC (Q4W x3 then Q8W) as the ED90 dose, supporting Phase 3 dose selection; dose-response also observed for blood eosinophil count reduction (57-76% at 20-100mg vs 14% placebo).

structural_features: 3-compartment model with time-varying body-weight-dependent allometric scaling on CL/V1/V2/V3; drug-substance manufacturing process (Process A/B vs. C) included as significant covariate on CL/V1/V2; follow-up analysis (POH0475) tested ADA status/titer as covariate - not significant
notes: n=69 (20 pediatric, 49 adult) ASMD patients/3100 concentrations across 5 trials up to 3 mg/kg Q2W IV; manufacturing process was a significant covariate (Process C: 25% lower CL, 18-21% lower V1/V2, translating to 16-24% higher Cmax/AUC); FDA noted model limitation (fixed Q2/Q3 without IIV) but found model acceptable overall.

structural_features: Three linked turnover/indirect-response models (NONMEM): (1) olipudase alfa concentration inhibits lyso-sphingomyelin (Lyso-SPM) production rate (Imax model; IC50/Imax influenced by body weight, turnover time influenced by age); (2) Lyso-SPM stimulates spleen-volume expansion rate (turnover model, power function, no significant covariates); (3) Lyso-SPM stimulates rate of DLco reduction (turnover model)
pk_exposure_metric: Not applicable (driven by model-predicted olipudase alfa/Lyso-SPM concentrations rather than a standard AUC/Cmax metric)
notes: Lyso-SPM model: 2739 measurements/58 subjects; Spleen volume model: 274 obs/54 subjects; DLco model: 222 obs/46 subjects; mechanistically linked PK to a biomarker (Lyso-SPM) and downstream clinical endpoints (spleen volume, DLco) across pediatric and adult ASMD patients.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: popPK-model-derived individual exposure metrics vs. efficacy (spleen volume, DLco, platelets) and safety (SAE, severe AE, TEAE-related dose interruption) at Week 52; no apparent E-R relationship identified for efficacy or safety across studied dose/exposure range.

structural_features: Two-compartment model, first-order absorption with lag time; saturable relative bioavailability (Frel) modeling less-than-dose-proportional exposure; auto-induction term on CL/F (rapid increase to steady state after first dose); covariates: alkaline phosphatase, creatinine clearance, sex on CL; race on Vc; formulation on Tlag/Ka; externally validated in IgAN patients (PROTECT trial)
notes: Model from 7 Phase 1 HV studies + Phase 2/3 FSGS trials, externally validated using 679 trough samples from 174 IgAN patients (PROTECT); renal impairment increased exposure (~15% higher AUC at 5th-percentile CrCL) but not considered clinically meaningful enough to warrant dose adjustment; body weight not a significant covariate.

structural_features: Not applicable
estimation_technique: Linear regression; Logistic regression; Ordinal logistic regression
notes: PROTECT trial (IgAN); n=135 (efficacy, UP/C at Week 36) and n=174 (safety); no significant E-R for efficacy (UP/C reduction), though lower exposures trended toward less reduction (confounded by renal function); exposure significantly associated with hyperkalemia incidence (p=0.03-0.05), supporting a monitoring recommendation; no significant E-R for hypotension or peripheral edema after covariate adjustment.

structural_features: PBPK model combining an ADAM absorption model with MechPeff permeability, a full-body distribution model, and an enzyme-kinetics elimination model; used to predict sparsentan as victim of CYP3A inhibitors/inducers and P-gp inhibitors, and as perpetrator (inducer) of CYP2B6/2C9/2C19
notes: Model adequately predicted weak/minimal interactions with moderate/weak CYP3A inhibitors (fluconazole, erythromycin, fluvoxamine) and moderate CYP3A inducer efavirenz; may underpredict rifampin (strong inducer) effect due to unmodeled P-gp/biliary excretion increase; inadequate to evaluate effects on CYP2C9/2C19 substrates.

structural_features: Two-compartment model, first-order absorption, linear clearance; alternative absorption models (zero-order, sequential/parallel zero-plus-first-order) tested but not superior; covariates: age and alkaline phosphatase on CL; healthy-vs-patient status and food on Ka; food on bioavailability
notes: n=253 subjects/3310 concentrations across 6 studies; simulations predicted 25% higher AUCtau and 18% higher Cmax in patients >=65 years vs. reference 34-year-olds; reviewer agreed no dose adjustment needed for the approved population (FA patients >=16 years).

structural_features: Longitudinal disease-progression model for mFARS (modified Friedreich's Ataxia Rating Scale): placebo-arm progression modeled as a linear slope with sigmoidal (Hill-function) time-delay onset; drug effect modeled as an additive change in disease-progression slope (binary treatment-arm effect rather than continuous PK exposure); covariates: pes cavus status on treatment effect, baseline mFARS on time-delay (T50)
pk_exposure_metric: Not applicable (treatment-arm indicator, not a continuous exposure metric)
notes: Study 1402 Part 1/2; characterized omaveloxolone's disease-modifying effect on mFARS progression vs. placebo; pes cavus status and baseline mFARS were significant covariates on treatment effect/delay.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: n=171 FA patients (27 with cardiac events); Cmax,ss was strongest univariate predictor of cardiac events but 95% CI for slope included zero in final model; FDA noted limitations (pooling heterogeneous event types, no adjustment for AE timing vs. Tmax) and concluded the PK-cardiac-risk relationship remains unclear, informing post-marketing QT/cardiac safety requirements.

structural_features: PBPK model to predict DDI liability of omaveloxolone as a victim of CYP3A modulators; model did not adequately capture observed PK profile
notes: FDA determined the PBPK analysis inadequate to predict CYP3A inhibitor/inducer effects (classified as high model risk given intended use in lieu of a clinical DDI study); ~4-fold exposure increase with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors was observed clinically and used for labeling despite inadequate PBPK verification for moderate inhibitors.

structural_features: 3-compartment mammillary model with zero-order IV infusion, first-order elimination; IIV on CL, V1, Q3, V3 (CL-V1 covariance); anti-drug-antibody (IgG) titer modeled as an Emax relationship on CL/V1 (high titers markedly reduce exposure - titer >7,000 reduces Cmax to ~35% and AUC to <10% of ADA-negative levels); study (treatment-naive F01/F02 vs. ERT-experienced F20/F50) also significant; FDA reviewer found applicant's inclusion of occasion-dependent bioavailability scientifically implausible (IV bioavailability should be fixed at 100%) and re-ran a corrected model
notes: Pooled Fabry disease trials (PB-102-F01/F02, F20, F50); Q4W 2 mg/kg regimen produced ~86% higher Cmax but similar AUC/Cavg vs. Q2W 1 mg/kg, supporting an alternative dosing option; FDA identified multiple data-quality/model-specification issues in the applicant's submitted PPK report.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: FDA reviewer assessed relationship between exposure and PD biomarkers (plasma Lyso-Gb3, eGFR) in Studies F20/F50; Lyso-Gb3 changes were not clinically meaningful or correlated with exposure; agalsidase beta comparator showed better PD effect in male patients (Study F20), while pegunigalsidase alfa maintained more consistent response in female patients.

structural_features: 2-compartment model with first-order absorption from 6 transit compartments (mean transit time, MTT) describing absorption delay, first-order elimination; covariates: body weight (allometric power model, 70kg reference) on CL/F, Vc/F, Q/F, Vp/F; fasted state on MTT/F; sprinkle-on-food administration on MTT
notes: n=701 subjects/9088 concentrations from 16 studies (healthy volunteers, COPD, FOP, multiple-osteochondromas patients, ages 6+); model used to derive weight-based pediatric dosing categories (20-<40, 40-<60, >=60 kg) matching adult drug exposure for skeletally immature children.

structural_features: Not applicable
estimation_technique: Linear regression; Empirical Bayes estimation (individual exposure derivation)
notes: FOP patients from Phase 2 (PVO-1A-001/201/202) and Phase 3 (PVO-1A-301) trials; no significant E-R relationship for heterotopic-ossification (HO) volume change at Day 84 (Phase 2), but statistically significant relationship between cumulative AUC and HO volume change at Month 12 in Phase 3 (p=0.0497); supports the chronic 5mg / flare-up 20-10mg dosing regimen despite study-design limitations (single dosing regimen per arm, high placebo-response variability).

structural_features: PBPK model with first-order absorption, a minimal PBPK model (single adjustable distribution compartment), and an enzyme-kinetics elimination model (CYP3A4-mediated, minor CYP2C8/2C19); used to predict DDI as victim of CYP3A/CYP2C inhibitors/inducers and to predict organ-impairment effects
notes: Model adequately predicted moderate CYP3A inhibitor erythromycin effect (~2.5-fold AUC increase, consistent with observed strong-inhibitor ketoconazole effect); considered inadequate to evaluate strong CYP2C19/CYP2C8 inhibitors, moderate CYP3A inducer efavirenz, or hepatic/renal impairment due to incompletely characterized metabolic pathways.

structural_features: 2-compartment target-mediated drug disposition (TMDD) model with first-order SC absorption (KA, F1) and target-mediated elimination via binding to complement C5 (Kin=C5 synthesis, Kout=C5 degradation, Kint1/Kint2=internalization rates of 1:1 and 1:2 pozelimab:C5 complexes); PK data show approach to saturation of TMDD elimination at higher doses (10-30 mg/kg); covariates: baseline body weight (allometric, estimated exponent ~0.76) on Vc/Vp and linear CL; baseline albumin on Vc (relevant given hypoalbuminemia in protein-losing enteropathy)
notes: n=114 subjects/2709 paired pozelimab-C5 samples pooled across healthy-volunteer, PNH, and pediatric CD55-deficient PLE (CHAPLE disease) trials (median age 8.5 years, range 5-19); simulations indicated >99% C5 target saturation at Ctrough >=50 mg/L; free-C5/CH50 suppression and downstream biomarkers (sC5b-9, ALP) tracked with exposure, supporting the weight-tiered loading/maintenance dosing regimen for the pediatric CHAPLE indication; model refined per FDA request (added body-weight and IIV effects on Vp/Kin/Kint1) to improve fit in CD55-deficient PLE patients.

structural_features: 2-compartment model with parallel linear and nonlinear (Michaelis-Menten, Vmax/Km) clearance; body-weight estimated effect on CL/V1 (fixed effect on Q, V2, Vmax); miglustat (coadministered chaperone) effect on linear CL estimated as covariate; age, race, sex, ERT-history evaluated on linear CL
notes: n=96 adult LOPD subjects receiving coadministered cipaglucosidase alfa + miglustat/1606 PK observations; miglustat significantly increased cipaglucosidase alfa exposure by inhibiting its clearance (~22% AUC increase at 130mg miglustat / ~35% at >130mg), supporting the fixed co-administration regimen; body weight, age, race, sex, ERT-history had no clinically meaningful impact on AUC/Cmax.

structural_features: Emax (indirect-effect) models linking cipaglucosidase alfa (and alglucosidase alfa comparator) exposure to biomarkers urinary Hex4 and plasma CK; shared race effect on Imax, separate ERT-history and age effects on Imax by drug
notes: Biomarker E-R relationship was flat across the observed exposure range, making EC50 estimates unreliable; no apparent E-R relationship for biomarkers (Hex4, CK) or functional endpoints (6MWT, FVC) using AUC/Cmax, consistent with cipaglucosidase alfa acting intracellularly after cellular uptake rather than via plasma concentration.

structural_features: 2-compartment disposition model with dual-transit absorption (fast + slow pathways, biphasic SC absorption) and combined linear + nonlinear (Michaelis-Menten) elimination (dose-dependent over-proportional exposure increase); renal-maturation function on eGFR to extrapolate to pediatric patients as young as 6 years; body weight and renal function significant covariates; age, gender, race not significant
notes: n=143 subjects (9-73 years)/1978 plasma concentrations across 5 studies; simulations showed comparable steady-state AUC but 76% higher Cmax in pediatric patients 6-<12 years vs. reference adults, prompting a new 128mg pediatric dose cap; presence of anti-drug antibodies did not affect PK.

structural_features: Indirect-response (turnover) model with effect compartment; nedosiran plasma concentration in the effect compartment drives Imax-type inhibition of 24-hour urinary oxalate (UO24) production, with a Hill coefficient describing concentration-effect steepness; between-subject variability on baseline UO24, IC50, Imax; no significant covariates identified
notes: n=46 PH1 patients/588 UO24 observations across 3 trials (ages 9-46); model-predicted individual PK/PD parameters were later used to support single/linear imputation of missing 24h urinary-oxalate values for the primary efficacy endpoint analysis (Days 90-180).

structural_features: 1-compartment model with sequential zero-order followed by first-order absorption (D1 duration, MAT mean absorption time) and linear elimination; body weight allometric covariate on V/F (exponent 1) and CL/F (fixed exponent 0.75); meal status (fed vs. fasted, low-fat/high-fat) covariate increasing relative bioavailability (Frel) and MAT
fitting_method_software: NONMEM v7.5.0 (applicant); NONMEM v7.3.0 + Pirana 2.9.9 (FDA reviewer reproduction)
notes: n=184 subjects (healthy adults + DMD pediatric patients)/1502 concentrations across 3 studies; FDA reviewer independently reproduced applicant's results in NONMEM 7.3.0 and found the analysis adequate.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Emax models (shared EC50 across endpoints) for functional efficacy endpoints (TTSTAND, TTCLIMB [sigmoid Emax], TTRW, 6MWT, NSAA) with a placebo/disease-progression component for TTSTAND/TTCLIMB; model estimated the approved 2 mg/kg/day dose achieves ~70% of maximal effect and 6 mg/kg/day achieves ~90%, supporting the 2 mg/kg/day dose recommendation.

structural_features: Longitudinal indirect-response model in which vamorolone AUCtau,ss produces a linear increase in Kin (production rate) of BMI z-score (a Cushingoid/weight-gain biomarker); placebo/disease effect modeled as an increase in Kout half-life; concomitant prednisone use modeled as an added increase in Kin
notes: n=166 subjects across 4 studies; exposure-dependent BMI z-score increase not significantly modified by baseline age, TTSTAND, time since diagnosis, or geographic region; characterized weight-gain/Cushingoid safety liability relative to exposure to inform benefit-risk of the recommended dose vs. higher doses.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: n=87 subjects (Study VBP15-004, up to 24 weeks); among AE categories screened (behavior/socialization, cushingoid features, GI, growth hormone deficiency, skin, weight gain) only cushingoid features and weight gain showed an exposure-response relationship; Cmax,ss could not be reliably estimated due to high shrinkage in absorption parameters, so AUCtau,ss was used exclusively.

structural_features: 2-compartment disposition model with parallel first-order/3-transit absorption (SC dosing); parallel linear/nonlinear elimination (slightly greater than dose-proportional exposure); coupled to a population PD model of serum TTR (transthyretin) reduction; ADA-affected PK samples excluded from PK model but TTR data retained in PKPD model since TTR response persisted despite ADA; covariates: body weight and renal function on AUC/Cmax/Ctrough
notes: Pooled from 4 studies (CS1, CS20, CS21, CS3); simulations showed comparable steady-state PK exposure and TTR reduction between 45mg SC Q4W and Q1M (once-monthly) regimens, supporting the once-monthly dosing label; mild renal impairment showed no clinically relevant PK difference vs. normal function; moderate renal impairment data limited but did not support alternate dosing.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Phase 3 trial (CS3) at target dose 45mg Q4W; no clear trend across Cmax/Ctrough exposure quartiles for efficacy (mNIS+7, Norfolk QOL-DN) or safety (moderate/severe TEAEs), suggesting a flat E-R relationship in the studied dose range.

structural_features: 2-compartment model, first-order oral absorption with lag time; allometric scaling on CL/F (power model, weight normalized to 40.5kg median); meal status covariate on bioavailability (F1)
notes: DMD pediatric population; used for individual exposure derivation supporting dose simulations and E-R analyses.

structural_features: Friberg-type chemotherapy-induced-myelosuppression model adapted for givinostat-induced thrombocytopenia: proliferating-cell compartment + 4 transit (maturation) compartments + circulating-platelet compartment with feedback (gamma) from circulating platelets on proliferation rate; linear drug-effect term (1-slope*concentration) inhibits proliferative cell generation; parameterized by mean transit time (MTT), baseline platelet count, and effect slope; weight covariate on baseline platelet count
fitting_algorithm: Not stated (minimization instability noted; switched from 3- to 4-transit compartments and simplified residual error model to resolve)
notes: n=169 subjects (137 with DMD)/3241 platelet measurements across 3 studies; used to simulate PK/PD (platelet time-course) under alternative dosing regimens (Study 48 8-week regimen; comparison of 3 dosing regimens) to inform final dose selection balancing efficacy and thrombocytopenia risk; model performed best in Study 48.

structural_features: Not applicable
estimation_technique: Linear regression (mixed-effects, including placebo data and covariates)
notes: Study 48 (n=118 givinostat, 61 placebo; 75 with evaluable PK for E-R); linear E-R models related givinostat average steady-state concentration to Month-18 change in 4-stair-climb (primary endpoint), time-to-rise-from-floor, 6MWT, NSAA, muscle fat fraction, and strength measures; FDA requested (and applicant incorporated) placebo-anchored slope estimation and adjustment for dose-modification/time effects.

structural_features: PBPK model intended to characterize oral bioavailability of givinostat (structural details largely redacted in the public review)
notes: FDA determined the applicant's PBPK analysis (report TR2278/E) was inadequate to support conclusions about givinostat's human oral bioavailability due to lack of adequate supporting clinical data.

structural_features: 2-compartment model with transit-compartment absorption (fixed KTR), nonlinear (Michaelis-Menten) saturable elimination (Vmax, Km) from central compartment; body-weight allometric exponent on Vmax (estimated 0.444) and fixed 0.75 exponent on Q/F
estimation_technique: Empirical Bayes estimation; Allometric scaling; Simulation
notes: n=20 WHIM syndrome subjects (6 pediatric <17 years)/760 PK samples across 2 trials; simulations supported a reduced 300mg dose in adults <=50kg (19% lower AUC vs. 400mg reference) and alternative doses (200/300/400mg) for adolescents >=12 years <=50kg.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: n=19 mavorixafor-treated + 17 placebo (Studies MKKA/103); population-PK-model-predicted exposure related to time above ANC/ALC thresholds (pharmacodynamic biomarkers of WHIM syndrome mechanism); also assessed safety event incidence by Week 13 Cmax/AUC quartile.

structural_features: 2-compartment model with 7-transit-compartment absorption (depot -> transit chain -> central/peripheral) and linear elimination from central compartment; body weight (allometric) covariate on CL; age covariate on Ka
notes: n=134 subjects (ages 2-76)/2571 concentrations across 6 studies (ALS and NPC trials); pediatric NPC dosing regimen (5 body-weight bands) was derived via allometric scaling from adult PK to target AUC0-24 of 12.9 ug*h/mL (2-fold safety margin below juvenile rat NOAEL) with no prior pediatric dose-finding study; FDA reviewer also explored miglustat coadministration effect on arimoclomol exposure (higher exposure with miglustat, not formally tested as covariate by applicant) and possible PD synergy.

structural_features: Renal-impairment population PK re-analysis (later supplement) merging the original PopPK dataset with a dedicated renal impairment study (OR-ARI-REN-01); eGFR and body weight tested/retained as covariates on CL (final model included both, best OFV)
estimation_technique: Empirical Bayes estimation; Simulation; Linear regression (applicant's exposure-eGFR analysis)
notes: Applicant's linear regression across 13 eGFR bins (15-120 mL/min) found 53% higher AUC0-inf in patients with eGFR 45-50 mL/min, supporting reduced-frequency (BID) dosing in moderate-severe renal impairment (vs. TID for eGFR>=50); FDA pharmacometrics reviewer rebuilt the population PK model incorporating renal-impairment data and NHANES-derived eGFR distribution to simulate steady-state Cmax/AUC under the proposed regimens.

structural_features: 1-compartment model with 5-minute absorption lag time (Tlag), combined additive/multiplicative residual error, CL-V covariance; body weight (power model) covariate on CL and V; dose (1g vs. 2g) covariate on absorption rate constant (Ka); miglustat comedication, disease type (NPC vs. GM2 gangliosidosis), meal timing tested but not retained
fitting_algorithm: FOCE-ELS (First Order Conditional Estimation-Extended Least Squares)
notes: n=95 subjects (ages 6-67 years)/567 concentrations across 3 trials (IB1001-201, -202, -301); model informed dosing age-category adjustments and confirmed proposed dosing regimen exposure across pooled NPC and GM2-gangliosidosis populations.

structural_features: Not applicable
estimation_technique: Empirical Bayes estimation (individual exposure derivation); graphical comparison
notes: Phase 3 crossover trial (IB1001-301); individual empirical Bayes AUC estimates vs. change in fSARA (ataxia efficacy endpoint) showed no apparent E-R relationship; E-R analysis for safety not performed due to low AE event rates.

structural_features: Distinct linear PopPK models for each active moiety/major metabolite: vanzacaftor (VNZ) - 1-compartment with 6 transit absorption compartments, first-order elimination; tezacaftor (TEZ) - 2-compartment, first-order; M1-TEZ metabolite - 2-compartment; deutivacaftor (D-IVA) - 1-compartment with 7 transit compartments (Vss=0.85 L/kg); M1-D-IVA metabolite - 1-compartment; M6-D-IVA metabolite - 2-compartment; body-weight-based scaling used to justify a 40kg weight cutoff across pediatric/adult age groups
estimation_technique: Empirical Bayes estimation; Simulation; Weight-based scaling
notes: n=708 subjects/6850 PK samples (VNZ analysis)/5 trials spanning healthy volunteers and CF patients (ages 6-71); simulations confirmed the 40kg weight cutoff produced comparable exposure across pediatric/adult age bands and supported dose/weight-band and CYP3A4-inhibitor-coadministration guidance for children 6-11 years and adults with moderate hepatic impairment.

structural_features: Indirect-response Emax models linking vanzacaftor average steady-state concentration (Cavg) to two longitudinal endpoints: percent-predicted FEV1 (ppFEV1, efficacy) and sweat chloride (SwCl, biomarker); covariates on vanzacaftor Emax/baseline response included age, CFTR genotype, baseline ppFEV1 or baseline SwCl; graphical evaluation of TEZ/D-IVA exposure impact on vanzacaftor Emax
notes: n=1113 subjects/8194 ppFEV1 measurements (parallel SwCl dataset) across 4 trials; used to simulate the dose-response relationship for vanzacaftor within the triple combination and support Phase 3 dose selection; FDA verified with no significant discordance.

structural_features: PBPK models for VNZ, D-IVA (plus a prior TEZ model carried over from original NDA 210491) characterizing CYP3A4/5-mediated metabolism; predicted victim DDI risk with CYP3A inhibitors/inducers in adults and children 6-11 years, and perpetrator risk on CYP2C9 substrates
notes: Predicted 2.4-4.8-fold increases in VNZ/D-IVA AUC with moderate CYP3A inhibitors and up to 14-fold increases in pediatric patients with strong inhibitor itraconazole; predicted 69-90% exposure reductions with CYP3A inducers (rifampin, efavirenz); supported specific dose-reduction regimens (once-weekly/every-other-day) when coadministered with strong/moderate CYP3A inhibitors; could not rule out DDI risk of D-IVA inhibiting CYP2C9 substrates (warfarin, tolbutamide).

structural_features: 2-compartment linear model with first-order absorption, absorption lag time (ALAG1), IIV on CL/F, V2/F, Ka, Q/F, V3/F with Q/F-V3/F correlation; covariates: body weight, age, and disease state (IgAN vs. healthy) on CL/F; sex on V2/F; body weight on V3/F; CYP3A4 inhibitors/inducers and region tested but not retained (underpowered, <5% of population exposed)
notes: Pooled healthy-volunteer + IgAN patient trials; body weight, age, and disease state were significant covariates on clearance; CYP3A4 inhibitor/inducer effects not statistically significant but deemed unreliable given small exposed subgroup.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: ALIGN trial, n=238 IgAN subjects (124 atrasentan 0.75mg, 114 placebo); Emax model related Ctrough,ss to UPCR percentage reduction (primary efficacy endpoint) - highest exposure quartile showed ~10% greater reduction than median; linear logistic regression showed anemia incidence increased with exposure, with younger age (<45y), lower body weight (<75kg), and concomitant antihypertensive/immunosuppressive use as risk covariates.

structural_features: PBPK model with mechanistic absorption (MechPeff), full-body distribution with permeability-limited liver, and enzyme-kinetics elimination (CYP3A/UGT-mediated); atrasentan is a mechanism-based inhibitor of CYP3A4/CYP2B6 in vitro; used to predict victim DDI risk (CYP3A inhibitors/inducers) and perpetrator risk (CYP3A/P-gp/CYP2B6 substrates)
notes: FDA determined the model inadequate to predict victim DDI risk from CYP3A inhibitors/inducers (uncertainty in relative contribution of UGTs/P-gp/OATP1Bs to clearance); adequate to conclude atrasentan (perpetrator) has no clinically significant effect on CYP3A substrate midazolam or P-gp substrate fexofenadine at the 0.75mg dose; inadequate to evaluate CYP2B6 substrate (bupropion) interaction due to insufficient model verification.

structural_features: First-order absorption (SC injection); Bayesian population PK modeling
notes: Only 12 healthy subjects (30 mg SC) were used to build the model despite richer PK data being available across doses/routes; no covariate assessment and no model evaluation/qualification were performed - FDA reviewer flagged this as a significant deficiency. One of the earliest FDA reviews to use a fully Bayesian (WinBUGS) PK modeling approach.

structural_features: Four-parameter logistic (Emax-type) model relating icatibant concentration to bradykinin-challenge biomarker response (blood pressure and other PD endpoints); fit by naive pooling (not mixed-effects)
notes: 344 concentration-response observations from a healthy-volunteer bradykinin-challenge model; used to select the 30 mg Phase 3 dose, but the subsequent placebo-controlled Phase 3 trial failed to show statistically significant efficacy at that dose. FDA pharmacometrics reviewer identified major deficiencies (naive-pooling ignoring within-subject correlation; biomarker dose derived from healthy-subject bradykinin levels lower than those seen during actual HAE attacks) - a cautionary early example of biomarker-based dose selection not translating to clinical efficacy.

structural_features: Zero-order delivery to absorption compartment followed by first-order absorption, linear elimination
notes: Reviewer independently confirmed sponsor's labeling statement that gender has no clinically relevant effect on clearance (CL/F ratio 1.07 [0.94-1.19] vs sponsor's 1.03 [0.92-1.14]). Reviewer separately used Berkeley Madonna simulation (leveraging PopPK parameters plus observed clinical DDI fold-changes) to derive alternative dosing regimens (150 mg twice-weekly with strong CYP3A inhibitors; 150 mg once-daily with moderate CYP3A inhibitors) - DDI fold-changes were from dedicated clinical studies (ketoconazole: 8.45-fold AUC increase; fluconazole: 2.95-fold), not from mechanistic PBPK.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Direct Emax model related FEV1 and sweat-chloride (CFTR-activity biomarker) response to ivacaftor exposure; 150 mg q12h dose selected because it provided Cmin,ss at or above the model-predicted EC90 (FEV1) and EC84 (sweat chloride); the same PK/PD modeling and simulation approach (using Studies 101 and 007 data) was used to select the 100 mg single starting dose for the pediatric (6-11 years) lead-in study. One of the first model-based, biomarker-driven dose selections for a precision-medicine CFTR modulator.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: NCA in healthy volunteers (n=6, single-dose escalation 15/30/60 units/kg IV) and in Gaucher disease patients (Study PB-06-001, n=10-16 per dose/visit group, Day 1 and Week 38 of biweekly 30 or 60 units/kg dosing); no exposure-response relationship was found for efficacy (spleen/liver volume reduction, hemoglobin) or safety at the two doses studied, and immunogenicity/intrinsic-factor (renal/hepatic impairment) effects on exposure were not explored - flagged by FDA as an evidence gap rather than forcing an unsupported label claim.

structural_features: 2-compartment structural model with topical application effect on central volume of distribution (Vc); high inter-individual variability in absorption/clearance
notes: PopPK pooled adult and pediatric (9-16y) subjects with/without axillary hyperhidrosis; IIV for CL, Vc, Ka remained very high (160-230% CV) and individual fits were erratic, so model-based exposures were not used for safety analysis (NCA used instead).

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: NCA-derived Cmax/AUC0-24 (highest exposure day per subject) used in univariate logistic regression against anticholinergic TEAEs; AUC0-24 significantly associated with treatment-emergent blurred vision; non-significant trend for dry mouth; no signal for urinary hesitation/mydriasis.

structural_features: First-order absorption with lag time (ALAG1) and linear elimination
fitting_method_software: NONMEM v7.4.3; PsN v4.8.1; R v4.2.0
notes: 651 subjects/3986 PK observations (healthy, hepatic/renal impairment, alopecia areata patients) across phase 1-3; ALT, BMI, male sex on CL/F and body weight on V2/F statistically but not clinically significant; supported 8 mg BID without population-specific dose adjustment.

structural_features: Minimal PBPK (liver + intestinal metabolism), complete absorption (fa=1.0); CYP3A4/CYP2C9/CYP1A2 relative metabolic contributions from rhCYP + itraconazole DDI data; CYP3A4 auto-induction included but negligible
notes: Predicted strong CYP2C9 inhibitors increase AUC/Cmax ~100%/13%, dual CYP2C9+3A4 inhibitor (fluconazole) ~140%/12%; no clinically significant change with itraconazole (CYP3A4 inhib) or efavirenz (CYP3A4 inducer); CYP2C9 poor metabolizers predicted ~2-fold higher AUC than normal metabolizers.
