structural_features: Emax model for efficacy (SALT score); indirect response (turnover) models for platelet count and hemoglobin safety endpoints, linked via individual EBE exposure (Cavg)
notes: 662 subjects (phase 2/3); binary (SALT<=20) and continuous SALT-change Emax models showed near-plateau of E-R at 8 mg BID exposure; indirect response models for platelet increase/hemoglobin decrease supported acceptable safety margin at proposed dose.

structural_features: First-order SC absorption with lag time, linear elimination
notes: Pooled PN and AD (adult/adolescent) data; body weight was only clinically meaningful covariate (exposure decreases with increasing weight); supported weight-tiered flat dosing (30 mg <90kg / 60 mg >=90kg Q4W with 60 mg loading dose); disease status/formulation/presentation not significant.

structural_features: Multi-state transition model for IGA; indirect turnover model with inhibitory drug effect on production rate for weekly-average PP NRS
notes: PK/PD models for IGA and PP-NRS in PN patients used to simulate weight-tiered dosing regimens; separate exposure-safety analysis (eczematous reactions, headache, asthma, edema) found no exposure-dependent trend.

structural_features: First-order absorption, linear elimination; body-weight-based allometric exponents on CL and V
notes: 1607 subjects/6860 concentrations across 11 studies (37.5-500mg); no target-mediated drug disposition observed; body weight not clinically significant given lack of dose-exposure-response relationship; adolescents ~17-21% higher exposure than adults due to lower weight.

structural_features: Indirect effect (Emax) model linking model-derived exposure to longitudinal EASI response, with/without topical corticosteroid use
notes: Emax=0.831, EC50=16.5 ug/mL; simulations supported 500mg loading (Wk0,2) + 250mg Q2W induction through Wk16, then Q2W or Q4W maintenance; no covariates significantly affected E-R relationship.

structural_features: First-order absorption and elimination; full Omega block IIV on CL, V2, F1
notes: Body weight, Japanese/Chinese ethnicity, subject status, baseline SCr/ALT/bilirubin tested as covariates on CL; high RSE for SCr effect but overall model deemed acceptable to generate exposures for downstream PK-PD and E-R analyses.

structural_features: Direct-effect sigmoidal Emax model linking exposure to FXIIa-mediated kallikrein activity; baseline kallikrein activity effect on EC50/E0
notes: PD biomarker (FXIIa-kallikrein activity) model used to support mechanistic plausibility and inform E-R efficacy modeling; no covariates had clinically meaningful impact on PD response.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Time-varying Poisson process model with maximum-inhibition E-R relationship described HAE attack rate reduction across phase 2 (2001) and phase 3 (3001/3002) trials; none of the tested covariates (age, ethnicity, sex, prior treatment, concomitant/rescue meds, body weight, obesity) had clinically meaningful impact on effectiveness.

structural_features: Mixed zero- and first-order absorption with lag time on zero-order process, linear elimination; fixed allometric exponents on CL/V; Asian race and baseline albumin effects on CL/F; food/formulation effects on absorption duration
notes: 345 subjects/7257 PK samples across 7 phase 1 + 1 phase 2 study; no pediatrics <12y enrolled; no covariates (renal/hepatic impairment, age, sex, race) had clinically meaningful exposure impact.

structural_features: Full-body PBPK with advanced compartmental absorption/transit (ACAT) model; particle-size-informed dissolution
analysis_goal: Drug-drug interaction (DDI) risk prediction; Extrapolation to new population
notes: Predicted effect of acid-reducing agents (elevated gastric pH) on absorption (worst case unlikely to reduce efficacy) and attempted extrapolation to severe (Child-Pugh C) hepatic impairment (excluded from trials); FDA noted uncertainty in the hepatic-impairment extrapolation given no observed data.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Exploratory E-R analysis (phase 2, N=33, single 600mg dose level) found no statistically significant relationship between exposure and time-to-symptom-relief (PGI-C); interpreted cautiously given small sample/narrow exposure range. No E-R safety analysis conducted given favorable safety profile.

structural_features: Multi-phase multi-layer mechanistic transdermal absorption model (MPML MechDermA; 5 skin layers); CYP3A4/CYP1A2 elimination contributions from in vitro data
notes: FDA determined model inadequate (>2-fold prediction error vs observed multiple-dose data; CYP contributions unverifiable without clinical DDI data; dermal absorption model unverified in pediatrics), so DDI risk with strong CYP3A4 (ketoconazole)/CYP1A2 (fluvoxamine) inhibitors could not be reliably characterized.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: TEAE rates stratified by quartiles of average daily ointment dose (g) and %BSA involvement in pooled controlled/uncontrolled trials (descriptive, not a fitted regression model); no clear dose- or BSA-dependent trend in TEAE severity identified.

structural_features: First-order absorption/elimination; fixed allometric exponents (0.75 CL/F, 1 V/F); lag time; food effect on F and Ka
notes: 2551 subjects/12299 samples (94.5% PsO patients, 72 adolescents); food decreased bioavailability (fasting recommended); ADA positivity raised AUC 1.3-2 fold without efficacy/safety change; moderate renal impairment raised AUC ~1.5-fold, coinciding with higher infection incidence in that small subgroup (n=19).

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Emax-logistic model of PASI90/IGA0-1 response vs Cavg,ss using 1864 phase 3 subjects; flat E-R relationship confirmed 200mg QD is on plateau (comparable efficacy to 100mg BID); no E-R difference by weight or age (adult vs adolescent) subgroup.

structural_features: First-order absorption and elimination; body weight effect on CL/F, Vc/F, Q/F, Vp/F; site of administration/drug presentation on Ka; disease status on Vc/F, Q/F
notes: Body weight most influential covariate but not considered clinically meaningful given lack of E-R relationship; mild hepatic/renal impairment, age, sex, race, ethnicity, region not significant.

structural_features: Indirect-response (turnover) Emax model with inhibition of prekallikrein (PKK) production rate; disease status effect on baseline PKK and IC50
notes: Sequential PK-then-PD estimation with low-moderate eta-shrinkage; separate descriptive exposure-response analysis (tertiles) for liver enzymes and platelet counts found no clear trend in Trial CS5.

structural_features: First-order absorption with fixed lag time, constant clearance; fat-free mass (FFM) and fat mass (FM) effects on CL/F and V1/F; race effect on CL/F
notes: High intersubject variability (127-4386% CV for V1/F, Q/F, V2/F); FFM/FM (body composition) and Asian-region effects on exposure were 20-30%, deemed not clinically meaningful; body weight effect on exposure confirmed not clinically relevant via resampling simulation; hepatic impairment not assessed (excluded from studies).

structural_features: PBPK model integrated with semi-mechanistic TMDD PD sub-model (Lua-scripted) capturing BTK target binding saturation and its time-dependent effect on systemic clearance
notes: Predicted effects of strong/moderate/weak CYP3A inhibitors (ketoconazole, itraconazole, ritonavir, fluconazole, erythromycin, fluvoxamine) and inducers (carbamazepine, rifampicin, efavirenz, dexamethasone) on remibrutinib PK at 25mg BID; TMDD parameters (kdeg, kirr, ksyn) manually optimized top-down against single/multiple-dose Study X2101 data since simulator lacked PD parameter-estimation capability.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: 1221 subjects/45230 measurements (phase 2/3 CSU trials); sigmoidal Emax nonlinear mixed model (continuous UAS7/ISS7/HSS7) and logistic-Emax model (binary endpoints) both showed positive E-R plateauing at 25mg BID exposure; no significant E-R relationship for safety (AEs, labs, BP).

structural_features: Two-compartment model with first-order absorption (lag time), parent (pirfenidone) and metabolite (5-carboxy-pirfenidone) modeled simultaneously; analyzed separately by occasion due to high inter-occasion variability
fitting_method_software: NONMEM (Version VI); R, PsN, Xpose, Pirana
notes: Only 88 of 261 pirfenidone-arm patients in PIPF-004 had characterized PK; reviewer re-fit 2-compartment models for parent and metabolite by occasion; sponsor's exposure-efficacy analysis was inconclusive (conflicting FVC vs PFS results) and not further pursued due to limited PK sampling.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Pirfenidone ~48% metabolized by CYP1A2; fluvoxamine (strong CYP1A2 inhibitor) increased AUC0-inf ~400% and Cmax; ciprofloxacin (moderate CYP1A2 inhibitor) increased AUC 81%; smoking (CYP1A2 inducer) decreases exposure; label recommends avoiding fluvoxamine and dose reduction with moderate CYP1A2 inhibitors/smoking cessation counseling.

structural_features: One-compartment model with first-order absorption/lag time (ALAG), linear elimination; IIV on V2/F, F1, KA; IOV on F1; linked sub-model for active metabolite BIBF 1202 (bioavailability/volume/KA parameterized as functions of parent parameters)
notes: n=1191 IPF patients; age and body weight correlated with exposure but not clinically meaningful; no effect of mild/moderate renal impairment; smoking status significant; reviewer agreed no dose adjustment needed for body weight/age/gender/renal function.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Multivariate logistic regression on diarrhea (most common AE) identified steady-state AUC, smoking status and race as predictors; increasing AUC associated with increased diarrhea risk; local (GI) vs systemic exposure effects could not be distinguished.

structural_features: 1-compartment open model with first-order absorption and elimination; endogenous baseline DCA modeled as fixed parameter with log-normal IIV; combined additive+proportional residual error
notes: Population CL=32.5 L/h, V=193 L, baseline DCA=139 ng/mL, t1/2~4.1h; covariates: age on baseline DCA, dose on CL, BMI/baseline/study population/dose on V; no covariates deemed clinically relevant; no significant sex effect on CL/V; race effect not assessable due to limited diversity.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Single 50mg dose study; AUC0-inf ~4.5-fold higher in mild and ~2.6-fold (later study) to 4.9-fold (n=4) higher in moderate hepatic impairment vs matched controls; small enrolled n (moderate n=4) limited conclusions; severe hepatic impairment not studied; contraindicated in hepatic impairment.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Flibanserin extensively metabolized by CYP3A4; fluconazole (multi-enzyme inhibitor) increased AUC0-inf 7-fold; itraconazole/ketoconazole (strong CYP3A4 inhibitors) increased Cmax 1.7-1.8-fold; co-administration with fluconazole caused severe hypotension/syncope in first 15 subjects, halting further study in that arm; contraindicated with CYP3A4 inhibitors and alcohol.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Efficacy exposure-response inconsistent across co-primary endpoints (SSE increased significantly at 100mg qhs but eDiary desire score not significant); clear dose/exposure relationship for CNS depressant AEs (dizziness, somnolence, hypotension); combined with DDI-driven exposure spikes this supported contraindications/REMS.

structural_features: Two-compartment model; renal function (creatinine clearance) as major covariate on clearance
notes: Re-evaluation of original 2-compartment popPK model with new renal-impairment data adequately described additional data; renal function remained major predictor; age-related exposure increase attributed to reduced renal function; no new labeling changes proposed.

structural_features: Mechanism-based model of sugammadex-rocuronium/vecuronium complexation (encapsulation) driving reversal of neuromuscular blockade
notes: No PK study conducted in hepatic impairment (sugammadex is renally eliminated); PK/PD interaction model with rocuronium used to simulate reversal in hepatic impairment via rocuronium PK/PD changes; prolonged recovery time predicted.

structural_features: PK/PD "displacement"/"capturing" interaction model assessing complexation of sugammadex with third-party drugs of high binding affinity (anesthetic drugs, commonly prescribed drugs, steroidal molecules)
notes: Toremifene, flucloxacillin and fusidic acid identified as carrying displacement-interaction risk; capturing-interaction risk for third drugs (e.g., hormonal contraceptives) could not be ruled out; labeling includes cautionary language for steroidal-structure drugs; no CYP-mediated DDI anticipated given limited metabolism/large molecular size.

structural_features: Two-compartment model with first-order absorption (KA); IIV on CL/F, Vc/F, V2/F, KA; IOV on Vc/F; built on pooled healthy-volunteer and gout-patient Phase 1/3 data
notes: CL/F lower in gout patients (6.48 L/h) than healthy subjects (8.31 L/h); IIV substantially higher in patients (63.4% vs 29.8% for CL/F); absolute bioavailability ~100%.

structural_features: Emax model linking lesinurad exposure to change in serum uric acid (sUA), with renal function as covariate
notes: Steep exposure-response for sUA lowering at 200mg qd; renal function is key covariate - at CrCL 30 mL/min only 55% of efficacy preserved, at 60 mL/min 80% preserved; consistent with mechanism (uricosuric transporter inhibition dependent on glomerular filtration).

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Dose-dependent decline in estimated creatinine clearance (eCRCL) observed across all renal-impairment categories, worse in patients with worse baseline renal function; contributed to renal safety labeling/monitoring recommendations.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Lesinurad is CYP2C9 substrate; CYP2C9 poor metabolizers had ~1.8-fold increase in exposure, similar magnitude to co-administration with moderate CYP2C9 inhibitor (fluconazole); consistent usage recommendations applied to both poor metabolizers and CYP2C9-inhibitor co-administration.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: FDA-internal analysis (Study 3003-1) of Day-2 trough concentrations vs. change in SOWS-Gossop withdrawal score; shallow concentration-response relationship, with substantial exposure overlap between 2.4 and 3.2 mg/day doses, supported that 2.4 mg/day dose is adequately effective; no exposure-response relationship found for QTc.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Dedicated intrinsic-factor studies; AUClast increased with severity of both hepatic impairment (mean t1/2 up to 48h in severe vs 14.9h normal) and renal impairment (AUC up to +172% in severe renal impairment); Cmax relatively preserved; supported dose reductions in moderate/severe hepatic and renal impairment.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Exploratory regression analyses (Study 05-04-048) in pediatric PNAC patients found decreases in ALT/AST and triglycerides correlated with decreasing DHA (not EPA) concentrations; no correlation with bilirubin; findings inconclusive due to lag time between exposure and biomarker change. A population-PK approach was recommended by FDA at a pre-IND meeting but not actually conducted/reported.

structural_features: Custom-built PBPK/in-vitro-based model predicting impact of CYP3A inhibitors/inducers on parenterally-administered segesterone acetate (SA) systemic exposure
notes: Applicant used PBPK modeling in lieu of clinical DDI studies (no mass-balance or dedicated human DDI study conducted); FDA reviewer found the model NOT adequate to support labeling and recommended the applicant conduct clinical DDI studies with strong index CYP3A inhibitors/inducers instead; in vitro, CYP3A4 accounts for ~85% of SA metabolic clearance.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Historical implant dose-finding study established SA concentration threshold (~80 pmol/L) below which luteal activity (ovulation) occurred; no luteal activity observed above this concentration, supporting minimum effective contraceptive concentration; no clear exposure-response found for progesterone vs. SA in the ring formulation dataset.

structural_features: Joint parent (revefenacin, 3 disposition compartments tested/2-3-compartment) and metabolite (THRX-195518, 2-compartment) model; fixed first-order absorption, exponential dose-on-bioavailability relationship, block ETA covariance, combined additive+proportional residual error (phase-specific)
fitting_method_software: NONMEM 7.4 (Pirana, R, Xpose4); later reanalysis in Phoenix NLME 8.1
notes: Central Vd 313 L in healthy subjects; sex/age/weight/CrCl not clinically meaningful covariates (within 75-125%); because non-compartmental analysis of dedicated renal/hepatic-impairment studies produced implausibly large extrapolated exposure ratios, a popPK model was built per FDA guidance instead, predicting ~20% increase in renal impairment and ~143% increase in metabolite AUCinf in moderate hepatic impairment, supporting no dosage adjustment for renal impairment but avoidance in hepatic impairment; dose-response for inhaled effectiveness (FEV1) was established separately and is decoupled from systemic exposure.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Standard adult healthy-volunteer PK characterization (compartment-model-independent and -dependent NCA methods) supporting basic PK description.

structural_features: Open 2-compartment model with elimination from central compartment; body-weight allometric scaling on CL and V1
notes: 130 pediatric patients (2-17y)/390 Gd plasma concentrations; body weight was the major covariate (nonlinear relationship), neither age nor gender were additional independent predictors; simulations supported body-weight-based dosing (0.1 mmol/kg) extrapolated from adults to pediatric patients 2-17y.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Dedicated crossover DDI study (TA-011): strong CYP3A4 inhibitor ketoconazole increased avanafil AUC 12.8-fold and Cmax 3.1-fold, informing contraindication/dose-limitation labeling language.

structural_features: Sequential zero- and first-order absorption; weight and sex effects on CL/V; dose effect on bioavailability (F1); renal function, food, and weak-moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor co-administration also evaluated
notes: 10,552 subjects across Phase 1-3; body weight and sex were influential covariates (AUC ~53% higher at 30kg vs 70kg; ~28% lower in males); used to derive individual post-hoc exposures for E-R analysis and support 50mg QD dose selection.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: 5346 subjects (Phase 2b + 3 pivotal Phase 3 trials); higher exposure associated with greater volume voided and reduced micturition frequency but flat E-R for incontinence episodes and for blood pressure safety; doses above 50mg offered no significant additional benefit, supporting 50mg QD.

structural_features: First-order absorption; age, race, site, weight, BMI, albumin, ALT, bilirubin, creatinine, and CLcr tested as covariates with no clinically relevant effect
notes: 7332 concentrations from 1089 subjects (60mg) + 171 subjects (30mg), postmenopausal women; dataset included dedicated hepatic and renal impairment studies as covariate inputs; none of the tested covariates had clinically relevant PK impact.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Pooled 3 pivotal Phase 3 studies; Emax modeling (vaginal maturation index) and logistic regression (moderate-to-severe symptom [MBS] responders) using individual post-hoc PopPK exposures; higher AUC24 associated with better vaginal maturation but flat E-R for MBS; doses >60mg showed no added benefit, supporting the 60mg QD dose.

structural_features: First-order absorption with lag time and linear elimination; model incorporated enterohepatic recycling of bazedoxifene (BZA); separate dense- and sparse-data models
notes: Body weight and ALT associated with higher BZA clearance; reviewer flagged that individual AUC estimates from the sparse-data model (unplanned PK sampling in Study 303) may be unreliable, prompting an independent reviewer reanalysis.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Binomial logistic model of endometrial hyperplasia probability vs. BZA AUC (normalized for formulation bioavailability), CE dose, and weight; found a 30% reduction in BZA exposure was associated with unacceptable loss of endometrial protection, directly supporting the approved BZA dose given the risk of unopposed estrogen effect.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Dedicated crossover DDI studies: CYP1A2 inhibitor fluvoxamine increased tasimelteon AUC 6.5-fold/Cmax 2.5-fold (avoid coadministration); CYP3A4 inducer rifampin decreased exposure ~90% (avoid); mild/moderate hepatic impairment increased AUC 43%/110%; elderly showed ~2-fold higher AUC than young subjects.

structural_features: Multi-compartmental disposition (inhaled long-acting beta-agonist); covariate exposure analysis of pooled Phase 2 dose-ranging PK data using stepwise multivariate linear regression (not a NONMEM mixed-effects population PK model)
notes: Covariate meta-analysis of Phase 2 COPD (1222.5) and asthma (1222.6) dose-ranging PK data (2, 5, 10, 20 ug) found ~2-fold higher olodaterol exposure in Asian vs. Caucasian subjects; dose selection (5 ug and 10 ug QD) was ultimately based on FEV1 dose-response rather than a formal exposure-response model.

structural_features: First-order absorption and elimination; BW as structural covariate on CL/F and V/F in base model; final model covariates BW, age, serum albumin, race, ethnicity, gender on CL/F, BW/age/gender on V/F, population/formulation on F
notes: Analysis based on 2106 subjects (2098 in final dataset) from 3 Phase 1, 1 Phase 2, 2 Phase 3 trials; body weight was the main clinically relevant covariate; supported dosing consistency across body weight range and lyophilized-to-prefilled-syringe formulation bridging.

structural_features: Indirect-response model with 3 sequential PASI transit compartments (ktr), Emax drug effect using post-hoc PK, kin/kout for plaque formation/degradation, forward addition/backward elimination covariate selection
fitting_method_software: NONMEM v7.2 (PK-PD); R v3.2.3 (Emax E-R models)
notes: Combined Phase 2/3 data; Emax model EC50 0.36-0.55 ug/mL for PASI75/90/100; longitudinal PK-PD model with transit compartments supported dose/regimen selection and confirmed adequacy of the approved dosing regimen.

structural_features: Zero-order absorption with lag time, linear elimination; CL/F partitioned into renal (73%) and non-renal (27%) clearance; covariates baseline eGFR (MDRD), baseline ESR, body weight on CL
notes: Model predicted ~2.2-fold AUC increase in moderate renal impairment, consistent with dedicated Study JADL; supported 1 mg dose recommendation for moderate renal impairment in resubmission package.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Pooled ~2200 patients across 5 studies; modeled ACR20/50/70, DAS28-hsCRP, CDAI, SDAI; prior cDMARD-IR status was a significant covariate; supported differential 2 mg vs 4 mg dose selection by subgroup.

structural_features: PBPK model of baricitinib DDI potential with strong OAT3 inhibitors (probenecid) and other perpetrators (e.g., ibuprofen)
notes: FDA found the PBPK analysis inadequate to support DDI labeling claims for strong OAT3 inhibitors because human data confirming the applicant's assumptions were unavailable; flagged as a review deficiency.

structural_features: Linear PK, no evidence of target-mediated elimination; body weight covariate on CL and V; age/gender/race not meaningful after BW correction
notes: Adolescents (N=21) vs adults (N=180): ~37% higher AUCtau,ss in adolescents but no dose adjustment needed; mild/moderate renal impairment (N=98/9) showed no effect on CL or V.

structural_features: Longitudinal exposure-response model relating AUC to monthly HAE attack rate; plateau effect at Month 5-6
notes: Based on Study DX-2930-03; supported 300 mg Q2W starting dose with option to extend to Q4W after 6 months without efficacy loss; exploratory safety E-R found no clear relationship with liver enzymes/hematology parameters.

structural_features: First-order absorption with lag time, linear elimination; covariates prandial state and dose on F/ka, body weight and sex on CL/F and V1/F
fitting_method_software: NONMEM v7.3 (gfortran v4.5.0); PsN v4.2.0 (SCM); R v3.2.2 (post-processing)
notes: 8400 PK observations from 562 subjects across 10 Phase 1 + 2 Phase 3 studies; body weight/sex effects not clinically important; supported 60/100/150 mg tablet dosing.

structural_features: Longitudinal indirect-response model for inflammatory lesion counts (continuous); logistic regression model for binary IGA response
notes: Emax model EC50 = 70.0 mg*h/L for lesion-count reduction; E-R relationship relatively flat within the evaluated dose range; no significant E-R identified for IGA or safety.

structural_features: First-order absorption; full covariate model approach; body weight significant on CL, Vc, Vp (power coefficients 1, 1.25, 0.52); age/sex/smoking status not clinically meaningful
notes: CL estimated at 0.25 L/day, absolute bioavailability 89%; body weight confirmed as important determinant of clearance; supported 150 mg dosing regimen.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: 1389 patients pooled across 90/150/180 mg dose groups; PASI75/90/100 modeled via logistic regression; body weight showed minor effect on PASI90/100 (6-7% higher response in <100 kg patients).

structural_features: First-order absorption (IR formulation); mixed zero/first-order absorption with lag time (ER formulation); linear elimination; significant covariates patient population (RA vs healthy), creatinine clearance, body weight on CL/F, body weight on Vc/F; CYP2D6 genotype tested, no effect
notes: Mild/moderate renal impairment predicted 13%/26% higher AUC (no dose adjustment); no clinically relevant hepatic-impairment effect; ER bioavailability relative to IR estimated at 76%.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Exposure-efficacy simulations (ACR responses, LDA, CR) from Phase 2/3 showed 30 mg QD provided only modest incremental benefit over 15 mg QD, supporting 15 mg QD dose selection.

structural_features: PBPK model bridging clinical DDI effects of CYP3A4 inhibitors/inducers from IR to ER formulation; P-gp/BCRP transporter modulation assessed
notes: PBPK adequately bridged CYP3A4 modulator DDI effects observed with IR formulation to ER formulation, supporting labeling caution with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors and no coadministration with strong inducers.

structural_features: Full PBPK model incorporating high protein binding (>99%) and ontogeny of physiology parameters; verified in adults and pediatric 12-17 yr topical PK data
notes: Model applied to predict systemic exposure in pediatric patients 9-11 years (24%/17% higher Cmax/AUC vs 12-17 yr group) because only 2 subjects in that age band had quantifiable plasma PK in the pediatric MUsT study.

structural_features: Same PBPK model applied to assess trifarotene (victim drug) interaction with fluconazole (moderate CYP2C9/CYP3A4 inhibitor); sensitivity analyses of worst-case Ki/fumic parameter values
notes: CYP2C9 and CYP3A4 together account for 84% of trifarotene metabolism; PBPK supported low DDI potential at clinically relevant exposures despite very low systemic absorption of the topical product.

structural_features: First-order elimination from central compartment with redistribution from peripheral compartment; target-mediated clearance (IGF-1R saturation) noted at high exposure; log-additive residual error
notes: 119 patients (36 oncology, 83 TED) across 3 trials; sex/weight significant on Vc but not clinically meaningful; confirmed 10 mg/kg loading + 20 mg/kg Q3W maintains troughs >20 ug/mL target for >90% target-mediated clearance saturation.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: 83-84 TED patients; no conclusive exposure-efficacy trend (proptosis, diplopia, CAS response) or exposure-safety trend (hyperglycemia, muscle spasm), likely limited by single dosing regimen and small sample size.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Dedicated QT study used supratherapeutic exposures (7.5% solution vs 1% marketed cream) in 32 healthy subjects; concentration-QTc analysis found no significant QTc prolongation (ddQTcF <1 msec at observed Cmax), supporting no QT labeling concern.

structural_features: First-order absorption with lag time, linear elimination; nonlinear bioavailability (dose effect on F); between-study random effect on clearance; body weight only covariate on CL/V
notes: 10,437 PK observations from 771 subjects across 14 studies; ~20% higher exposure in pediatric patients 12-<18 yr vs adults; no clinically meaningful effect of age, renal, or hepatic impairment.

structural_features: Sigmoid Emax PK/PD model linking plasma concentration to ex vivo plasma kallikrein inhibition; separate linear regression of AUCtau vs HAE attack rate
notes: Emax 90.4%, EC50 11.0 ng/mL for kallikrein inhibition; attack-rate correlation with AUCtau only evident in the lower dose range (55-110 mg), supporting selection of 110/150 mg free-base doses for the registration trial.

structural_features: First-order oral absorption, linear elimination; mixture model on Vc/F for a patient subgroup (N=35); covariates BW, ALT, sex, age, race, albumin, bilirubin, eGFR tested; Asian race retained on F
estimation_technique: Likelihood-ratio test model selection; Empirical Bayes estimation
notes: Developed from AURA-LV/AURORA 1 lupus nephritis trials; supported the approved 23.7 mg BID dosing regimen; no dose- or time-dependent nonlinear kinetics found within the evaluated dose range.

structural_features: PBPK model for DDI with CYP3A4 inhibitors/inducers (fluconazole, ketoconazole, diltiazem/verapamil, efavirenz) and OATP1B1/3 substrates (rosuvastatin, pravastatin)
notes: Adequate for CYP3A modulator DDI (e.g., ~70%/62% AUC/Cmax decrease with efavirenz); found inadequate to estimate OATP1B substrate DDI risk (likely underestimated), so clinical monitoring recommended.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Exposure-response analyses across AURA-LV supported safety/effectiveness of 23.7 mg BID; more pronounced eGFR declines observed in South Asian patients, associated with higher total dose.

structural_features: Parallel first-order elimination plus target-mediated drug disposition (TMDD) with quasi-steady-state (QSS) approximation; empirical sigmoidal time-dependent function added to linear CL
notes: 670 subjects (664 SLE, 6 healthy), 6049 concentrations; body weight most significant covariate on CL, followed by type I IFN gene-signature status; no covariate had clinically meaningful impact.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Pooled Phase 3 (studies 04/05); evaluated BICLA, SRI(4), annualized flare rate, and herpes zoster incidence across exposure quartiles in ITT and completer subgroups; supported 300 mg Q4W dose selection.

structural_features: Zero-order input with lag time, linear elimination for parent avacopan and metabolite M1; covariates body weight, ALT, eGFR, health status on CL; body weight, albumin, health status on V
notes: Combined Phase 1/2/3 data; FDA specifically requested a PBPK DDI analysis for moderate/weak CYP3A4 modulators, but the applicant did not perform one (believed clinical data sufficient); review team remained concerned about moderate CYP3A4 inducers.

structural_features: First-order absorption, linear elimination; covariates body weight (CL, Vc, Q, Vp), ICS dose level (CL, Vc), Asian race (CL), formulation (CL), age (Vc)
estimation_technique: Stepwise covariate modeling; Empirical Bayes estimation
notes: 1008 volunteers/asthma patients; body weight was the most influential covariate; adolescents (12-17 yr, N=41) had 32% higher Ctrough,ss than adults, but no dose adjustment needed given flat efficacy/safety E-R relationship.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: NAVIGATOR trial; annualized asthma exacerbation rate (AAER) ratios were consistently <1 across all body weight quartiles despite ~87% Ctrough,ss increase from lowest to highest weight quartile, indicating no clinically relevant body-weight effect on efficacy.

structural_features: First-order absorption and elimination; nonspecific (not target-mediated) elimination via reticuloendothelial system; body weight and trial-type (ECZTRA vs non-ECZTRA) as covariates
notes: Pooled 13,361 concentrations from 2,561 subjects across 10 trials (healthy, asthma, AD); absolute bioavailability 76%; no clinically significant differences by renal/hepatic impairment or age.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Positive E-R relationships observed for EASI-75 and IGA 0/1; body weight was not a significant covariate on efficacy, though an exploratory subgroup analysis suggested >100 kg patients may benefit more from Q2W vs Q4W maintenance dosing.

structural_features: Parallel first-order and zero-order absorption processes, linear elimination; allometric body-weight scaling on CL/Q (exponent 0.453) and Vc/Vp (exponent 0.52); covariates sex, age, race, hepatic function, DDI, fed status
notes: 7795 PK observations from 995 subjects across 11 Phase 1-3 studies; renal excretion is a major elimination route but creatinine clearance not evaluated as covariate (mostly normal renal function).

structural_features: Drug-induced platelet reduction described by tachyphylactic Emax function on platelet proliferation feeding into 3 transit (maturation) compartments (mean transit time 7.21 days), analogous to a myelosuppression turnover model
notes: 12,189 PD observations from 2333 subjects; baseline platelet count included as covariate via power model on Emax; characterized nadir occurring at Week 4.

structural_features: Longitudinal indirect-response model for EASI score: linear combination of Emax function (drug effect on Kout) and open-label placebo effect
notes: 11,951 PD observations from 2273 subjects across 1 Phase 2 + 3 Phase 3 studies; time-course of EASI reduction well characterized, supporting efficacy dose-response conclusions.

structural_features: Longitudinal logistic regression model for probability of IGA response; time-dependent placebo effect and Emax drug effect
notes: Age, sex, Asian race, baseline IGA score identified as covariates; younger age and Asian race associated with lower Emax; strong exposure-response relationship confirmed for IGA response probability.

structural_features: Sequential zero-order then first-order absorption (SC dosing); parallel linear and nonlinear (Michaelis-Menten-type) clearance affected by anti-drug antibody (ADA) titer
notes: Pooled data from healthy subjects and GPP/UC/AD patients (4086 observations, 196 subjects); high maximum ADA titer (>3600) associated with ~50% AUC decrease; lighter body weight associated with higher AUC.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: 53 GPP patients from Study 1368-0013 (single 900 mg IV dose); logistic regression for binary GPPGA pustulation endpoints and linear regression for continuous GPPGA score supported the single 900 mg IV dosing regimen.

structural_features: Sequential zero-order input plus first-order absorption with lag time, linear elimination; parent drug and active metabolite (BMT-153261) modeled sequentially; covariates included organ impairment status, eGFR, Child-Pugh
notes: 1388 subjects, 18,781 PK samples; PK comparable between healthy subjects and psoriasis patients; supported no dose adjustment in mild-to-severe renal or hepatic impairment.

structural_features: Longitudinal multilevel logistic regression combining placebo effect and drug effect (Emax function of Cavgss and time) on log-odds scale, for PASI/sPGA efficacy; separate model for infection/infestation safety events
notes: 1524 patients across Phase 2/3 (IM011011, IM011046, IM011047); 50% lower exposure predicted ~9% decrease in PASI75 and ~6% decrease in sPGA0/1; supported no dose adjustment for specific populations at 6 mg QD.

structural_features: Absorption lag time, first-order absorption, first-order elimination; body weight effect on Vc/F and Vp/F (power exponent 0.662); Japanese race effect on CL/F; separate 1-compartment model used for APDS PK/PD linkage
notes: 118 healthy participants (2803 concentrations, Study 2101) for 2-compartment model; APDS PK from Study 2201 Part 1 (1-compartment) showed consistent parameters, supporting cross-population PK similarity.

structural_features: Emax concentration-response model linking leniolisib plasma concentration to ex vivo %pAkt-positive B-cell inhibition (direct downstream PI3Kdelta pathway marker)
notes: Doses of 10/30/70 mg BID predicted to achieve ED50/ED70/ED90 of pAkt inhibition at 15/35/70 mg BID; supported selection of the 70 mg BID approved dose in APDS patients.

structural_features: PBPK model for DDI with typical CYP3A4 perpetrators (itraconazole, erythromycin, rifampin, efavirenz) and victim assessment for midazolam; CYP1A1-mediated metabolism component
notes: Adequate to predict single-dose leniolisib PK and CYP3A4 DDI direction; found inadequate to accurately predict magnitude of interaction effects and hepatic-impairment PK (no clinical data for verification); recommended avoiding strong CYP3A4 inhibitors/inducers.

structural_features: Zero-order input with lag time (implied absorption complexity), linear elimination; allometric scaling on CL/F and Q/F, Vc/F
fitting_method_software: NONMEM v7.5.0 (also earlier version VII Level 5.0); PsN v5.2.6
notes: Iteratively developed population PK model across multiple studies as data accrued; used as backbone for downstream PK/PD analyses.

structural_features: Bounded-outcome-score (Aranda-Ordaz transform) nonlinear mixed-effects model for longitudinal SALT (Severity of Alopecia Tool) score, with censoring at 0/100 boundaries
fitting_method_software: NONMEM v7.5.0; R v4.0.3; PsN v5.2.6
fitting_algorithm: Laplace estimation with interaction (SAEM with IMP)
notes: Modeled continuous efficacy (SALT score) longitudinally to characterize dose-response for alopecia areata; supported labeling/dosing conclusions on time-course of hair regrowth.

structural_features: Friberg-type transit-compartment turnover model (proliferation compartment + 3 maturation/transit compartments) with feedback mechanism, describing ritlecitinib-induced lymphopenia
notes: Simulated probability of Grade 1-4 lymphopenia and nadir timing; stratified lymphocyte change from baseline by age for 50 mg daily dosing; supported safety monitoring conclusions rather than dose change.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Used population-PK-derived individual exposure metrics to evaluate concentration-response for infections, herpes zoster, and rash; statistically significant E-R relationship found for infections and rash but not for herpes zoster.

structural_features: First-in-human IV and SC bioavailability/bridging studies pooled; covariates body weight and anti-drug antibody (ADAb/NAb) status on CL/F
notes: Body weight was the principal covariate on exposure; anti-BKZ neutralizing antibody (NAb) positivity reduced plasma concentrations more than binding-antibody (ADAb) positivity; accumulation ratio ~1.74 for Q4W dosing.

structural_features: Indirect-response model for IGA: mono-exponential placebo effect (PLmax, PLhalf) plus Emax stimulation of Kin; Markov element linking prior visit's IGA score to current-visit probability
notes: Covariates: baseline IGA score on Kout, baseline weight and Asian/Japanese race on EC50; supported 320 mg Q4W/Q8W dosing regimen selection at end of Phase 2b.

structural_features: Analogous indirect-response/Emax PK-PD model for PASI response, incorporating baseline PASI and age effects on onset of treatment effect
notes: Simulations from this model showed Q8W regimen maintains PASI90 response in the majority of patients, while Q12W would lead to more patients losing response; directly informed the approved Q4W->Q8W regimen.

structural_features: Two-compartment PK model with target-mediated drug disposition (TMDD) - clearance driven by IFNgamma production; PK-PD-disease network (IFNgamma, CXCL9, CXCL10, sIL2R, ferritin); indirect response model where emapalumab neutralizes IFNgamma stimulation of CXCL9 production via inhibitory Emax model
notes: n=49 patients (2414 PK records) for popPK, n=47 (1110 records) for popPK/PD; only body weight and total IFNgamma concentration were significant PK covariates; emapalumab half-life varied 2.5-19 days depending on IFNgamma/disease severity; supported twice-weekly dosing regimen.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Univariate/multivariate logistic regression identified CXCL9, IFNgamma, CXCL10 (biomarkers, not drug concentration) as prognostic for clinical response at EOT; ROC analysis found CXCL9 threshold of 292 pg/mL (EOT) / 465 pg/mL (week 2) discriminated responders; safety exposure-response showed no clear trend for AEs vs. emapalumab concentration; relationship between emapalumab exposure and efficacy was confounded by dose titration and TMDD.

structural_features: Two-compartment model with first-order processes, fixed F1=1 and KA=0.535/hr; exponential IIV on CL and V2 with correlation; additive+proportional residual error; covariate search via SCM in PsN
notes: n=963 subjects, 4632 PK samples pooled from 2 Phase 1, 1 Phase 2b, 2 Phase 3 studies; significant covariates: eGFR, weight, injection site/study group on CL and V2/F.

structural_features: Ordered-categorical (proportional-odds/logit) PK/PD models for FSFI Q1, Q2 domains and FSDS-DAO distress item vs. model-predicted average concentration; separate BP model linking double-delta SBP/DBP to peripheral-compartment concentration with circadian-rhythm and device-effect terms
notes: Overall exposure-response for FSFI Q1/Q2 was flat/weak (no clear efficacy exposure-response, no body-weight trend); FSDS ordered-categorical model showed higher concentration associated with higher probability of achieving lower distress scores; blood-pressure model showed a clear drug effect on BP linked to peripheral-compartment concentration, supporting the hypertension safety signal.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Dedicated Study BMT-115 (renal impairment): AUC0-inf increased 1.2-/1.5-/2-fold in mild/moderate/severe renal impairment; more AEs (nausea/vomiting) in severe renal impairment. Dedicated Study BMT-116 (hepatic impairment): modest Cmax/AUC increases (1.3-/1.7-fold) in moderate hepatic impairment; no PK data in severe hepatic impairment.

structural_features: Three-compartment model with body weight as fixed covariate on clearances/volumes; clearance also related to standardized renal function; distinct clearance/inter-compartmental clearance for surgical (general-anesthesia) patients vs. healthy subjects; ~25% non-renal clearance component identified but not reliably estimable so model conservatively assumed all clearance renal
notes: Final popPK dataset n=104 surgical patients; model used to simulate Cmax after short infusion durations (1, 2, 4 min) of the 10-mg dose (N=1000 simulated subjects/regimen) to inform safe infusion-duration labeling; modestly lower clearance in surgical patients (20.6 vs 24.1 L/hr for 70kg subject) not considered clinically relevant.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Concentration-QT (C-QT) analysis using a non-linear Emax model (from thorough QT study DP10013 and confirmed in Study DP10022) predicted ddQTcF of ~13.4 ms at Tmax for a 10-mg 1-minute IV infusion, informing recommendation for a longer infusion duration to reduce peak concentration and QT risk.

structural_features: Three-compartment model, pooled across bolus (procedural sedation) and continuous-infusion (general anesthesia) dosing data; earlier physiologic recirculation models (assuming lung metabolism) were abandoned after in vitro data showed lung metabolism is much slower than hepatic
notes: Pooled analysis of 11 clinical trials, n=359 subjects (126 healthy, 193 procedural sedation, 40 anesthesia); CL 9.7% higher in females, 13% lower in African Americans (also 16% lower Vss); age/ASA class/BMI/eGFR/CrCL had no effect; race/body-weight findings led sponsor to use fixed-dose rather than weight-based bolus dosing.

structural_features: Concentration-effect (effect-compartment/indirect) model relating plasma remimazolam concentration to sedation depth (MOAA/S score), including simulated time-to-peak-effect
notes: MOAA/S score decreased as plasma concentration increased; effect-site concentrations of ~1779 ng/mL corresponded to MOAA/S=0 (deep sedation) down to ~341 ng/mL for MOAA/S<=4; onset of sedation fast (1-2 min).

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: PK not altered by renal impairment (including ESRD, not requiring dialysis) - no dose adjustment needed. Hepatic impairment: Cmax not significantly changed but t1/2 of unbound drug prolonged with severity (42.9 min healthy -> 59.2 min moderate -> 105 min severe HI), increasing sedation/recovery time; severe hepatic impairment requires careful titration.

structural_features: Three-compartment serial model with first-order plus saturable (Michaelis-Menten, Vmax/Km) clearance; saturable pathway turned off in CYP2D6 poor metabolizers; fixed allometric exponents on body weight for all CL/V terms; full covariate model with gender effect
notes: n=362 subjects from 6 Phase 1/2 studies; itraconazole (CYP3A4/P-gp inhibitor) reduced first-order clearance by 44.8%; females had lower CL (-13.3%), V1 (-36.7%), Q2 (-35.1%) after weight correction; age/race not meaningful covariates.

structural_features: Indirect response model linking individual predicted plasma concentration (from final popPK model) to continuous pain-score endpoint, with separate time-effect and drug-effect (Emax/EC50) terms
notes: Study CP130-2001: n=265 (51 placebo + 214 active) used for E-R parameter estimation; indirect response model (rather than effect-compartment) selected because time- and drug-effects entered similarly; used together with Study 2002 results to select the Phase 3 PCA loading/demand-dose regimen.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Dedicated hepatic impairment study (n=34, incl. 6 severe): Cmax/AUC comparable in mild/moderate HI but ~4-fold lower Cmax in severe HI (altered protein binding/distribution, Vz increased 126->348 L); dedicated renal impairment study (incl. ESRD) showed no clinically relevant PK changes; no dose adjustment needed for renal impairment; loading-dose reduction considered for severe hepatic impairment.

structural_features: Three-compartment model with one saturable (capacity-limited, Bmax/Km) peripheral distribution compartment plus linear elimination; transit-compartment absorption model (Ntr, ktr) with nonlinear dose-dependent bioavailability; IIV on CL, V2, mean transit time, Bmax
notes: Pooled 10 studies, n=1179 subjects/9799 observations, doses 2-600mg; retained covariates: weight on CL/V2, age on Bmax, eGFR on CL, OAB-status on CL; simulated AUC 42.7% higher in severe renal impairment (eGFR 15-30) vs. mildly decreased; elderly (>80y) and OAB-status effects not clinically relevant; underweight (<60kg) subjects had 71%/31% higher Cmax/AUCtau.

structural_features: Generalized Poisson (micturition frequency) and Poisson (urgency incontinence, strong urgency) count models linking simulated 24-hr trough concentration (C24h) to efficacy endpoints
notes: Study P008 Phase 2 PK-PD modeling of MF/UUI/SU informed Phase 3 dose selection; 3mg data showed inconsistent exposure-response gradient in rest-of-world dataset (excluded) but consistent gradient in Japanese dataset (included); model could not extrapolate above 100mg dose.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: No dedicated PK studies for renal/hepatic impairment or DDI were conducted for the DRSP/E4 combination; DDI conclusions bridged from reference product Yaz (DRSP/EE) label and published literature - DRSP is a CYP3A substrate; strong/weak CYP3A inducers decrease DRSP exposure (reduced contraceptive effectiveness risk); strong CYP3A4 inhibitor (ketoconazole, per Yaz label) increases serum potassium risk; E4 component not metabolized by CYP3A and does not inhibit/induce major CYPs in vitro.

structural_features: Three-compartment disposition model with linear clearance (IV dosing); separate IV-oral model adds sequential zero-order/first-order absorption (D1, Ka, F1); full covariate approach: body weight on all CL/V terms, age/AST/bilirubin on CL, MDRD (renal function) on CL and V
notes: Model-based covariate/forest-plot analysis showed normal/mild/moderate/severe renal impairment had significantly different AUC vs. reference hemodialysis patient, while age (25-80y) and mild/moderate hepatic impairment were within reference range; hemodialysis itself reduces plasma concentrations 70-80% and drug is undetectable after 2 dialysis sessions; entire indicated population is dialysis-dependent ESRD, so renal-impairment characterization is central to the whole program.

structural_features: Two-compartment model; allometric scaling with fixed exponents (0.75 on CL/Q, 1 on V1/V2) for body weight; distinct functional forms for eGFR-clearance relationship in adults (sigmoidal/asymptotic Hill-type function) vs. pediatrics (power function), reflecting different eGFR equations (CKD-EPI vs. Schwartz)
notes: Pooled healthy-volunteer and pediatric (2-17y) and renal-impairment (Study GDX-44-005) data; used to characterize/extrapolate exposure across pediatric ages and renal function without requiring separate full studies in every subgroup.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Thorough QT study (crossover, n=48) found linear concentration-dependent increase in dQTcF (slope 0.0011 msec per ug/mL); predicted ddQTcF of only 2.23 (upper CI 3.26) msec at supratherapeutic dose Cmax, well below regulatory threshold of concern; no clinically significant QT signal.

structural_features: Two-compartment model with first-order absorption; IIV on CL, V2, Q, V3, Ka with full covariance matrix; IOV on F1 (relative bioavailability)
notes: Pooled n=1036/1070 subjects (healthy + moderate/severe COPD) across 10 studies; significant covariates: disease state (COPD vs. non-COPD, ~35% lower F1) and moderate renal impairment (25.1% reduced clearance, n=95); body weight/age/sex/race/hepatic enzymes not significant; renal-impairment exposure increase not considered clinically relevant given high inter-subject variability and limited renal clearance.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Dedicated Study RPL554-PK-103: Cmax/AUCinf ~2.3-fold and ~2.2-fold higher in moderate hepatic impairment vs. healthy controls; ~1.2-fold/2.3-fold higher in severe hepatic impairment; no dose adjustment proposed but label recommends caution in hepatic impairment.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Dedicated Study RPL554-PK-102 evaluated fluconazole (CYP2C9 inhibitor) effect on ensifentrine PK via statistical DDI evaluation.

structural_features: Linear 3-compartment model (ADVAN11 TRANS4) with elimination from central compartment; allometric scaling (weight/72.25)^0.75 on intercompartmental clearances Q2/Q3, (weight/72.25)^1 on volumes V1/V2/V3; CrCL and healthy-volunteer status included as covariates on CL
notes: N=90 (72 patients, 18 healthy volunteers) pooled across studies; model used to simulate pediatric doses achieving adult-comparable exposure; CrCL and healthy-volunteer status were significant covariates on clearance.

structural_features: SUZ disposition: 2-compartment with zero-order depot entry, first-order absorption (dose-dependent Ka/F1; separate absorption model for abdominoplasty subjects), parallel linear clearance; active metabolite M6-SUZ: separate 2-compartment model formed irreversibly from parent, with autoinduction of metabolite clearance
notes: N=1435 subjects pooled across healthy/abdominoplasty/bunionectomy studies; model informed dose selection incl. modified regimen for moderate hepatic impairment and missed-dose scenarios via simulation.

structural_features: Minimal PBPK model for SUZ/M6-SUZ with mechanistic absorption; simulated DDI with strong/moderate/weak CYP3A inhibitors and inducers
notes: FDA's independent PBPK review reproduced predicted exposure ratios for CYP3A modulators (e.g., efavirenz induction, moderate/weak inhibitors); supported labeling without dedicated clinical DDI trials for weak/moderate perpetrators.

structural_features: Power model relating SPID48 (pain relief endpoint) to combined SUZ+M6-SUZ average concentration; linear/power/sigmoidal forms tested
notes: N=1725 subjects (abdominoplasty + bunionectomy pooled); baseline pain score was the only clinically relevant covariate; supported the 100 mg/50 mg q12h dose as achieving near-maximal, consistent response.

structural_features: Oral depot compartment with dose-dependent relative bioavailability, 3-compartment absorption transit chain, separate Ka for fed/fasted states, 2 systemic compartments with linear elimination
fitting_method_software: NONMEM v7.4.4; PsN v4.7.0; Pirana v2.9.9
analysis_goal: Drug-drug interaction (DDI) risk prediction; Dose/regimen selection
notes: Significant covariates: dose, verapamil/clarithromycin (DDI, on bioavailability and CL), body weight, sex, race, Child-Pugh class, rifampin; supported marketing both 10 mg and 25 mg QD doses.

structural_features: Threshold/quartile comparison of steady-state AUCtau vs annualized pulmonary exacerbation rate and FEV1 (efficacy); multivariable logistic regression of AUC24 vs hyperkeratosis (safety)
notes: Efficacy E-R limited by missing PK data in ~50% of Study 301 subjects, results inconsistent with observed efficacy; safety analysis found AUC24 significantly associated with hyperkeratosis incidence.

structural_features: Mechanistic absorption model plus minimal PBPK model with single-adjusting compartment; brensocatib evaluated as a CYP3A4 perpetrator toward midazolam
notes: Predicted low likelihood of clinically relevant DDI of brensocatib as CYP3A4 perpetrator on midazolam (weak inducer, not inhibitor of other CYPs tested).

structural_features: Sequential zero- and first-order absorption with linear elimination; joint modeling of R- and S-enantiomer mixture
notes: Covariates age, weight, AST/ALT/bilirubin, eGFR, sex, race, formulation evaluated; no dose adjustment found necessary based on these factors.

structural_features: Longitudinal disease-progression model of FVC decline with an initial-offset parameter plus a disease-modifying slope parameter, driven by Cmin,ss
notes: 18 mg dose showed superior efficacy vs 9 mg (~14 mL greater placebo-adjusted FVC at Week 52); model showed reduced efficacy at 9 mg when co-administered with pirfenidone, resolved by escalation to 18 mg.

structural_features: Logistic regression models of AEs (diarrhea: Emax exposure-response form; weight loss >=5%: linear form; infection and nausea: linear form) vs Cmin,ss/AUC,ss
notes: N=963 subjects; probability of diarrhea and weight loss increased with exposure; no meaningful exposure-response relationship found for nausea.

structural_features: Static mechanistic (basic/R-value) DDI risk model as a CYP/UGT-enzyme and transporter perpetrator, using in vitro Ki and reversible/time-dependent inhibition parameters
notes: Static DDI risk assessment at steady state for nerandomilast 18 mg BID indicated low in vivo inhibition potential across all CYP and UGT isoforms evaluated.

structural_features: 1-compartment PK with first-order absorption/elimination linked to an indirect-response (inhibition of kin) model for blood eosinophil count
analysis_goal: Extrapolation to new population; Dose/regimen selection
notes: Covariates: baseline eosinophils, CRSwNP vs asthma population, age, weight, Asian race on Emax/EC50; adolescent PK/PD predicted via NHANES-based virtual population (N=15), comparable to adult empirical Bayes estimates (N=479), supporting pediatric extrapolation.

structural_features: Negative binomial generalized linear model relating PK/PD metrics (AUCtau,ss, Ctrough, blood eosinophil count) to annualized asthma exacerbation rate
notes: N=742 (486 depemokimab/256 placebo); analysis considered exploratory due to narrow (single dose level) exposure range; no clear exposure-response relationship found for exacerbation-rate reduction.

structural_features: Linear 2-compartment model with first-order absorption/lag; dual-depot absorption structure to capture double concentration peaks in the fasted food-effect study; 2 metabolites formed independently via first-order process from the central compartment, with optional peripheral distribution
notes: N=1206 unique subjects pooled across 7 trials; model intended to bridge/reconstruct expected parent and metabolite exposures in motion-sickness subjects for safety assessment, but FDA found the updated model's parameter estimates unreliable (non-convergence, unreliable dosing history, failure to recapitulate the previously observed food effect); mild-moderate renal impairment showed no clinically meaningful CL/F difference.

structural_features: 3-compartment infusion model with first-order elimination from the central compartment; parameterized as CL, V1, Q2/V2, Q3/V3
notes: N not stated explicitly in extracted narrative; body weight, sex, race and age were significant covariates on clearance/volume; dose adjustment supported for age >=65y, ASA-PS III, or BMI >40 kg/m2. A companion PopPK/exposure-response report linking PK to BIS/MOAA-S sedation depth was referenced repeatedly but detailed quantitative results were not extractable as text from this PDF (tables/figures only).

structural_features: Adult base model: 3-compartment with linear elimination from central compartment, lean-body-mass scaling on CL/V1/Q2/V2, eGFR added on central clearance
notes: Adult population PK model for a gadolinium-based MRI contrast agent; age, sex, and health status also visually associated with CL/V1 but not formally retained.

structural_features: Pediatric model reduced from the adult 3-compartment model (3rd peripheral-compartment parameters estimated near zero; adult structure did not converge in pediatric data); lean-body-mass scaling retained on CL/V1/Q2/V2; maturation factor (using post-menstrual age) added to CL to capture renal ontogeny
notes: N=93 pediatric participants (0 to <18 years), single 0.04 mmol Gd/kg IV dose; maturation factor accounted for kidney function maturing ~2 years post-birth.

structural_features: 2-compartment model with first-order absorption and Michaelis-Menten (nonlinear/target-mediated) elimination; intercompartmental clearance fixed to improve model stability
fitting_algorithm: Not stated (GAM covariate screening + stepwise selection)
notes: N=672 subjects, 2665 concentrations; significant covariates ethnicity, total bilirubin, age, BMI, creatinine, alkaline phosphatase; results supported recommending a lower starting dose (0.04 mg/kg vs 0.08 mg/kg).

structural_features: 1-compartment model with allometric function of body weight on CL and V; renal (CLr) and non-renal (CLnr) clearance parameterized separately; maturation function added to renal clearance for pediatric extrapolation
analysis_goal: Extrapolation to new population; Dose/regimen selection
notes: N=83 subjects (incl. 2 pediatric, ESRD/severe renal impairment, healthy volunteers); ALT and CrCL were significant covariates on non-renal/renal clearance respectively; simulations supported dosing across pediatric age cohorts. A formal exposure-response analysis was NOT conducted (insufficient PK data).

structural_features: One- and two-compartment structures were tested with first-order absorption (+/- lag time); final selected structure not specified in extracted narrative text (parameter table was image-only)
notes: N=141 patients, 1814 plasma concentrations from 3 trials (BH29884, BH29992, ACE001JP/ACE002JP); stepwise covariate screening performed; FDA judged the model acceptable.

structural_features: Linear regression of annualized bleeding rate (ABR) vs average concentration; logistic regression of probability of ABR=0 vs average concentration
notes: Positive exposure-efficacy relationship identified at the 1.5 mg/kg/week maintenance dose; analyses based on N=83 (patients treated >=12 weeks) and N=52 (>=24 weeks).

structural_features: Structural model developed in healthy subjects/RA patients (N=2413), then refit to ITP patients with structural parameters fixed except inter-individual variability terms; allometric CL/V exponents of 0.662/1.23 on body weight
analysis_goal: Extrapolation to new population; Dose/regimen selection
pk_exposure_metric: AUC (daily AUC at steady state, DAUCss)
notes: Refit dataset N=113 ITP patients; weight-based dosing judged not practically beneficial since dose was already titrated by clinical response (platelet count).

structural_features: Logistic regression of DAUCss vs probability of platelet response (>=50,000/uL increase) at Week 12 (efficacy); Emax model of R406 concentration vs systolic/diastolic blood pressure (safety)
notes: Efficacy analysis N=79 ITP patients (higher exposure associated with Week-12 response, not later timepoints); safety analysis N=2435 (RA+ITP pooled), BP Emax ~10 mmHg with EC50 ~16,300-17,000 ng*hr/mL; liver enzymes/ANC not meaningfully exposure-related.

structural_features: 6-compartment PK/PD "lifespan" model: 2 PK compartments plus 4 PD compartments (1 precursor-production + 2 transit/maturation + 1 platelet compartment) with a linear drug-effect slope on platelet production rate
analysis_goal: Dose/regimen selection; Drug-drug interaction (DDI) risk prediction
notes: N=394 subjects with chronic liver disease; FDA simulated 273 subjects x200 replicates using PBPK-predicted concentrations as PK/PD model input to evaluate dose adjustments for concomitant CYP modulators.

structural_features: Full PBPK model with mechanistic oral absorption; retrograde-calculated CYP2C9-mediated hepatic clearance; used to predict DDI with CYP2C9/CYP3A4 modulators (itraconazole, rifampicin, verapamil, sulfaphenazole)
notes: 6 candidate PBPK models evaluated; final model predicted AUC increases of 20-50% (and up to 2.2-fold) with strong CYP2C9/3A4 inhibitors, feeding into the linked PK/PD model to simulate resulting platelet-count risk.

structural_features: 3-compartment PK (absorption lag time, first-order elimination) with allometric weight scaling on CL/F and V, linked via a linear drug-effect slope to a platelet-precursor turnover model (KPR/KM/KL rate constants, 4 precursor/platelet compartments)
pk_exposure_metric: Peak platelet count (PD metric; PK metric not separately named)
notes: N=427 subjects (78 healthy, 349 chronic-liver-disease patients); 200-replicate simulations informed a platelet-count-based dose-stopping rule; Japanese ethnicity and female sex reduced CL/F ~13% each; chronic liver disease reduced CL ~13.5%.

structural_features: Population PK model (body-weight-tiered dosing) linked to an exposure-response relationship for terminal complement (free C5) inhibition and LDH normalization
notes: PK/PD simulations conducted before Phase 3 to select weight-tiered dosing; body weight was the only clinically significant covariate; Ctrough > 175 ug/mL threshold associated with near-maximal LDH-lowering effect; concomitant-medication classes assessed as covariates on the base Pop-PK model showed no impact on exposure.

structural_features: 2-compartment model with first-order absorption (ka with lag time) and linear elimination; non-zero covariance IIV on CL/F, V2/F, ka
analysis_goal: Dose/regimen selection; Drug-drug interaction (DDI) risk prediction
notes: N=456 patients; covariates polycythemia-vera disease status, body weight, creatinine clearance, and dose on CL/F and V2/F; no dose adjustment needed for mild-moderate renal/hepatic impairment; formulation not a significant covariate.

structural_features: Minimal PBPK model with first-order absorption; retrograde-estimated CYP3A4/2C19/2D6 intrinsic clearance; used to predict DDI with CYP3A4/2C19 modulators
notes: Model-predicted fractional metabolism ~72% CYP3A4, 11% CYP2C19, 1.4% CYP2D6; supported dose reduction to 200 mg QD with strong CYP3A inhibitors and avoidance of dual CYP2C19/3A4 inhibitors.

structural_features: Logistic regression models of AUC0-24,ss vs Grade>=3 anemia/thrombocytopenia, diarrhea, nausea/vomiting, SAEs, and treatment discontinuation/dose reduction
notes: N=404 patients (4 phase 2 studies + 1 phase 3 study); increasing exposure associated with higher probability of most AEs except dose interruption; baseline hemoglobin/platelet count also contributed; exploratory CYP3A4-genotype subgroup E-R limited by small sample size.

structural_features: 1-compartment model with first-order absorption (ka) and linear elimination; block-omega IIV on CL/F and V/F
notes: Weight, albumin, and baseline transfusion burden were significant covariates on CL/F and V/F; mild-moderate renal/hepatic impairment, race, and manufacturing-process/formulation differences had no clinically meaningful effect.

structural_features: Graphical/regression analysis of AUCavg15 vs probability of >=33% reduction in RBC transfusion burden (efficacy) and vs Grade>=3 TEAEs (safety)
notes: Efficacy N=249 (confounded by response-based dose titration and narrow exposure range, no clear trend); safety N=372, statistically significant (p=0.03) inverse relationship between AUCavg and Grade>=3 TEAEs.

structural_features: Mechanistic indirect-response model: liver PK of active siRNA (givosiran + AS(N-1)3' metabolite), with parameters allometrically scaled from a nonclinical rat PK/PD model, driving RISC-loading kinetics and an Imax model of ALAS1 mRNA-mediated inhibition of urinary ALA synthesis; additive hemin inhibitory effect included for acute hepatic porphyria (AHP) patients
notes: N=125 subjects (111 AHP, 14 compensated hepatic erythropoietic porphyria patients) for the population PK component; weight and eGFR were significant PK covariates; the PK/PD model's IC50/Imax parameters were bridged from rat liver PK/PD data to predict human RISC loading and urinary ALA suppression.

structural_features: 2-compartment model (plasma) with first-order absorption/elimination coupled to an effect compartment for whole blood (whole-blood:plasma partitioning link)
notes: N=245 patients (1848 plasma + 1869 whole-blood concentrations); significant covariates baseline albumin (CL/F), blood volume (V/F), baseline Hb/dose/hematocrit (blood:plasma ratio); no age/race/sex effect found.

structural_features: Graphical exposure-efficacy analysis: change from baseline hemoglobin at Week 24 and hemolysis markers (reticulocytes, indirect bilirubin, LDH) vs whole-blood concentration
notes: N=238 patients (204 adult + 34 adolescent); the 1500 mg dose exceeded the 1 g/dL Hb-improvement threshold whereas 900 mg did not.

structural_features: Logistic regression of plasma Cmax/AUC vs probability of increased ALT, decreased WBC, and diarrhea (Grade>=1 AEs)
notes: No relationship found between exposure and SCD-related Grade>=2 AEs (vaso-occlusive crises, acute chest syndrome, pneumonia).

structural_features: PBPK model verified to predict voxelotor PK in healthy subjects/SCD patients and DDI with midazolam, caffeine, ketoconazole, and rifampicin
notes: Default Simcyp compound files used without modification for perpetrator/victim DDI predictions across CYP1A2/2B6/2C19/3A4 substrates and inhibitors/inducers.

structural_features: 1-compartment disposition with a transit absorption compartment for SC dosing (IV dose enters central compartment directly); first-order elimination; C3 level and PNH-study-phase covariate on CL/V2
notes: Included subjects with moderate/severe renal impairment from a dedicated Phase 1 study; simulated SC-infusion dose-delivery error (+/-10-15%) did not meaningfully impact steady-state LDH.

structural_features: Direct-response PK/PD model relating pegcetacoplan concentration to hemoglobin and LDH response (an indirect-response/turnover model was attempted but gave poor precision for the Hb turnover rate, so the simpler direct-response model was retained)
notes: Steady-state concentrations at the proposed 1,080 mg BIW dose predicted to provide maximal Hb response regardless of prior eculizumab treatment experience.

structural_features: First-order absorption with lag time; formulation (tablet vs capsule) effect on Ka and lag time
notes: PopPK model from 5 Phase 1 studies (174 healthy subjects) and 2 Phase 2 studies (178 cGVHD subjects, total N=352); cGVHD status and fed state affected CL/F; supported no dose adjustment for age, body size, renal function.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Post-hoc exposure-efficacy (overall response, duration of response, LSS/GSR scores) and exposure-safety (headache, fatigue, LFTs, nausea, diarrhea) analyses from Studies KD025-208/213 were flat across observed exposure range, supporting 200 mg QD with no exposure-driven dose adjustment.

structural_features: Minimal PBPK distribution model with first-order absorption/elimination for belumosudil and metabolite M2
notes: PBPK model adequate to show minimal DDI as victim of moderate CYP3A inhibitors/inducers and as perpetrator on CYP2C9/CYP3A/CYP2C8 (non-OATP1B substrates); inadequate to rule out effects on P-gp, BCRP, OATP1B1, MATE1/2K substrates.

structural_features: Target-mediated drug disposition (TMDD) model (Kdec, KD, Kint, Rtot0, Rtotss) plus first-order absorption compartment with lag time; exponential IIV, combined additive+proportional residual error
notes: Final model from 3 studies, 1538 PK observations/200 subjects; BSA and JAK2 V617F allele burden covariates on CL/F, healthy-vs-GVHD status on Vc, age on Ka; body weight/allele burden effects deemed not clinically impactful given individualized titration.

structural_features: Longitudinal indirect-response (Imax) model linking concentration to HCT/PLT/WBC decline, plus separate Emax model with effect compartment for probability of complete hematologic response (CHR/CHRP)
notes: Pooled data from PEGINVERA and PROUD-PV/CONTINUATION-PV; IC50 values for HCT/PLT/WBC Imax models were at/below 5th percentile of observed concentrations, indicating selected dose achieves plateau response; Emax model predicted 30-55% probability of CHR/CHRP at AUC range 50-550 h*ng/mL.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Linear logistic regression of post-hoc Cmin vs probability of thrombocytopenia and GGT elevation, pooled from PEGINVERA/PROUD-PV/PEN-PV/CONTINUATION-PV; significant relationships identified but effects tolerable and did not lead to discontinuation.

structural_features: Parallel linear and nonlinear (Michaelis-Menten) clearance; allometric scaling of CL (exponent 1.72) and Vc (exponent 0.52) by body weight
notes: 4 studies, N combining healthy subjects and CAD patients; body weight and Japanese ethnicity were significant covariates on CL/Vc/Vmax; supported two-tier weight-based fixed dosing regimen.

structural_features: Indirect longitudinal Emax model for hemoglobin response vs time, sex-specific Emax
notes: Time-matched Emax model (n=24 CARDINAL + 9 BIVV009-01C) estimated Emax 2.7 g/dL Hgb increase, EC50 192 ug/mL, with steady-state Cmin values in all CARDINAL patients above EC50, supporting saturated response at proposed dose; longitudinal model estimated t50 of 7.4 days.

structural_features: First-order absorption; time- and dose-dependent clearance (autoinduction) modeled as exponential increase to steady state
notes: 186 healthy subjects + 155 PKD patients, 4686/4913 samples from 341 subjects in final model; characterized autoinduction of clearance after multiple dosing.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Safety E-R in 155 patients: no signal for ALT/AST/triglycerides/DXA; significant exposure-driven increases in insomnia and hot-flush incidence, and testosterone levels in males (68 patients).

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Efficacy E-R in 57 (Hgb responder, Studies 006/011) and 26 (transfusion burden, Study 007) mitapivat-treated patients found no significant exposure-response trend, attributed to individualized dose-titration algorithm.

structural_features: Indirect-response (turnover) model for hemoglobin change over time driven by individual PK-predicted concentration profiles
notes: Model developed using Hgb data from 168 PKD patients; used to simulate/support the proposed dose-titration algorithm (Base Case vs Fast Response vs Super Aggressive titration scenarios).

structural_features: Minimal PBPK model with single adjusting compartment; ADAM (advanced dissolution absorption metabolism) PBPK sub-model for gastric pH effects
notes: PBPK adequate to predict CYP3A4 inhibitor/inducer DDI effects on mitapivat exposure and mitapivat's inhibitory effect as perpetrator on CYP3A/OAT3 substrates; inadequate for mitapivat's induction effects on several CYP/transporter substrates; ADAM-PBPK adequate for elevated gastric pH effect on absorption.

structural_features: Central compartments for OCA, glyco-OCA, and tauro-OCA plus a gallbladder accumulation/release compartment for conjugates; first-order absorption; enterohepatic recirculation
notes: 16 studies, >25,000 non-BLQ samples; hepatic impairment and body weight were key covariates (severe hepatic impairment: 218% higher AUC); informed FDA-proposed less-frequent alternative dosing regimens in hepatic impairment.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Phase 3 study 747-301 data linked PopPK-predicted trough OCA to ALP/bilirubin reduction via Imax models (IC50 ~10.7 and ~68.9 ng/mL) and predicted >40% probability of composite endpoint response at 5/10 mg QD; biomarker C4 declined with exposure, plateauing ~50 ng/mL.

structural_features: Physiologic (mechanistic) model of hepatic disposition for OCA/CDCA and conjugates incorporating anatomical/physiological changes (liver volume, hepatic blood flow) in hepatic impairment
notes: Used to simulate liver vs. plasma exposure across hepatic impairment severity in response to FDA information requests; supported switch to less frequent (e.g., every other day/weekly) dosing in moderate/severe hepatic impairment.

structural_features: First-order absorption with absorption lag time (ALAG); linear elimination; 3-compartment model was numerically unstable in NONMEM so 2-compartment chosen
notes: Pooled Phase 1-3 data; covariates on CL/F (age, CLcr, race, gender), Vc/F (body weight, health status, food), Ka (age); individual post-hoc AUC estimates fed into E-R analyses; hepatic/renal impairment effects assessed via dedicated studies rather than the PopPK model.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Continuous efficacy (SBM frequency change) via regression on AUC; responder/non-responder and AE occurrence via logistic models; concomitant CYP3A inducers reduced exposure ~83% with E-R relationship shown to be consistent across Phase 2b/3 trials; concomitant CYP3A4 inhibitors increased exposure.

structural_features: PBPK model of CYP3A4/P-gp substrate naldemedine; verified against clinical DDI studies (itraconazole, fluconazole, rifampin); bioavailability parameterized via Fa x FG x FH; adapted efavirenz PBPK model used to bridge to untested CYP3A modulator combinations (maraviroc, alfentanil)
fitting_method_software: Simcyp Population-based Simulator v14 (sponsor); reviewer re-verified in Simcyp v16
notes: Verified against 4 clinical DDI studies; used to predict untested moderate/strong CYP3A inhibitor/inducer interactions and support labeling/dosing recommendations with CYP3A modulators.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Human mass-balance/ADME study; NCA of naldemedine, metabolites, and total radioactivity in plasma/urine/feces to characterize elimination pathways.

structural_features: First-order absorption with lag time; combined residual error; inter-individual variability on CL/F and V2/F with block correlation matrix; OATP1B1 genotype was the only significant covariate on CL/F
notes: 1624 subjects (5 Phase 1 + 4 Phase 3 studies); OATP1B1 genotype significant covariate on CL/F (reduced IIV from 43.9% to 42.5%); provided exposure metrics for downstream E-R analyses.

structural_features: Discrete-time first-order Markov chain model linking monthly average elagolix exposure (Cavg) to transition probabilities between responder/nonresponder states for dyspareunia (DYS) and non-menstrual pelvic pain (NMPP)
notes: N=1671 (placebo + 150mg QD + 200mg BID arms) pooled across Phase 3 trials; evaluated via GOF, VPC, and bootstrap.

structural_features: Indirect-response (turnover) model for lumbar spine BMD loss vs. elagolix exposure/duration, compared against a separate quantitative systems pharmacology (QSP) estradiol-BMD model
notes: FDA requested simulations to 36 months (only 12-month observed BMD data available); indirect-response model predicted continued dose/duration-dependent bone loss without plateau, better matching observed clinical pattern than the QSP model which showed an implausible plateau/increase.

structural_features: Full PBPK model for elagolix as CYP3A substrate/perpetrator; verified against observed DDI data for digoxin and midazolam
fitting_method_software: Simcyp (sponsor: v15.0.86.0; FDA reviewer re-verification: v16)
notes: Used to predict elagolix effects as CYP3A4 inducer/perpetrator on midazolam and digoxin exposure (FDA found CYP3A induction over-predicted at some doses, recommended sponsor verify further); supported patient monitoring recommendation for concomitant digoxin.

structural_features: Static mechanistic (non-dynamic) model accounting for gut and hepatic CYP3A4/5 induction/inhibition; not a full dynamic PBPK simulation
notes: Rifamycin SV has minimal systemic absorption (~83% excreted unchanged in feces); static mechanistic model predicted no clinically relevant CYP3A4/5 induction/inhibition for systemic exposure of concomitant substrates (midazolam AUCR 0.91, tacrolimus AUCR 0.86); sensitivity analysis (EC50=1 uM) suggested possible induction but judged not clinically significant given short 3-day treatment and low colonic CYP3A expression.

structural_features: First-order absorption with lag time; creatinine clearance (renal function) was the only significant covariate on apparent clearance (CL/F)
notes: Model built on Phase 1 data then expanded with Phase 2/3 data; prucalopride is primarily renally eliminated (CLcr significant on CL/F; once included, no other covariates including age/sex/race were significant) - supports renal-impairment dosing guidance.

structural_features: Full-body PBPK model with a permeability-limited liver (PerL) distribution model and enzyme kinetics for CYP3A-mediated elimination; verified against 6 Phase 1 PK studies (Cmax/AUC/CL/tmax predictions within 20-50% of observed)
notes: Used to predict DDI with CYP3A/P-gp/BCRP inhibitors (ketoconazole, verapamil, cyclosporine, quinidine) and inducers (rifampicin), plus transporter-substrate interactions with metformin (OCT/MATE) and digoxin (P-gp); ketoconazole and ambiguous ketoconazole effect noted as not fully captured by PBPK vs. observed/in vitro data.

structural_features: First-order absorption with lag time; dose-dependent bioavailability; first-order elimination; allometric (fixed exponent) weight effect on Vc/F, weight estimated on CL/F; food, sex, and Asian ethnicity effects on Ka
notes: Analysis incorporated CYP2C19 metabolizer phenotype (EM/IM/PM) as baseline covariate; sex effect on vonoprazan PK further evaluated via the model.
