structural_features: Full PBPK model with first-order absorption, full PBPK distribution, and enzyme-kinetics elimination model (CYP3A4/CYP2D6/CYP2C19/SULT2A1-mediated); verified against clarithromycin DDI data
notes: Model reproduced observed clarithromycin effect on vonoprazan PK (fm ~38% CYP2D6, ~36% CYP3A4, ~4% CYP2C19); used to bridge to untested CYP2C19 inhibitors (omeprazole/lansoprazole comparator models); reviewer flagged that CYP2C19 time-dependent inhibition parameters were not incorporated, which may explain under-prediction for some interactions (e.g., proguanil).

structural_features: First-order elimination from central compartment; inter-compartmental clearance (Q); no significant covariates identified (base model = final model); peripheral volume (V2) and Q fixed to historical healthy-volunteer literature values due to sparse patient data
notes: Sparse PK from 29/39 sampled HRS-1 patients (56 randomized to active arm, high early dropout); FDA reviewer noted large residual error limited predictive utility and doubted value of covariate testing given narrow patient demographic range.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Graphical exploration of model-predicted exposure vs. HRS reversal/serious adverse events found no clear trend; FDA reviewer judged the E-R analysis inadequately powered/exploratory and recommended serum creatinine as a more appropriate response variable than the composite endpoint used.

structural_features: Sequential zero- and first-order absorption, first-order elimination; body weight covariate on CL and V (allometric-style fixed exponent); food/sex/Asian ethnicity tested on Ka; no clinically meaningful effect of sex, age, race, ethnicity, smoking, or UC disease status
fitting_algorithm: Bayesian estimation (MCMC; ESS and Gelman-Rubin diagnostics reported)
notes: 16,205 quantifiable concentrations from 1079 subjects; typical CL/F 1.06 L/h, Vss/F 70 L, t1/2,eff 33.9 h; body weight only clinically notable covariate but not warranting dose adjustment.

structural_features: Indirect-response (turnover) model with circadian rhythm for lymphocyte egress linked to etrasimod exposure
notes: Data from 15 Phase 1 + 2 Phase 2 + 2 Phase 3 studies; simulations predicted lymphocyte recovery to near baseline within 1-2 weeks after discontinuation (median 10-11 days to 90% of baseline) - supports washout/discontinuation guidance.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: E-R analyses for clinical remission, endoscopic improvement, symptomatic remission, mucosal healing at Week 12 using pooled Phase 2/3 data with post-hoc PopPK-derived exposure estimates; heart rate E-R also evaluated (bradycardia risk assessment, consistent with sphingosine-1-phosphate receptor modulator class).

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Single-dose (21 g) food-effect study (BLI400-101) in healthy subjects: Cmax/AUC >2-fold higher fasting vs. fed, supporting "take with meals" labeling; no population PK, exposure-response, or DDI modeling conducted - majority of Phase 3 patient PK samples were below LLOQ.

structural_features: First-order elimination from central compartment with 5 absorption transit compartments; allometric scaling (CL exponent 0.75, V exponent 1.00); M3 method used to handle BLQ data
notes: 707 subjects (5 studies, QD and TIW dosing) with 3523 evaluable concentrations; concomitant clopidogrel reduced CL by 42.4%, dialysis status affected Ka; no significant effect of age/weight/sex/hyporesponder status.

structural_features: Linear treatment-effect model of daprodustat exposure on hemoglobin (Conc-Hb) with random effects structure; iteratively updated 2015->2019->2022 dose-response Hb model
notes: Longitudinal population PK/PD model pooling 3 CKD dialysis studies (200807, 204837, 204836) supported comparison of QD vs TIW dosing regimens; showed Hb peak-to-trough fluctuations were minimal/not clinically important with TIW dosing.

structural_features: Not applicable
estimation_technique: Logistic regression; Cox proportional hazards regression
notes: Post-hoc multivariate analysis of ASCEND-D/ASCEND-TD (Cmax vs thromboembolic events, nonfatal MI, nonfatal HF hospitalization by Week 52) found Cmax was not a significant predictor of any of the 3 cardiovascular safety measures; small event numbers limited power.

structural_features: Minimal PBPK model; ADAM module used for absorption/dissolution
notes: PBPK adequately predicted daprodustat AUC/Cmax increases with CYP2C8 inhibitors gemfibrozil/trimethoprim; clopidogrel PBPK models (borrowed pioglitazone/montelukast component models) were not reliably validated and underpredicted the interaction, so clinical recommendation for clopidogrel relies on observed clinical DDI data instead.

structural_features: First-order absorption from SC injection with dose-dependent relative bioavailability (F1); linear elimination
notes: 223 subjects (81 healthy, 37 AML, 105 MM) across phase 1-3 trials, 2240 evaluable concentrations; body weight affected bioavailability (F1) and Vc/F; mild/moderate renal and mild hepatic impairment had no significant PK effect.

structural_features: Indirect-response (turnover) model: stimulatory sigmoid Emax function on Kin (production rate) of CD34+ cell count, with independent G-CSF effect on Kin and apheresis effect on Kout
notes: Model derived using CD34+ cell count data linked to empirical Bayes PK estimates from popPK model; supported mechanistic understanding of motixafortide-driven stem cell mobilization for apheresis timing.

structural_features: Precursor-pool indirect (turnover) model: stimulatory Emax function applied to first-order transfer rate constant (Ktr) from precursor pool, describing WBC mobilization
notes: Companion PK/PD model to the CD34+ model, describing WBC count response as a supportive mobilization biomarker.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Logistic-regression E-R models of injection-site reaction/systemic reaction (1846 AE observations, 243 subjects) and of any-grade/grade>=3 TEAEs vs first-dose Cmax; probability of injection-site reaction plateaued near Cmax ~750 ng/mL.

structural_features: Erlang (transit-compartment) absorption for parent (MMB); formulation effect on transit rate constant (Ktr); dose-dependent bioavailability (Emax model); metabolite M21 modeled as 1-compartment with first-order absorption, sequential PPK
notes: 618 myelofibrosis patients (3552 PK obs) for MMB, 507 patients (2228 obs) for metabolite M21; eGFR and AST were covariates on M21 clearance; IIV on CL was high (~80%, low shrinkage ~3%) but model deemed acceptable for deriving E-R exposures.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Efficacy E-R (spleen volume/TSS response) using posterior PK exposures; simulation-based reviewer sensitivity analysis also conducted in NONMEM 7.4.3/R.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Safety E-R across 7 AE endpoints (anemia, AEs, thrombocytopenia, diarrhea, peripheral neuropathy, discontinuation, bilirubin); significant exposure relationships found only for grade>=3 thrombocytopenia and peripheral neuropathy.

structural_features: Delayed first-order absorption (tlag, ka), parallel linear and nonlinear (Michaelis-Menten, Vmax/Km) elimination plus time-dependent clearance (TDmax, TD50); Applicant's simpler linear 1-compartment model was rejected by FDA reviewer as inadequate (failed to capture saturable, neutrophil-mediated clearance)
fitting_method_software: MONOLIX 2020 (reviewer's independent model); Applicant's software not stated
notes: 289 subjects across 6 studies (2495 concentrations); FDA reviewer rejected Applicant's PopPK model (ill-conditioned, failed GOF) and built independent Monolix model with saturable clearance; covariates: lean body mass on Vmax, race (Chinese Han) on V/F, age on Ka.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: 196 patients (phase 3 GC-627-05); no significant E-R relationship for duration of severe neutropenia or incidence of severe neutropenia at the single 20 mg dose studied, using both Applicant's and reviewer's (corrected PK) exposure estimates.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Safety E-R (any TEAE, grade>=3 TEAE, grade>=2 alopecia/nausea/bone pain/asthenia/leukopenia/thrombocytopenia) showed no significant exposure relationships at the single 20 mg dose; narrow exposure range limited detection of E-R signal.

structural_features: First-order absorption with lag time; linear model restricted to therapeutic dose range (100/200 mg BID) because iptacopan shows less-than-dose-proportional PK at lower doses attributed to target-mediated drug disposition (TMDD, irreversible binding to complement Factor B)
notes: 234 subjects (PNH, IgAN, C3G) receiving 100/200 mg BID; body weight, baseline eGFR, and ethnicity (Chinese/Japanese/other Asian) were covariates on CL/F; covariate effects deemed not clinically relevant as exposure was near plateau of PK/PD curve.

structural_features: Indirect-response (turnover) models: LDH via concentration-dependent production rate (kin); hemoglobin via concentration-dependent elimination rate (kout); shared baseline/steady-state response parameterization
notes: 161 PNH patients (53 anti-C5 experienced); estimated LDH EC50 ~29.8 ng/mL, EC90 ~268 ng/mL; model predicted LDH normalization to 237 U/L at steady state, supporting 200 mg BID dose being near the E-R plateau for efficacy.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Graphical (loess) exposure-safety analysis of platelet count, total cholesterol, and T3 versus trough concentration; iptacopan decreased platelets and increased cholesterol/T3 versus anti-C5 comparators, but effects were exposure-independent (driven by treatment status, not dose).

structural_features: DDI victim/perpetrator PBPK, mechanistic absorption/hepatic uptake model
notes: PBPK inadequate to predict DDI effects of CYP2C8/OATP1B1/3 modulators (rifampin, gemfibrozil) on iptacopan, or iptacopan's DDI risk as CYP2C8 perpetrator (repaglinide), due to uncertainty in hepatic OATP1B1/3 uptake contribution to iptacopan disposition.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: PK of active metabolite 3-quinuclidinol characterized via NCA in n=16 subjects after topical ocular dosing (Day 1 and Day 8 of QD dosing); minimal systemic exposure (Cmax ~2.2 ng/mL), no significant accumulation (RAUC0-t 1.19), AUCinf/half-life not estimable due to limited quantifiable samples; FDA reviewer independently verified sponsor's PK values using WinNonlin.

structural_features: Parallel linear and nonlinear (target-mediated-like) elimination with first-order absorption; pooled IV and SC dosing data
notes: Pooled PopPK model across 4 studies (Phase 1 healthy volunteers plus Phase 3 THRIVE/THRIVE-2/OLE thyroid eye disease trials); 298 subjects, 4123 PK observations; linear clearance ~0.216 L/day (t1/2 ~18 days, consistent with a monoclonal antibody); body weight, ADA status, sex, and smoking status were statistically significant but not clinically meaningful covariates.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Using popPK-model-derived individual exposure metrics (first-dose, steady-state, cumulative AUC/Cmax/Ctrough) across quartiles, no apparent exposure-response relationship was found for efficacy or for 7 safety endpoints including infusion-related reactions (n=298), supporting the fixed IV dosing regimen without exposure-based dose adjustment.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Single-dose IV (2 mg/kg) 3-arm PK/bioequivalence study (n=135) compared ONS-1045 (IV bevacizumab-vikg) to US- and EU-licensed Avastin; Cmax/AUCinf geometric mean ratios met BE criteria (90% CI 80-125%). Separate IVT PK substudy (n=14, nAMD patients) showed minimal systemic exposure (~0.3% of IV Cmax) after 1.25 mg intravitreal dosing; limited sampling (to Day 4 only) precluded full serum PK characterization.

structural_features: First-order absorption with lag time; base/full/final covariate models selected via Wald Approximation Method; covariates sex, smoking status, race on clearance
notes: Sponsor pooled 5 population PK study reports (healthy subjects and COPD/asthma patients, 250-500 mcg QD) for roflumilast and its active N-oxide metabolite; males had 19% greater CL than females, smokers had 31% greater CL than nonsmokers; FDA reviewer noted the model underpredicted higher observed concentrations in COPD patients and no labeling statements were derived from the analysis.

structural_features: PBPK simulation incorporating liver volume, blood flow, and CYP enzyme abundance to predict effect of hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh A/B cirrhosis) on roflumilast/N-oxide exposure
notes: Clinical hepatic-impairment study only tested 250 mcg; SimCyp simulated/bridged exposure at the proposed 500 mcg dose in Child-Pugh A/B patients; simulations over-predicted observed cirrhosis-patient concentrations; sponsor concluded PK changes at 500 mcg would resemble those at 250 mcg, supported by linear in vitro CYP1A2/3A4/2C9/2C19 metabolism far above clinical Cmax.

structural_features: First-order elimination, instantaneous (inhaled) input; covariates age, body weight, sex, disease type (COPD vs asthma) on CL/F
notes: Pooled 5 Phase II/III studies (Concept1 SDDPI device), 2409 COPD/asthma patients, 20097 observations across 75-600 mcg QD; Cmax increased ~41% and AUC ~23% over the studied age range, Cmax decreased ~25-27% and AUC ~21% over the studied weight range, AUC ~17% higher in asthma vs COPD; none of the covariate effects were judged clinically meaningful enough to warrant dose adjustment.

structural_features: Sigmoidal/simple Emax dose-response model (E0, Emax, ED50) relating inhaled dose to change in trough FEV1; both patient-level and study-level (meta-analytic) versions built
notes: FDA pharmacometrics review found the sponsor's covariate model structures for Emax/ED50 were inappropriate, causing the sponsor's model to overstate the incremental efficacy benefit of 150 mcg vs 75 mcg (and 75 vs 37.5 mcg) especially in more severe COPD patients; expanding the dataset (3454 to 34615 observations, 1835 to 5558 patients) did not resolve parameter instability, so the model-based claim of added benefit for more severe patients at the higher dose was not supported.

structural_features: Fluticasone furoate (FF): first-order absorption and first-order elimination; race covariate on CL/F; M3 method used for high proportion of BLQ (censored) concentration data
notes: FF popPK dataset: 11798 observations from 1307 healthy/COPD subjects (94% COPD); East Asian/Japanese/South Asian subjects had 23-30% higher FF AUC(0-24) than white Caucasian subjects and other race groups 10-26% higher, but all remained below levels associated with HPA-axis suppression risk.

structural_features: Vilanterol (VI): zero-order absorption and first-order elimination; covariates age, weight, study on CL/F, and age, smoking, sex, study on V1/F
notes: VI popPK dataset: 10807 observations from 1167 healthy/COPD subjects (85% COPD); CL/F decreased 27% and V1/F decreased 30% over the observed COPD age range (41-84y); CL/F increased 47% over the observed weight range (35-160kg); a Phase II study subgroup (n=40) showed unexplained 1.5-2.7 fold higher exposure vs Phase III (n=1052) without associated heart-rate increase.

structural_features: Threshold inhibitory Emax model relating FF serum AUC(0-24) to 24-hr weighted mean serum cortisol (HPA-axis safety biomarker); parameters AUCthreshold=380 pg*h/mL, E0=225 nmol/L, AUC50=1345 pg*h/mL, Hill coefficient n=3.2
notes: Cortisol suppression only occurs above an FF exposure threshold (~380 pg*h/mL); AUC50 (1345 pg*h/mL) was several-fold higher than mean FF AUC(0-24) at the therapeutic 100 mcg dose (184 pg*h/mL) in COPD patients, supporting an adequate safety margin against HPA-axis suppression at the marketed dose.

structural_features: First-order absorption for both UMEC and VI; allometric-type power covariate models on CL/F (weight, age, creatinine clearance for both analytes) and on V2/F (weight, UMEC only); M3/F_FLAG censored-likelihood method used for ~20-25% BLQ data
notes: Combined UMEC/VI popPK model; weight, age, and creatinine clearance were statistically significant but only marginal covariates on UMEC/VI apparent clearance (no dose adjustment warranted); no PK interaction detected between co-administered UMEC and VI; individual subject AUC/Cmax derived via post-hoc (empirical Bayes) parameter estimates.

structural_features: Linear PK (no evidence of target-mediated drug disposition); estimated absolute bioavailability and first-order Ka for SC dosing; time-varying albumin inversely associated with CL; body weight positively associated with CL, Q, V2, V3; BMI inversely associated with SC bioavailability
notes: 1129 UC patients (952 induction-phase + 914 maintenance-phase PK datasets, Studies AMAN/AMBG); mild/moderate renal impairment evaluated as covariate (no dose adjustment recommended); supported 300 mg IV Q4W induction / 200 mg SC Q4W maintenance dosing.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Phase 2 (AMAC, n=248, exposure-based dose-adjustment cohorts) and Phase 3 (AMAN n=1156; AMBG maintenance) data; higher exposure generally associated with higher response/remission rate in both induction and maintenance, supporting proposed doses; body weight/BMI noted as potential confounders via univariate logistic regression.

structural_features: Mixed-order absorption (zero-order into depot then first-order into central compartment) with lag time; time-dependent increase in CL/F with repeated dosing modeled as a saturable (Emax vs. number of doses) function, consistent with auto-induction; dose-dependent CL/F via a power model centered on 80 mg
notes: Pooled Phase 1-3 NASH/MASH population (fibrosis stages F0-3); characterized time- and dose-dependent clearance supporting 80 mg/100 mg QD dosing.

structural_features: Multiple Emax/probability exposure-response models at Week 52 for biomarkers/efficacy (SHBG, FT4, ApoB, LDL-C, MRI-PDFF percent change; probability of >=30%/>=50% fibrosis-related reduction; probability of NASH resolution) and for safety (probability of diarrhea, nausea), all driven by steady-state average concentration (Cave,ss)
notes: Based on Phase 3 MGL-3196-11 plus supportive studies; E-R models supported dose justification for 80/100 mg; resmetirom is a CYP2C8 substrate and weak inhibitor (clinical DDI shown with pioglitazone, clopidogrel).

structural_features: Separate but structurally identical models for elafibranor and its active, equipotent metabolite GFT1007; sequential zero-order then first-order absorption after a short lag time; linear first-order elimination; body weight included a priori as mechanistic covariate on CL/Vd; additional covariates (albumin, BMI, age, sex, PBC population, formulation, food status) on CL/F, Q/F, Vp/F, relative bioavailability, absorption duration, lag time
fitting_method_software: NONMEM v7.5.0; R v3.5.3 with mrgsolve package for simulation
notes: Pooled Phase 1/2/3 PBC population PK data; supported combined elafibranor+GFT1007 exposure-based dose selection/labeling.

structural_features: Indirect-response model (inhibition of zero-order ALP production rate) driven by combined elafibranor+GFT1007 steady-state AUC (AUCt,ss,sum); joint ALP-total-bilirubin model; separate E-R models for GLOBE score and pruritus (WI-NRS)
notes: E-R analysis in PBC patients supported dose justification for the approved 80 mg dose (linear exposure-total-bilirubin relationship; exposure largely overlapping between 80 mg and 120 mg cohorts in Study 216-1).

structural_features: Kinetic-PD (K-PD) framework used because linerixibat plasma concentrations were too low/variable for conventional population PK: (1) TSBA (bile acid) indirect-response model with circadian sine-wave fluctuation, food-driven enterohepatic recirculation, and drug effect via a first-order-degrading virtual dose-amount compartment; (2) itch-score (worst daily itch NRS) indirect-response model with logit transform bounding scores 0-10 and inverse-exponential decay of drug effect
pk_exposure_metric: Not applicable (dose/virtual drug amount used in place of plasma concentration)
notes: N=511 (healthy subjects + PBC patients); baseline ALP was a significant covariate on baseline TSBA in PBC patients; models used because linerixibat is a minimally-absorbed, locally-acting IBAT inhibitor; supported PBC dosing regimen and itch efficacy characterization.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: GSRS Question 11 diarrhea-severity score modeled as a dose-response relationship (proportional odds model) to characterize tolerability and inform regimen/dose selection.

structural_features: Static mechanistic (cutoff/R-value) model considering cumulative intestinal + hepatic CYP3A4 inhibition
notes: Static mechanistic model concluded linerixibat did not meet criteria for clinical DDI investigation with CYP3A4 or OATP1B substrate drugs given its low fraction absorbed; in vitro, linerixibat did not induce CYP1A2/2B6/3A4.

structural_features: Sequential lag time and first-order absorption (food effect on lag time/Ka), first-order elimination; allometric scaling of CL/V by body weight; power model with eGFR on CL
notes: Pooled 15 studies: 96 healthy volunteers, 2003 NDD-CKD, 2098 DD-CKD subjects (14021 PK samples); Japanese descent and bilirubin (healthy only) were additional covariates on CL.

structural_features: Precursor cell compartment linked to a chain of hemoglobin life-span compartments (erythropoiesis turnover/indirect-response model); linear, Emax, and sigmoid-Emax exposure-effect functions tested
notes: 3952 subjects, 47988 Hb observations; model linked cumulative vadadustat AUC to hemoglobin response dynamics, supporting QD vs TIW regimen comparison and dose titration strategy.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: E-R for diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, hepatotoxicity, hyperkalemia, MACE, and non-fatal MI showed flat/near-flat relationships across exposure range; GI events had largest but still modest incidence increase (15.3% to 18.1%, 10th to 90th exposure percentile).

structural_features: Zero-order release followed by first-order absorption into central compartment (separate parameters for liquid-filled capsule vs tablet formulations); linear elimination
notes: Pooled 11 Phase 1 + 2 Phase 2 + Phase 3 studies; covariates: formulation-specific Ka/D1, fasted/high-fat-meal on bioavailability, renal impairment and body weight on CL/F and volumes; sex retained in final model.

structural_features: Emax model relating danicopan concentration to inhibition of alternative-pathway hemolysis (APH) biomarker (baseline APH0, Imax, IC50)
notes: 475 time-matched APH-concentration samples from 69 PNH subjects (Study 301); weight and East Asian ethnicity were covariates on APH0; simulations predicted 77.5% (150mg) and 79.9% (200mg TID) APH inhibition at trough, supporting dose selection.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Efficacy E-R (Hgb change, Hgb responder, transfusion avoidance, LDH change) in 63 subjects (Study 301) showed no meaningful relationship, likely confounded by dose-escalation design for non-responders.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Safety E-R (TEAEs >5% incidence, liver enzymes, meningococcal infection, and later added lipid endpoints TC/LDL/triglycerides) in 73 subjects found no meaningful relationship; flat E-R for hyperlipidemia signal despite small observed lipid increases.

structural_features: Target-mediated drug disposition (TMDD) model with saturable binding (Bmax, Kd-type parameters); sequential ITS/SAEM/IMP estimation
fitting_algorithm: SAEM (sequential ITS, SAEM, IMP with EONLY=1)
notes: Pooled MDS/myelofibrosis/solid-tumor data (N=107 MDS3001 relapsed/refractory MDS, plus other indications); spleen volume and myelofibrosis diagnosis were covariates on Bmax; theory-based allometric exponents (0.75/1) applied; corrected a molecular-weight error (free acid vs sodium salt) in DV2/LDV2 calculation.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: MDS3001: statistically significant positive E-R relationship between Cavg and both primary (>=8-week transfusion independence) and key secondary (>=24-week TI) efficacy endpoints; limited by single dose level studied in the MDS population and frequent dose modifications.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: MDS3001 Phase 3: positive E-R relationship between Cmax and Grade 3-4 thrombocytopenia risk, supporting consideration of dose/regimen optimization to reduce toxicity.

structural_features: First-order SC absorption and elimination; allometric scaling (weight on CL/volumes); time-varying ADA-titer effect on CL; transient drug-target-drug complex (DTDC)-mediated clearance in subjects switching from eculizumab/ravulizumab, modeled with exponential decay constant
notes: 6115 concentrations from 9 healthy volunteers + 421 PNH subjects (210 treatment-naive, 211 switch from another C5 inhibitor); supported bridging PK between treatment-naive and switch populations and between IV/SC routes.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Time-matched concentration vs CH50/free-C5 pharmacodynamic biomarkers (428 subjects); concentrations >=100 ug/mL associated with near-complete terminal complement inhibition (CH50 <30 U/mL in 99.9% of samples), supporting the Q4W maintenance dose/trough target.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: No relevant exposure-efficacy relationship for steady-state normalized LDH; logistic regression of AUC/Cmax vs safety outcomes (AESI, infections) showed no clinically relevant exposure-safety relationship.

structural_features: Semi-mechanistic TMDD model with quasi-steady-state (QSS) approximation plus additional nonlinear drug clearance; first-order SC absorption with lag time; normalized weight as structural covariate
notes: 2235 evaluable concentrations from 150 hemophilia A/B participants + 63 healthy participants; ADA status, hepatic function, race, renal impairment, and hemophilia type were tested but not significant after accounting for weight-adjusted CL.

structural_features: Emax model linking model-predicted free TFPI (from PPK model) to peak thrombin generation
notes: Supported mechanistic link between marstacimab target engagement (free TFPI suppression) and procoagulant biomarker (peak thrombin) response.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Quasi-Poisson regression of ABR vs Cavg,ss (Phase 2/3 data) showed a negative relationship (higher exposure, fewer bleeds), supporting the 150 mg SC QW (300 mg loading) dose; adolescent dosing justified via PPK/PD-model simulation across 30-120 kg weight range.

structural_features: First-order absorption after SC injection from depot compartment, first-order elimination from central compartment; disease status (healthy volunteer vs. Cushing's patient) as covariate on all parameters; clearance increases with body size, decreases with age similarly in both populations, but typical CL/F and V2/F differ ~40-60% between healthy volunteers and patients
notes: 216 healthy volunteers (4244 obs) + 197 Cushing's disease patients (2368 obs); age/body-weight/race/gender had no clinically meaningful effect on clearance; no dosage adjustment recommended based on age or body size.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Pivotal trial B2305 data; multivariate logistic regression of responder status (mUFC <= ULN) and safety (>1% HbA1c increase, abnormal LFTs) vs. trough concentration and covariates; found the higher proposed 900 ug BID starting dose was NOT supported by the E-R relationship for efficacy or safety, and FDA recommended a lower 600 ug BID starting dose; significant E-R relationship found for hyperglycemia.

structural_features: First-order absorption (Ka) with SC injection-site effect (thigh/abdomen/unknown), mono-exponential (linear) elimination; combined with an endogenous PTH circadian-rhythm baseline model (cosine function) to separate exogenous drug PK from endogenous hormone fluctuation; mixed-order absorption tested but did not converge
fitting_method_software: NONMEM v7.2 (with Perl-speaks-NONMEM v3.5.3 for bootstrap/VPC)
notes: 16 studies (11 non-hypoparathyroid + 4 hypoparathyroid + 2 special-population [hepatic/renal impairment] studies); body weight was statistically significant on CL/F and V/F but reviewer judged it clinically minor (explained only 0.7-8% of variability); antibody-positive subjects showed higher apparent V and CL.

structural_features: FDA reviewer-developed mechanistic systems model of calcium homeostasis (adapted from published Peterson & Riggs calcium-homeostasis model), incorporating rhPTH(1-84) PK, exogenous calcitriol (vitamin D) PK via added depot compartment, parathyroid-gland-pool depletion, and 24-hour urinary calcium excretion flux
fitting_method_software: R (open source, modified published model code)
notes: Reviewer simulated alternate calcium/calcitriol co-administration regimens and degrees of PTH-gland-pool loss (50-99%) using sponsor PKPD study C09-002 and Mosekilde-IIT data for model evaluation, to explore hypocalcemia/hypercalciuria risk under various dosing scenarios in hypoparathyroidism.

structural_features: IV bolus input, first-order elimination from central compartment, plus an additional (hemodialysis) clearance pathway (CLon_HD) active only during dialysis sessions
notes: 583 CKD/secondary-hyperparathyroidism (sHPT) patients on hemodialysis (1 Phase 1 + 2 Phase 2 + 2 Phase 3 studies); renal impairment had minimal PK impact since hemodialysis was the dominant elimination route; simulations explored effect of dialysis duration/frequency on accumulation.

structural_features: Mechanism-based, sequential population PK/PD model linking predicted individual etelcalcetide concentrations (from the PopPK model) to serum intact PTH (iPTH) and corrected calcium (cCa) turnover dynamics
fitting_algorithm: Monte Carlo importance sampling expectation maximization (for final model); individual Bayesian estimation for covariate effects
notes: Simulations across fixed doses (2.5-15 mg TIW) supported the phase 3 dose-titration scheme by predicting proportion of patients achieving >=30% iPTH reduction, hypocalcemia (cCa <7.5 mg/dL), and dose level distribution over time.

structural_features: First-order absorption/elimination; anti-drug-antibody (ADA) titer (low/high, time-varying) and creatinine clearance (CrCL) identified as influential covariates on CL; ADA titer also affected V2; patient status (healthy vs. patient) affected bioavailability (F); prior 1-compartment structure from earlier analyses was superseded
notes: Full model = final model (no covariates dropped on backward elimination); VPCs stratified by ADA status and creatinine clearance showed adequate performance.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Phase 2 dose-ranging (BA058-05-002, N=225) linear dose-exposure relationship used as surrogate for E-R on BMD; Phase 3 ACTIVE trial (N=2463) logistic-regression E-R analysis of AUC vs. headache/dizziness/other AEs found no relationship, attributed to narrow exposure range at the single approved 80 mcg dose; abaloparatide showed significantly less hypercalcemia than teriparatide (3.4% vs 6.4%).

structural_features: Not applicable
estimation_technique: Not stated (power-model regression of ln Cmax/AUC vs. ln dose)
notes: Only a basic NCA-derived dose-proportionality assessment was conducted for this single-dose oral GH-secretagogue diagnostic agent; no population PK or formal exposure-response model was developed (an internal FDA note explicitly listed "exposure-response data" and "dose-response data" as items that could not be evaluated due to incomplete/unacceptable bioanalytical data for one supporting study); sex-based Cmax/AUC differences were tested and found not significant (p>0.23).

structural_features: Two-compartment serum-to-choroid-plexus distribution model for the mPEG moiety; cross-species (rat, monkey, human) interspecies scaling with biodistribution coefficient scaled from N9-GP (nonacog beta pegol) rat data to predict choroid plexus mPEG accumulation/vacuolation risk
notes: Predicted mPEG concentrations in children's choroid plexus at the proposed 0.24 mg/kg/week dose were below levels associated with vacuolation in monkeys; FDA judged the modeling supportive only, citing reliance on theoretical/cross-study comparisons.

structural_features: Lonapegsomatropin: one-compartment model, parallel first- and zero-order absorption, nonlinear serum clearance; released hGH: one-compartment, first-order absorption, linear clearance; linked Emax PK/PD model for hGH stimulation of IGF-1 production
notes: Covariates sex, age, body weight, renal function evaluated in final PK/PK-PD models (Studies CT-101, CT-301); simulations supported dosing recommendations including missed-dose scenarios.

structural_features: 3-compartment QSS TMDD model: linear elimination from central compartment plus TMDD in all 3 compartments and additional TMDD via a non-renewable target pool from the peripheral compartment; joint model across 4 studies/3 manufacturing sources (MacroGenics, Eli Lilly, AGC Biologics) with product-specific KSS/CL/Kint effects
notes: Developed in response to a Complete Response Letter deficiency; PROTECT PK substudy (Eli Lilly N=138, AGC Biologics N=33, ages 8-17) showed the to-be-marketed AGC product had ~27% lower AUCinf than the Eli Lilly clinical-trial product; PK comparability was not established (90% CI outside 0.8-1.25 for AUClast/AUCinf) despite similar Cmax.

structural_features: Not applicable (Emax model, Hill coefficient fixed=1, relating teplizumab AUCinf to total lymphocyte count decline over first 28 days)
notes: Emax model using Protege study data (EC50=306.5 ng*day/mL) showed a shallow E-R relationship; adding Encore study data (49% higher clearance) gave a similar EC50 (~362 ng*day/mL); shallow relationship limited its use to bridge PK differences between manufacturing sources.

structural_features: Two-compartment model (Vc, Vp, Q) with transit-compartment first-order absorption, food-effect on absorption, Box-Cox transformation of random effects; covariates: smoking (CYP1A2 induction) and study effects on CL, body weight (allometric) and race on Vc
notes: Pooled Phase 1-3 model; smoking (CYP1A2 induction) increased CL; no age trend in participants 19-65 years; predicted exposures fed into E-R and PBPK-DDI analyses supporting the 45 mg QD dose.

structural_features: Full PBPK oral absorption model (ADAM model, MechPeff-derived jejunal permeability, Rodgers-Rowland Vss); fezolinetant primarily cleared via CYP1A2 (fmCYP1A2~0.9, verified against clinical fluvoxamine DDI data), minor CYP2C9/2C19 contribution
notes: Verified against strong CYP1A2 inhibitor fluvoxamine (9.4-fold AUC increase); predicted weak (cimetidine, 1.6-2.0-fold AUC) and moderate (mexiletine, 3.4-4.6-fold AUC) CYP1A2 inhibitor effects; FDA judged model adequate and recommended avoiding moderate/strong CYP1A2 inhibitors.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Pooled Phase 3 data (Studies 2693-CL-0301/0302) showed a shallow but positive relationship between exposure and reduction in hot-flash frequency/severity; 45 mg had slightly better efficacy than 30 mg.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Pooled Phase 2/3 data (30-180 mg) found a significant exposure-ALT/AST elevation relationship (HR 1.29 at 30 mg, 1.47 at 45 mg vs placebo for >3xULN); baseline ALT was the strongest predictor (HR 2.6-6.0), informing hepatic monitoring recommendations.

structural_features: Semi-mechanistic joint model for prodrug (palopegteriparatide/mPEG), released PTH(1-34), and metabolite PTH(1-33): 1-compartment first-order absorption from SC depot with linear elimination; parallel prodrug dissociation (kdiss) and PTH(1-34)->PTH(1-33) metabolism (kmetab) occurring in both plasma and SC depot
fitting_algorithm: Not stated (COSSAC stepwise covariate search using importance-sampling log-likelihood)
notes: Pooled Trials CT-103, TCP-104, TCP-105, TCP-201, TCP-304; final model identified sex as covariate on prodrug/mPEG clearance; simulations predicted free PTH(1-34) at the highest recommended 60 mcg/day dose stays below the upper limit of normal. No dedicated exposure-response analysis was performed since dosing is individually titrated to response.

structural_features: Three-compartment popPK model with transit-compartment absorption, linear clearance; allometric scalers fixed at 0.75 (CL) and 1 (V); covariates: food/formulation on absorption, eGFR on CL, age on central volume, time-varying body weight on CL/V in pediatrics
notes: 6,647 PK observations from 342 subjects (4 phase 1, 2 phase 2, 2 phase 3 studies); no clinically significant PK differences by renal impairment, age, sex, race; model used to simulate pediatric dosing (25 mg bid for 10-<20 kg) to match adult/adolescent reference exposures.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Separate adult/pediatric E-R models linked AUC24 to serum androstenedione change, % glucocorticoid dose reduction, and probability of achieving physiologic GC dosing (Trial CAH3003); relationships were generally flat/shallow, and the GC-response odds ratio was close to 1, so FDA cautioned against over-interpreting E-R as the basis for dose selection.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Dedicated clinical DDI studies: strong CYP3A4 inhibitor ketoconazole increased AUC/Cmax by 45%/25%; strong CYP3A4 inducer rifampin required dose increase from 100 mg to 200 mg (evening dose) for moderate inducers; crinecerfont itself is a weak CYP3A inhibitor.

structural_features: First-order SC absorption, concentration-independent/time-invariant (linear) clearance from serum compartment; body-weight-based allometric scaling on CL/F and V/F; a Michaelis-Menten (non-linear clearance) hypothesis was tested and rejected (model instability)
notes: 7 clinical studies (5 adult + 2 pediatric, ages 1-68 years); covariates tested included FGF23, PHEX mutation type, and hyperphosphatemia; supported pediatric dosing (Q2W/Q4W regimens) bridging from adult data.

structural_features: Direct-effect Emax/Hill model linking individual-predicted (simulated, since PD sampling often lacked paired PK) burosumab concentration to serum phosphorus response; PK/PD relationship established as directly linked without temporal delay after SC dosing (delay only seen after IV dosing, so indirect-response models were not pursued)
estimation_technique: Empirical Bayes estimation (simulated concentrations used as driver)
notes: 161 adults + 65 pediatric patients (7 studies); body weight was a significant covariate on E0 and Emax; age effects on E0/Emax/EC50 evaluated to support pediatric extrapolation of the phosphorus-response relationship.

structural_features: Linear distribution to peripheral compartments; parallel linear elimination plus target-mediated (nonlinear, saturable) elimination from the peripheral compartment(s); saturable FcRn-mediated absorption/bioavailability process for SC dosing
notes: 13,346 concentrations from 1459 subjects (healthy, low-BMD, osteopenic, osteoporotic postmenopausal women); significant covariates on CL: body weight, eGFR, Japanese race, manufacturing process; on V2: body weight, age, sex; no significant impact of prior alendronate/PMO treatment, patient population, or baseline sclerostin - supported no dose adjustment across studied covariates including renal function (eGFR 7-144 mL/min/1.73m2).

structural_features: Time-varying indirect-response (turnover) dose-BMD model (adapted from a previously published PMO treatment model) describing percent change from baseline in lumbar spine and total hip BMD over monthly/quarterly SC dosing schedules
pk_exposure_metric: Not applicable (BMD is the response, dose/duration is driver)
notes: Pooled Phase 2 (n=393, n=241 Japanese) + Phase 3 (n=7180) data; estimated max response 11.4% (lumbar spine) and 6.0% (total hip); time to 50% Emax was 5.4 months (spine) and 8.25 months (hip); supported the approved 210 mg SC QM dosing regimen.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: FDA assessed whether romosozumab exposure was associated with major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) risk; despite the boxed warning for cardiovascular risk, available (limited) PK data did not support evidence of a clear exposure-response relationship for MACE.

structural_features: First-order absorption with lag time (ALAG); linear inter-compartmental disposition (Q/F) between central/peripheral compartments; Michaelis-Menten (saturable) elimination from the central compartment (Vmax, Km); dose-dependent relative bioavailability (BIO, ED50 parameters)
notes: Model considered acceptable to support labeling on intrinsic factors; formal exposure-response analysis for efficacy was NOT attempted because dose was individualized/titrated to clinical response (mUFC normalization) without regard to exposure, confounding any E-R signal.

structural_features: Full PBPK model for osilodrostat as a CYP3A4/CYP2C19/CYP1A2 substrate and CYP2C19 inhibitor; reviewer refined the default Simcyp omeprazole model to account for CYP2C19 time-dependent inhibition (TDI), which the applicant's submission had omitted
notes: FDA recommended a post-marketing DDI study with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., ketoconazole) given significant residual uncertainty in the PBPK-predicted interaction and potential for off-label co-administration in Cushing's disease patients.

structural_features: Dual (zero-order then first-order) absorption; saturable Michaelis-Menten elimination; body weight, sex (incl. oral estrogen use), age group, and race as covariates on a common bioavailability-scaling parameter (affecting Vmax/F, V/F, and zero-order rate k0/F)
notes: 330 adult growth-hormone-deficient (AGHD) subjects across 3 Phase 3 trials (4364 PK + 4886 IGF-1 concentrations); all tested covariates significant at p<0.001; supported once-weekly fixed-dose (vs. titrated) labeling.

structural_features: Indirect-response model (kin/kout turnover) for IGF-1 stimulation (Emax/EC50 on IGF-1 production rate) linked to somapacitan central-compartment concentration; additional linear exposure-response sub-models relating IGF-1avg SDS to truncal fat, lean body mass, visceral adipose tissue, and appendicular skeletal muscle mass changes
notes: Dose-exposure-response simulations across 0.1-8 mg supported evaluating fixed vs. titrated dosing; established dose-response chain (dose->Cavg->IGF-1->body-composition endpoints).

structural_features: Zero-order absorption from SC injection site, linear elimination; relative bioavailability (F) fixed to 1 with only between-subject variability estimated; clearance and volume allometrically scaled to body weight using fixed literature exponents (0.75 for CL, 1.0 for V), which significantly improved fit (dOFV=-50 vs. no scaling)
notes: 120 subjects, 2711 PK observations (29 healthy/obese adults + 91 rare genetic obesity disorder [RGDO] patients); model used to determine adolescent/pediatric starting and maintenance doses and to evaluate exposure in renal impairment (11 patients, CrCl 60-90 mL/min).

structural_features: (1) Emax exposure-response model for efficacy with estimated EC50, showing therapeutic concentrations sit at/near the plateau of the E-R curve; (2) FDA reviewer-developed longitudinal weight-change model combining historical pre-treatment growth trajectories (POMC/PCSK1 and LEPR genetic subtypes) with empirical Bayes PK estimates to characterize inter-individual variability in treatment-related weight loss across induction/open-label/blinded-placebo treatment epochs
pk_exposure_metric: Cavg (Cavg=20.62 ng/mL at therapeutic dose, near E-R plateau)
notes: Reviewer's independent E-R and longitudinal weight-modeling analyses supported the adolescent dosing recommendation and confirmed that most patients regain weight during blinded placebo epochs and lose weight again on setmelanotide re-initiation.

structural_features: Three-compartment model, first-order absorption with separate lag times by formulation (oral solution vs. tablet), estimated relative tablet bioavailability; between-subject variability on CL, V2, tlag, Ftab, Ka; interoccasion variability on Ftab/Ka
notes: Pooled 5,560 PK observations from 316 subjects across 17 studies; significant covariates were meal timing, sex, formulation, and PPI co-administration on bioavailability; supported titration-based dosing given large IC50 variability in the linked E-R model.

structural_features: Disease-baseline-proportional Imax model linking simulated steady-state paltusotine trough concentration to IGF-1 reduction; IC50=17.7 ng/mL (95% CI 2.89-32.6, 141% BSV); Imax=57% of disease baseline IGF-1 (48.7% BSV)
notes: Trial 08 (n=111); high between-subject variability in IC50 (141%) supported need for individualized dose titration; no significant covariate effects of age, race, sex, baseline BMI on maximum IGF-1 reduction.

structural_features: Full PBPK model of paltusotine (CYP3A4/UGT1A1/P-gp substrate) built from physicochemical/in vitro/clinical data; verified against carbamazepine (CYP3A inducer) DDI data with only modest support; used to predict victim DDI with CYP3A4 inducers/inhibitors and UGT1A1 inhibitor atazanavir
notes: FDA judged PBPK verification with carbamazepine only modestly adequate; predictions considered low-to-medium confidence, supportive but not sole basis for dosing; PBPK could not assess paltusotine as a P-gp perpetrator (dabigatran) due to its complex oral absorption.

structural_features: 2-compartment model with first-order absorption/elimination for elinzanetant coupled with a 2-compartment model with linear+nonlinear elimination for active metabolite M30/34; circadian influence on clearance; separate linear mixed-effects models linking metabolites M27/M18-21 to M30/34
notes: 8,703 elinzanetant + ~5,800-5,932 metabolite observations from 1,318 subjects (11 phase 1, 1 phase 2, 3 phase 3 OASIS studies); significant covariates: study population and BMI on elinzanetant CL (healthy subjects 59.6% higher CL than VMS patients), age/BMI on M30/34 CL; race, mild hepatic and mild/moderate renal impairment not significant; weak CYP3A4 inhibitors increased AUC ~13% (not clinically meaningful).

structural_features: Longitudinal model: placebo base model + Emax drug-effect model (Ctrough,ss as Emax covariate) describing time-course of hot-flash frequency/severity; fixed EC50 shared between frequency and severity submodels
notes: 16,539 HF frequency/severity records from 1,418 subjects (OASIS 1-3), externally qualified with Phase 2b SWITCH-1; no covariates had clinically meaningful impact on efficacy; simulated E-R plateaued near the approved 120 mg dose; exploratory safety E-R found no significant relationship with AST/ALT elevation or somnolence/dizziness/fatigue.

structural_features: Full PBPK model of elinzanetant and active metabolite M30/34 accounting for CYP3A4-mediated metabolism and mass balance (~15% fecal recovery of unabsorbed drug, <1% urinary)
notes: Predicted moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor (erythromycin) increases AUC/Cmax 3.0-/2.0-fold, with 60 mg + moderate inhibitor giving exposure comparable to 120 mg alone (informing dose-reduction labeling); weak CYP3A inhibitors (cimetidine) had no clinically significant effect.

structural_features: One-compartment prodrug model: first-order absorption from SC depot, irreversible release of free mPEG and free CNP(89-126) (linker cleavage, krel) in both SC and plasma compartments; shared absorption/clearance/volume parameters between navepegritide and free mPEG
notes: 4,740 samples from 167 participants (35 healthy adults, 132 children with achondroplasia) across 4 studies; model used to simulate impact of early/delayed/missed doses and increased body temperature (fever) on Free CNP(89-126) steady-state exposure.

structural_features: Not applicable
estimation_technique: Nonlinear regression (Emax model with Hill coefficient)
notes: FDA reviewer's independent Emax model (E0=4.3, Emax=5.9 cm/yr AGV, EC50=1944, EC95=2438 pmol/L*h) confirmed that the 100 mcg/kg once-weekly dose achieves near-maximal annualized growth velocity response; FDA considered the Applicant's LOESS-only analysis insufficiently rigorous.

structural_features: Standard oral absorption/elimination model (CL/F, V/F) with covariates including sex, race, renal/hepatic impairment status, liver metastasis, and concomitant PPI/H2RA use
analysis_goal: Dose/regimen selection; Drug-drug interaction (DDI) risk prediction
notes: FDA verified the popPK model with no significant discordance; no clinically meaningful covariate effects (age, race, body weight, mild hepatic impairment, mild-moderate renal impairment); post-hoc PK parameters supported nab-paclitaxel combination dosing rationale (Day 3 AUC0-24 744.5-32451.0 ng*h/mL).

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: No E-R relationship for PFS/efficacy for either drug; logistic regression showed increasing relacorilant AUC0-24 significantly associated with probability of all-grade anemia (p=0.0404) but not neutropenia; nab-paclitaxel dose reduced from 100 to 80 mg/m2 in combination (relacorilant is a strong CYP3A inhibitor) to match monotherapy exposure.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Free aflibercept Cmax/AUC characterized across single IVT doses 0.05-4 mg in AMD/CNV patients (Studies VGFT-OD-0502/0702); exploratory subgroup analyses (age, sex, BMI, renal function, geographic region) found no clinically relevant influence on plasma concentrations.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: NCA of systemic brolucizumab following IVT dosing in 25 nAMD patients (Study RTH258-E003): low, highly variable exposure (AUC CV 133%, Cmax CV 135%) with no accumulation after 3 monthly doses, supporting minimal systemic PK risk of the IVT regimen.

structural_features: 3-compartment linear model: vitreous humor (VH, injection site, fixed volume 0.0045 L), aqueous humor (AH), and plasma (CL, Vc) compartments; IIV on all parameters except VH/AH volumes; correlated random effects (kVH-kAH, kAH-CL); M3 method for BLQ handling
analysis_goal: Dose/regimen selection; Extrapolation to new population
notes: 1,095 aqueous humor + 8,372 plasma observations from 2,246 patients; age reduced vitreous elimination rate; plasma ADA (~10% of patients) decreased vitreous exposure 23%; body weight increased plasma CL/F and Vc/F; plasma CL 13.7% lower in females (no vitreous difference).

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Linear regression assessed VH exposure vs. BCVA/CST change from baseline (pooled Phase 3 nAMD/DME trials); logistic regression linked VH elimination half-life to probability of qualifying for shorter treat-and-extend dosing interval.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Logistic regression of intra-ocular inflammation (IOI) probability vs. VH exposure predictors in 1,849 pooled Phase 3 patients (including renal/hepatic impairment and elderly subgroups) supported the favorable benefit-risk profile at the approved 6 mg dose.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Repeat-dose (42-day) NCA in healthy subjects (topical ocular TP-03 0.25%) showed marked whole-blood accumulation (~33- to 37-fold Cmax/AUC) despite ocular-only dosing, terminal half-life ~58 days (effective half-life ~11 days); ANOVA indicated systemic steady-state not yet reached by Day 42.5.

structural_features: One-compartment model with first-order absorption (Ka); M3 likelihood method (Beal) for below-limit-of-quantification handling given 39.9% BLQ samples due to low systemic exposure after intravitreal dosing
fitting_method_software: NONMEM v7.3+ (dataset prep in R v4.0+)
notes: Dose was the only statistically significant covariate (on relative bioavailability, attributed to injection-volume differences across dose levels); age, body weight, sex, creatinine clearance and renal impairment (mild/moderate/severe) were not significant, supporting the fixed 2 mg dose across subgroups.

structural_features: Mechanistic liver-RISC model: allometrically-scaled (rat-to-human, CL exponent 0.75/volume exponent 1.0) liver PK feeding a RISC-complex compartment, linked via indirect-response model with inhibitory effect on antithrombin (AT) synthesis rate (Ksyn); dose-dependent turnover rate (Qmax, Hill coefficient) from peripheral liver to RISC
notes: Built from AT activity data in 41 hemophilia A/B subjects (Studies ALN-AT3SC-001/002); 1000-virtual-patient simulations across 1-140 mg guided selection of 80 mg QM dose (plateau of AT-lowering dose-response); also used to evaluate race (Asian ethnicity) effect on AT<15% discontinuation risk and to support AT monitoring program design.

structural_features: First-order SC absorption, linear elimination; interindividual variability shared between CL and Vc
notes: 545 adult participants (255 healthy, 290 ITP), 7076 concentration records across 12 studies; disease status, body weight, sex, formulation, and dose were significant covariates but with no clinically relevant impact on exposure.

structural_features: Indirect-response model for longitudinal platelet counts linked to rilzabrutinib exposure (AUC,ss/Cmax,ss/Cmin,ss), with corticosteroid use/response and baseline platelet count as covariates
notes: 305 participants (86 LUNA 2 + 219 PRN1008-018), 10,652 weekly platelet counts; flat E-R for primary response-rate endpoint at the 400 mg BID dose despite a positive trend for continuous platelet increase with AUC,ss.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Higher rilzabrutinib exposure (AUC,ss, Cmin,ss) associated with higher rates of diarrhea and nausea; anemia not modeled due to rare events (<5%).

structural_features: DDI victim/perpetrator, renal-impairment PBPK
notes: PBPK predicted ritonavir (CYP3A/P-gp inhibitor) increased rilzabrutinib AUC/Cmax 7.3-/6.3-fold; carbamazepine (inducer) decreased AUC/Cmax ~77-80%; renal-impairment PBPK model was deemed not adequate by FDA; transporter-related DDI PBPK analyses considered inadequate (risk assessment only).

structural_features: Parallel linear and nonlinear (Michaelis-Menten) elimination; covariates: body weight and time-varying albumin on CL, baseline albumin and dose on V1, ADA-positive status and health status on Vmax/Km
notes: Single-arm Study TMA-001 (N=58 HSCT-TMA patients); plasma exchange/infusion (7 patients) had no clinically significant effect on CL; model used to generate exposure metrics for exploratory E-R only, in a submission FDA ultimately found did not demonstrate substantial evidence of effectiveness.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: FDA found no association between exposure/trough concentration/C4d complement inhibition and treatment response; non-responders had comparable or higher exposure than responders, undermining the mechanistic plausibility argument for effectiveness (cited in CRL-type effectiveness conclusion).

structural_features: Parallel linear and nonlinear (target-mediated/Michaelis-Menten) elimination; allometric scaling (body weight) on CL-linear/Vmax/Vc/Vp/Q; base model via FOCEI (rich data), full covariate model via Bayesian MCMC in NONMEM (sparse Phase 3 data as priors)
notes: Pooled UC/CD trials (C13002, C13006, C13007, C13009, C13011); reviewer required correction of a co-medication covariate coded as time-independent rather than time-varying; final model showed no clinically meaningful effect of immunomodulators (azathioprine/mercaptopurine/methotrexate/aminosalicylates) on clearance.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Ulcerative colitis: significant positive E-R relationship between Week-6 trough concentration and clinical response/remission, supporting effectiveness but potentially confounded by imbalanced prior-TNF-antagonist-failure distribution across exposure quartiles.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: Crohn's disease: no significant exposure-response relationship identified via univariate/multivariate logistic regression for induction of clinical remission.

structural_features: Structural model shown only as a diagram (compartment count not stated in text); stepwise covariate selection
notes: Pooled 14 studies (Phase 1-3); model used primarily to derive per-patient AUC for downstream E-R analyses; renal/hepatic impairment and DDI dosing recommendations were based on dedicated studies, not the popPK model.

structural_features: Stochastic count model for weekly spontaneous bowel movements (SBM) as a function of exposure and covariates
notes: Significant exposure-response for SBM frequency; concomitant strong-opioid use was the only covariate significantly influencing predicted response; FDA reviewer independently confirmed a significant E-R curve for the primary efficacy endpoint.

structural_features: Not applicable
notes: GI adverse events (abdominal pain, diarrhea, nausea, flatulence, vomiting) showed significant dose/exposure-response over 12-week treatment (Trials 04/05); opioid-withdrawal AEs had too few events to establish a relationship.

structural_features: Minimal PBPK model; retrograde calculation of hepatic clearance from ketoconazole DDI trial data
notes: Simulated CYP3A inhibitor (ketoconazole) and inducer (efavirenz, predicted ~50% AUC reduction) effects; FDA required model revisions (P-gp contribution to hepatic/biliary clearance, brain exposure implications given doubled headache incidence with ketoconazole).

structural_features: First-order absorption and elimination
notes: Pooled 410 subjects (88 healthy + 322 IBS-d patients) from 1 Phase 2 + 2 Phase 1 studies; FDA pharmacometrics team did not formally review this model, deeming it unnecessary since eluxadoline is considered primarily locally acting; model used to show post-hoc AUC in OATP1B1 intermediate-function genotype patients was similar to that in healthy subjects at the same dose, supporting no genotype-based dose adjustment.
